title.zh: 卷101 氐 吐榖渾 宕昌 高昌 鄧至 蠻 獠
title.en: Volume 101: Di Peoples, Tuyuhun, Dangchang, Gaochang, Dengzhi, Man, Liao
title.raw: 卷101 氐 吐榖渾 宕昌 高昌 鄧至 蠻 獠 Volume 101: Di Peoples, Tuyuhun, Dangchang, Gaochang, Dengzhi, Man, Liao

sentences.zh: 氐 吐谷渾 宕昌 高昌 鄧至 蠻 獠

translations.literal: Di; Tuyuhun; Dangchang; Gaochang; Dengzhi; Man; Liao
translations.idiomatic: The Di; Tuyuhun; Dangchang; Gaochang; Dengzhi; the Man; the Liao

sentences.zh: 氐者，西夷之別種，號曰白馬。

translations.literal: The Di were a separate branch of the Western Yi, called the White Horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were a distinct branch of the Western barbarians, known as the White Horse Di.

sentences.zh: 三代之際，蓋自有君長，而世一朝見，故詩稱「自彼氐羌，莫敢不來王」也。

translations.literal: In the era of the Three Dynasties they presumably had their own chieftains, yet each generation paid court once; hence the Odes say, "From those Di and Qiang, none dared not come to pay homage."
translations.idiomatic: During the Three Dynasties they already had their own rulers and came to court once each generation, which is why the Book of Odes says, "From those Di and Qiang, who would not come to do homage?"

sentences.zh: 秦漢以來，世居岐隴以南，漢川以西，自立豪帥。

translations.literal: From the Qin and Han onward they dwelt for generations south of Qi and Long and west of the Han River, setting up their own powerful leaders.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han times onward they lived for generations south of the Qi-Long region and west of the Han River valley, with their own powerful chiefs.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝遣中郎將郭昌、衞廣滅之，以其地為武都郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han sent Palace Attendant Guo Chang and Wei Guang to destroy them and made their territory Wudu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han sent the palace attendant Guo Chang and Wei Guang to subdue them and organized their lands as Wudu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 自汧渭抵於巴蜀，種類實繁，或謂之白氐，或謂之故氐，各有侯王，受中國封拜。

translations.literal: From the Qian and Wei rivers to Ba and Shu the clans were truly numerous; some were called White Di, some Old Di; each had marquises and kings receiving investiture from the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qian and Wei rivers to Ba and Shu the Di clans were numerous; some were called the White Di, others the Old Di. Each group had its own lords and received titles from the Chinese court.

sentences.zh: 漢建安中，有楊騰者，為部落大帥。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era of Han there was one Yang Teng, who was great chieftain of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian'an period of Han a man named Yang Teng rose to be the great chieftain of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 騰勇健多計略，[2]始徙居仇池。

translations.literal: Teng was brave, strong, and full of stratagems;[2] he first moved to dwell at Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was bold, vigorous, and resourceful;[2] he was the first to relocate his people to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 仇池方百頃，因以為號，四面斗絕，高七里餘，羊腸蟠道三十六回，其上有豐水泉，煮土成鹽。

translations.literal: Chouchi covered a hundred qing; he took this as his title. On all four sides it rose sheer; its height was more than seven li. A coiled goat-path track wound thirty-six turns. Above were abundant springs; boiling earth yielded salt.
translations.idiomatic: Chouchi covered about a hundred qing of land, and he took that name for his domain. Cliffs rose on every side to a height of more than seven li, with a twisting goat-track of thirty-six switchbacks. Rich springs on the summit allowed them to boil earth and make salt.

sentences.zh: 騰後有名千万者，魏拜為百頃氐王。

translations.literal: After Teng there was one named Qianwan; Wei enfeoffed him as King of the Hundred-Qing Di.
translations.idiomatic: After Teng came a leader named Qianwan, whom Wei invested as King of the Hundred-Qing Di.

sentences.zh: 千万孫名飛龍，漸強盛，晉武帝假平西將軍。

translations.literal: Qianwan's grandson was named Feilong; he gradually grew powerful, and Emperor Wu of Jin provisionally appointed him General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwan's grandson Feilong gradually grew in power, and Emperor Wu of Jin granted him the provisional title of General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 無子，養外甥令狐茂搜為子。

translations.literal: Having no son, he adopted his sister's son Linghu Maosou as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons and adopted his sister's son Linghu Maosou as his heir.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康中，茂搜自號輔國將軍、右賢王，羣氐推以為主。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui, Maosou styled himself General Who Assists the State and Right Worthy King; the Di masses pushed him to be their lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui, Maosou took the titles General Who Assists the State and Right Worthy King, and the Di clans acclaimed him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 關中人士流移者多依之。

translations.literal: Many displaced persons from Guanzhong relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Many refugees from the Guanzhong region came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 愍帝以為驃騎將軍、左賢王。

translations.literal: Emperor Min appointed him General of Agile Cavalry and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min appointed him General of Agile Cavalry and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 茂搜死，子難敵統位，與弟堅頭分部曲。

translations.literal: When Maosou died, his son Nandi succeeded and divided the forces with his younger brother Jiantou.
translations.idiomatic: When Maosou died, his son Nandi took power and split the tribal forces with his younger brother Jiantou.

sentences.zh: 難敵自號左賢王，屯下辨；

translations.literal: Nandi styled himself Left Worthy King and encamped at Xiabian;
translations.idiomatic: Nandi styled himself Left Worthy King and encamped at Xiabian;

sentences.zh: 堅頭號右賢王，屯河池。

translations.literal: Jiantou was titled Right Worthy King and encamped at Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantou took the title Right Worthy King and encamped at Hechi.

sentences.zh: 難敵死，子毅立，自號使持節、龍驤將軍、左賢王、下辨公，以堅頭子盤為使持節、冠軍將軍、右賢王、河池公。

translations.literal: When Nandi died, his son Yi established himself, styling himself Bearer of the Staff, Dragon-soaring General, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Xiabian; he made Jiantou's son Pan Bearer of the Staff, Champion General, Right Worthy King, and Duke of Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: After Nandi's death his son Yi took power, taking the titles Bearer of the Staff, Dragon-Soaring General, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Xiabian, while appointing Jiantou's son Pan Bearer of the Staff, Champion General, Right Worthy King, and Duke of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 臣晉，晉以毅為征南將軍。

translations.literal: He submitted to Jin; Jin made Yi General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Jin, and Jin appointed Yi General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 三年，[3]毅族兄初襲殺毅，并有其眾，自立為仇池公，臣於石虎，後稱藩於晉。

translations.literal: In the third year,[3] Yi's clansman elder cousin Chu assassinated Yi, seized his followers, and established himself as Duke of Chouchi, submitting to Shi Hu and later declaring himself a vassal of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year,[3] Yi's elder clansman Chu murdered Yi, absorbed his forces, and proclaimed himself Duke of Chouchi. He first submitted to Shi Hu and later acknowledged Jin as his suzerain.

sentences.zh: 永和十年，改初為天水公。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yonghe, Chu was changed to Duke of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yonghe, Chu was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 十一年，毅小弟宋奴使姑子梁三王因侍直手刃殺初，初子國率左右誅三王及宋奴，復自立為仇池公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Yi's younger brother Songnu had his cousin by marriage Liang Sanwang, on duty in attendance, slay Chu with his own hand; Chu's son Guo led his attendants to execute Sanwang and Songnu and again established himself as Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Yi's younger brother Songnu had his brother-in-law Liang Sanwang kill Chu while on palace duty. Chu's son Guo then led his guards to execute Sanwang and Songnu and restored himself as Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 桓溫表國為秦州刺史，國子安為武都太守。

translations.literal: Huan Wen memorialized to make Guo Inspector of Qin Province and Guo's son An Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen recommended Guo for Inspector of Qin Province and Guo's son An for Administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，國從叔俊復殺國自立。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Guo's younger cousin Jun again killed Guo and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Guo's younger cousin Jun murdered Guo and seized power for himself.

sentences.zh: 國子安叛苻生，殺俊，復稱藩於晉。

translations.literal: Guo's son An rebelled against Fu Sheng, killed Jun, and again declared himself a vassal of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's son An rebelled against Fu Sheng, killed Jun, and once again submitted to Jin as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 安死，子世自立為仇池公。

translations.literal: When An died, his son Shi established himself as Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: When An died, his son Shi proclaimed himself Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: [4]晉太和三年，以世為秦州刺史，弟統為武都太守。

translations.literal: [4]In the third year of Taihe of Jin, Shi was made Inspector of Qin Province and his younger brother Tong Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: [4]In the third year of the Taihe era, Jin appointed Shi Inspector of Qin Province and his younger brother Tong Administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 世死，統廢世子纂自立。

translations.literal: When Shi died, Tong deposed the heir Zuan and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died, Tong deposed the heir Zuan and took power himself.

sentences.zh: 統一名德。

translations.literal: Tong had another name, De.
translations.idiomatic: Tong also went by the name De.

sentences.zh: 纂聚黨襲殺統，自立為仇池公，遣使詣簡文帝，[5]以纂為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Zuan gathered partisans, raided and killed Tong, established himself as Duke of Chouchi, and sent envoys to Emperor Jianwen;[5] Zuan was made Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan rallied supporters, attacked and killed Tong, and proclaimed himself Duke of Chouchi. He sent envoys to Emperor Jianwen,[5] who appointed Zuan Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 晉咸安元年，苻堅遣楊安伐纂，克之，徙其民於關中，空百頃之地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xian of Jin, Fu Jian sent Yang An to attack Zuan, took him, moved his people to Guanzhong, and emptied the land of the hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xian'an, Fu Jian sent Yang An against Zuan, defeated him, relocated the population to Guanzhong, and left the hundred-qing region deserted.

sentences.zh: 宋奴之死，二子佛奴、佛狗逃奔苻堅，堅以女妻佛奴子定，[6]拜為尚書、領軍。

translations.literal: At Songnu's death, his two sons Fonu and Fogou fled to Fu Jian; Jian gave his daughter in marriage to Fonu's son Ding[6] and appointed him Minister of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Songnu died, his sons Fonu and Fogou fled to Fu Jian. Jian married his daughter to Fonu's son Ding[6] and appointed Ding Minister of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 苻堅之敗，關右擾亂，定盡力於堅。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated, the right of the passes was disturbed; Ding exerted himself fully for Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat threw the region west of the passes into turmoil, Ding did everything he could to support him.

sentences.zh: 堅死，乃率眾奔隴右。

translations.literal: When Jian died, he then led the masses to flee to Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's death he led his followers west into Longyou.

sentences.zh: 徙治歷城，去仇池百二十里，置倉儲於百頃。

translations.literal: He moved his seat of government to Licheng, a hundred twenty li from Chouchi, and set up granaries at the hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his capital to Licheng, a hundred and twenty li from Chouchi, and established storehouses at the hundred-qing site.

sentences.zh: 招夷夏得千餘家，自稱龍驤將軍、仇池公，稱藩於晉，孝武即以其自號假之，後以為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He recruited Yi and Xia and gained more than a thousand households, styled himself Dragon-soaring General and Duke of Chouchi, and declared himself a vassal of Jin; Emperor Xiaowu immediately granted him his self-assumed titles provisionally, and later made him Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered more than a thousand Yi and Chinese households, took the titles Dragon-Soaring General and Duke of Chouchi, and submitted to Jin. Emperor Xiaowu provisionally confirmed the titles Ding had chosen for himself and later appointed him Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 登國四年，[7]遂有秦州之地，自號隴西王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dengguo,[7] he then held the territory of Qin Province and styled himself King of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dengguo[7] he seized Qin Province and proclaimed himself King of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 後為乞伏乾歸所殺，無子。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by Qifu Gangui and had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by Qifu Gangui and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 佛狗子盛，先為監國，守仇池，乃統事，自號征西將軍、秦州刺史、仇池公，諡定為武王。

translations.literal: Fogou's son Sheng had earlier been regent, guarding Chouchi; he then took charge of affairs, styled himself General Who Campaigns West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Chouchi, and gave Ding the posthumous title King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Fogou's son Sheng had earlier served as regent at Chouchi. He now took control, styled himself General Who Campaigns West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Chouchi, and gave Ding the posthumous title King Wu.

sentences.zh: 分諸氐羌為二十部護軍，各為鎮戍，不置郡縣。

translations.literal: He divided the various Di and Qiang into twenty tribal-guard units, each garrisoned in defense, and did not establish commanderies and districts.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the Di and Qiang into twenty tribal guard units, each posted as a garrison, and did not set up regular commanderies or districts.

sentences.zh: 遂有漢中之地，仍稱藩于晉。

translations.literal: He then held the territory of Hanzhong and still declared himself a vassal of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Hanzhong and continued to acknowledge Jin as his suzerain.

sentences.zh: 天興初，遣使朝貢，詔以盛為征南大將軍、仇池王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing he sent envoys to pay tribute; an edict made Sheng General Who Campaigns South and King of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxing era he sent tribute envoys, and an imperial edict appointed Sheng General Who Campaigns South and King of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 隔礙姚興，不得歲通貢使。

translations.literal: Blocked by Yao Xing, he could not send tribute envoys every year.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's power blocked his route, so he could not send annual tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 盛以兄子撫為平南將軍、梁州刺史，守漢中。

translations.literal: Sheng made his elder brother's son Fu General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Liang Province, guarding Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng appointed his nephew Fu General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Liang Province to hold Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 劉裕永初中，封盛為武都王。

translations.literal: In the Yongchu era of Liu Yu, Sheng was enfeoffed as King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongchu era Liu Yu enfeoffed Sheng as King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 盛死，私諡曰惠文王，子玄統位。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, his private posthumous title was King Wen the Kind; his son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng died he was given the private posthumous title King Wen the Kind, and his son Xuan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 玄字黃眉，[8]號征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、秦州刺史、武都王，雖稱藩於劉義隆，仍奉晉義熙之號，[9]後始用義隆元嘉正朔。

translations.literal: Xuan's courtesy name was Huangmei;[8] he was titled General Who Campaigns West, Grand Prefect with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Qin Province, and King of Wudu. Although he declared himself a vassal of Liu Yilong, he still used the reign title Yixi of Jin;[9] only later did he adopt Yilong's Yuanjia calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, whose courtesy name was Huangmei,[8] took the titles General Who Campaigns West, Grand Prefect with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Qin Province, and King of Wudu. Though he submitted to Liu Yilong, he still used Jin's Yixi reign era[9] and only later adopted Yilong's Yuanjia calendar.

sentences.zh: 初，盛謂玄曰：「吾年已老，當終為晉臣，汝善事宋帝。」故玄奉焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sheng said to Xuan: "I am already old and shall in the end remain a subject of Jin; you should serve the Song emperor well," and so Xuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sheng had told Xuan, "I am growing old and mean to remain a loyal subject of Jin to the end. You must serve the Song emperor well." That is why Xuan did so.

sentences.zh: 玄善於待士，為流舊所懷。

translations.literal: Xuan was skilled in treating scholars and was cherished by displaced elders.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan treated scholars generously and won the loyalty of displaced men of standing.

sentences.zh: 始光四年，世祖遣大鴻臚公孫軌拜玄為征南大將軍、都督、梁州刺史、南秦王，玄上表請比內藩，許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shiguang, the Emperor sent Grand Herald Gongsun Gui to invest Xuan as General Who Campaigns South, Area Commander, Inspector of Liang Province, and King of Southern Qin; Xuan memorialized asking to be treated like an inner vassal, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shiguang the Emperor sent Grand Herald Gongsun Gui to invest Xuan as General Who Campaigns South, area commander, Inspector of Liang Province, and King of Southern Qin. Xuan petitioned to be treated as an inner vassal, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 玄死，私諡孝昭王，子保宗統位。

translations.literal: When Xuan died, his private posthumous title was King Xiao the Filial; his son Baozong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan died he received the private posthumous title King Xiao the Filial, and his son Baozong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 初，玄臨終，謂弟難當曰：「今境候未寧，方須撫慰，保宗沖昧，吾授卿國事，其無墜先勳。」

translations.literal: Earlier, on his deathbed Xuan said to his younger brother Nandang: "The borders are not yet settled and must be soothed; Baozong is young and ignorant. I entrust the state's affairs to you—do not let our forefathers' achievements fall."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Xuan told his younger brother Nandang, "The frontier is still unsettled and needs steady hands. Baozong is young and inexperienced. I leave the government in your care—do not let our ancestors' achievements be lost."

sentences.zh: 難當固辭，請立保宗以輔之。

translations.literal: Nandang firmly declined and asked to establish Baozong to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang firmly refused and insisted that Baozong be enthroned so he could assist him.

sentences.zh: 保宗既立，難當妻姚氏謂難當曰：「國險宜立長君，反事孺子，非久計。」

translations.literal: After Baozong was established, Nandang's wife, of the Yao clan, said to Nandang: "The state is perilous and ought to install an elder lord; instead you serve a child—this is no long-term plan."
translations.idiomatic: Once Baozong was enthroned, Nandang's wife of the Yao clan told him, "In such a dangerous realm we need a mature ruler. To serve a boy is no lasting policy."

sentences.zh: 難當從之，廢保宗而自立，稱藩于劉義隆。

translations.literal: Nandang followed this, deposed Baozong, and established himself, declaring himself a vassal of Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang agreed, deposed Baozong, and took the throne himself, submitting to Liu Yilong as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 難當拜保宗為鎮南將軍，鎮石昌，[10]以次子順為鎮東將軍、秦州刺史，守上邽。

translations.literal: Nandang appointed Baozong General Who Guards the South and stationed him at Shichang;[10] he made his second son Shun General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qin Province, guarding Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang appointed Baozong General Who Guards the South and posted him at Shichang,[10] while his second son Shun became General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qin Province, holding Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 保宗謀襲難當，事泄被繫。

translations.literal: Baozong plotted to raid Nandang; the affair leaked out and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Baozong plotted to attack Nandang, but the conspiracy was discovered and he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 先是，四方流人以仇池豐實，多往依附。

translations.literal: Earlier, displaced persons from the four quarters, because Chouchi was rich and substantial, mostly went to attach themselves there.
translations.idiomatic: For some time refugees from all directions had flocked to Chouchi because the region was prosperous and secure.

sentences.zh: 流人有許穆之、郝惔之二人投難當，並改姓為司馬，穆之自云名飛龍，惔之自云名康之，云是晉室近戚。

translations.literal: Among the displaced were Xu Muzhi and Hao Yinzi, who came to Nandang; both changed their surnames to Sima. Muzhi called himself Feilong and Yinzi called himself Kangzhi, saying they were close kin of the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Two refugees, Xu Muzhi and Hao Yinzi, joined Nandang and both took the surname Sima. Muzhi called himself Feilong and Yinzi Kangzhi, claiming to be near relatives of the Jin imperial house.

sentences.zh: 康之尋為人所殺。

translations.literal: Kangzhi was soon killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi was soon murdered.

sentences.zh: 時劉義隆梁州刺史甄法護刑政不理，義隆遣刺史蕭思話代任，難當以思話未至，遣將舉兵襲梁州，破白馬，遂有漢中之地。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yilong's Inspector of Liang Province Zhen Fahu did not govern punishments and administration properly; Yilong sent Inspector Xiao Sihua to replace him. Because Sihua had not yet arrived, Nandang sent generals to raise troops and raid Liang Province, broke through Baima, and then held the territory of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong's Inspector of Liang Province, Zhen Fahu, governed badly. Yilong sent Xiao Sihua to replace him, but before Sihua arrived Nandang sent troops to invade Liang Province, broke through Baima, and seized Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 尋而思話使其司馬蕭承之先驅進討，所向克捷，遂平梁州，因又附義隆。

translations.literal: Soon Sihua had his Major Xiao Chengzhi advance as vanguard to attack; wherever he went he was victorious, and Liang Province was pacified; Nandang therefore attached himself again to Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sihua sent his major Xiao Chengzhi ahead with the vanguard. Chengzhi won every engagement, recovered Liang Province, and Nandang once again submitted to Yilong.

sentences.zh: 難當後釋保宗，遣鎮董亭。

translations.literal: Later Nandang released Baozong and sent him to garrison Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang later released Baozong and posted him to garrison Dongting.

sentences.zh: 保宗與兄保顯歸京師，世祖拜保宗征南大將軍、秦州牧、武都王，尚公主；

translations.literal: Baozong and his elder brother Baoxian returned to the capital; the Emperor invested Baozong as General Who Campaigns South, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu, and married him to a princess;
translations.idiomatic: Baozong and his elder brother Baoxian went to the capital, where the Emperor appointed Baozong General Who Campaigns South, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu and married him to an imperial princess;

sentences.zh: 保顯為鎮西將軍、晉壽公。

translations.literal: Baoxian was made General Who Guards the West and Duke of Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxian was made General Who Guards the West and Duke of Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 後遣大鴻臚崔賾拜難當為征南大將軍、儀同三司、領護西羌校尉、秦梁二州牧、南秦王。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Herald Cui Ze was sent to invest Nandang as General Who Campaigns South, with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Protecting the Western Qiang, Governor of Qin and Liang Provinces, and King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Herald Cui Ze was dispatched to invest Nandang as General Who Campaigns South, with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Protecting the Western Qiang, Governor of Qin and Liang, and King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 難當後自立為大秦王，號年曰建義，立妻為王后，世子為太子，置百官，具擬天朝。

translations.literal: Later Nandang established himself as Great King of Qin, titled his era Jianyi, made his wife queen, his heir crown prince, set up the hundred officials, fully imitating the heavenly court.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang later proclaimed himself Great King of Qin, adopted the era name Jianyi, made his wife queen and his heir crown prince, and created a full bureaucracy modeled on the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 然猶貢獻于劉義隆不絕。

translations.literal: Yet he still sent tribute to Liu Yilong without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Even so he continued to send tribute to Liu Yilong without interruption.

sentences.zh: 尋而其國大旱，多災異，降大秦王復為武都王。

translations.literal: Soon his state suffered great drought and many portents; he demoted himself from Great King of Qin back to King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his realm suffered severe drought and many omens, and he demoted himself from Great King of Qin back to King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 太延初，難當立鎮上邽，世祖遣車騎大將軍、樂平王丕等督河西高平諸軍取上邽，又詔諭難當，難當奉詔攝守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan, Nandang established a garrison at Shanggui; the Emperor sent General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Leping Pi, and others to supervise the armies of Hexi and Gaoping and take Shanggui, and also issued an edict instructing Nandang; Nandang received the edict and held the post in trust.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiyan era Nandang set up a garrison at Shanggui. The Emperor sent General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Leping Pi, and others to command the Hexi and Gaoping armies and seize Shanggui, while also issuing instructions to Nandang, who complied and withdrew to a caretaker role.

sentences.zh: 尋而傾國南寇，規有蜀土，襲義隆益州，攻涪城，又伐巴西，獲雍州流人七千餘家還于仇池。

translations.literal: Soon he mobilized the whole state to raid south, aiming to possess the land of Shu; he attacked Yilong's Yizhou, assaulted Fucheng, and also campaigned against Baxi, taking more than seven thousand households of displaced persons from Yong Province back to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he marched south with his whole kingdom, intent on seizing Shu. He invaded Yilong's Yizhou, attacked Fucheng, raided Baxi, and brought more than seven thousand refugee households from Yong Province back to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 義隆怒，遣將裴方明等伐之。

translations.literal: Yilong was enraged and sent generals Pei Fangming and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yilong sent generals such as Pei Fangming against him.

sentences.zh: 難當為方明所敗，棄仇池，與千餘騎奔上邽，世祖遣中山王辰迎之赴行宮。

translations.literal: Nandang was defeated by Fangming, abandoned Chouchi, and with more than a thousand horsemen fled to Shanggui; the Emperor sent Prince of Zhongshan Chen to welcome him to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang was defeated by Fangming, abandoned Chouchi, and fled to Shanggui with a thousand horsemen. The Emperor sent Prince of Zhongshan Chen to escort him to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 方明既克仇池，以保宗弟保熾守之，河間公齊擊走之。

translations.literal: When Fangming had taken Chouchi, he set Baozong's younger brother Baochi to guard it; Duke of Hejian Qi struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: After Fangming captured Chouchi he left Baozong's younger brother Baochi to hold it, but Duke of Hejian Qi attacked and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔保宗鎮上邽，又詔鎮駱谷，復其本國。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered Baozong to garrison Shanggui and also to garrison Luogu, restoring his original state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier edicts had ordered Baozong to garrison Shanggui and Luogu and had restored his ancestral domain.

sentences.zh: 保宗弟文德先逃氐中，乃說保宗令叛，事泄，齊執保宗送京師，詔難當殺之。

translations.literal: Baozong's younger brother Wende had first fled among the Di; he then urged Baozong to rebel. When the affair leaked out, Qi seized Baozong and sent him to the capital; an edict ordered Nandang to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Baozong's younger brother Wende had fled among the Di and persuaded Baozong to rebel. When the plot was exposed, Qi arrested Baozong and sent him to the capital, where an edict commanded Nandang to execute him.

sentences.zh: 氐羌立文德，屯于濁水。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang established Wende and encamped at Zhuoshui.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang enthroned Wende and encamped at Zhuoshui.

sentences.zh: 文德自號征西將軍、秦河梁三州牧、仇池公，求援於義隆。

translations.literal: Wende styled himself General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Qin, He, and Liang Provinces, and Duke of Chouchi, and sought aid from Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Wende styled himself General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Qin, He, and Liang, and Duke of Chouchi, and asked Yilong for help.

sentences.zh: 義隆封文德為武都王，遣偏將房亮之等助之。

translations.literal: Yilong enfeoffed Wende as King of Wudu and sent subordinate generals Fang Liangzhi and others to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong enfeoffed Wende as King of Wudu and sent subordinate generals such as Fang Liangzhi to support him.

sentences.zh: 齊逆擊，禽亮之。

translations.literal: Qi counterattacked and captured Liangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi counterattacked and captured Liangzhi.

sentences.zh: 文德奔守葭蘆，武都、陰平氐多歸之。

translations.literal: Wende fled to hold Jialu; the Di of Wudu and Yinping mostly submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wende fled to hold Jialu, and many Di of Wudu and Yinping rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 詔淮陽公皮豹子等率諸軍討之，文德走漢中，收其妻子僚屬資糧，及保宗妻公主送京師，賜死。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi and others to lead the armies to suppress him; Wende fled to Hanzhong. They seized his wife, children, officials, and provisions, and sent Baozong's wife the princess to the capital, where she was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi and others to campaign against him. Wende fled to Hanzhong. The Wei forces seized his family, officials, and supplies, sent Baozong's wife the princess to the capital, and had her executed.

sentences.zh: 初，公主勸保宗反，人問曰：「背父母之邦若何？」

translations.literal: Earlier, the princess had urged Baozong to rebel. Someone asked: "How can you turn against the land of your parents?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the princess had urged Baozong to rebel. When someone asked, "How can you turn against the land of your parents?"

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「禮，婦人外成，因夫而榮，事立，據守一方，我亦一國之母，豈比小縣之主。」

translations.literal: the princess said: "By ritual, a woman is formed outside her natal home and gains honor through her husband. Once the affair succeeds and we hold a region, I too am mother of a state—how can I be compared to the mistress of a small district?"
translations.idiomatic: the princess replied, "By ritual a woman belongs to her husband's house and shares his glory. If the venture succeeds and we hold a territory, I shall be mother of a kingdom—how can that be compared with ruling some petty county?"

sentences.zh: 以此得罪。

translations.literal: For this she was punished.
translations.idiomatic: It was for this that she was punished.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，拜難當營州刺史，還為外都大官。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, Nandang was appointed Inspector of Ying Province and later became Grand Officer of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Nandang was appointed Inspector of Ying Province and later served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子和，隨父歸國，別賜爵仇池公。

translations.literal: His son He, following his father in returning to the state, was separately granted the title Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: His son He accompanied his father back to their homeland and was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 子德襲難當爵，早卒。

translations.literal: His son De inherited Nandang's title and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son De inherited Nandang's rank but died young.

sentences.zh: 子小眼襲，例降為公，拜天水太守，卒。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyan inherited; by precedent the rank was reduced to duke; he was appointed Administrator of Tianshui and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoyan inherited the line, but by precedent the title was reduced to duke. He was appointed Administrator of Tianshui and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子大眼，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Dayan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dayan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 小眼子公熙襲爵。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan's son Gongxi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan's son Gongxi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 正光中，尚書右丞張普惠為行臺，送租於南秦、東益，普惠啟公熙俱行。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, Right Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhang Puhui served as mobile headquarters, delivering rent to Southern Qin and Eastern Yi; Puhui memorialized that Gongxi should travel with him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era Right Assistant Minister Zhang Puhui served as mobile headquarters commander delivering tax grain to Southern Qin and Eastern Yi, and he requested that Gongxi accompany the mission.

sentences.zh: 至南秦，以氐反不得進，遣公熙先慰氐。

translations.literal: When they reached Southern Qin, because the Di had rebelled they could not advance; he sent Gongxi ahead to soothe the Di.
translations.idiomatic: At Southern Qin a Di rebellion blocked their advance, so Puhui sent Gongxi ahead to pacify the Di.

sentences.zh: 東益州刺史魏子建以公熙險薄，密令訪察，公熙果有潛謀，將為叛亂。

translations.literal: Eastern Yi Inspector Wei Zijian, because Gongxi was treacherous and shallow, secretly ordered an investigation; Gongxi indeed had hidden designs and was about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yi Inspector Wei Zijian, finding Gongxi treacherous and unreliable, secretly ordered surveillance and discovered that Gongxi was indeed plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 子建仍報普惠，令其攝錄。

translations.literal: Zijian then reported to Puhui and ordered him to seize and record the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian reported to Puhui and told him to arrest Gongxi.

sentences.zh: 普惠急追，公熙竟不肯赴，東出漢中。

translations.literal: Puhui pursued in haste, but Gongxi ultimately refused to come and fled east into Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui pursued him urgently, but Gongxi refused to submit and fled east into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 普惠表列其事，公熙大行賄賂，終得免罪。

translations.literal: Puhui memorialized listing the affair; Gongxi lavished bribes on a grand scale and in the end escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui submitted a detailed report, but Gongxi bribed his way free and ultimately escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 後為假節、別將，與都督元志同守岐州，為秦賊莫折天生所虜，死於秦州。

translations.literal: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff and Separate Commander; together with Area Commander Yuan Zhi he guarded Qi Province, was captured by the Qin bandit Mozhe Tiansheng, and died in Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Bearer of the Staff and separate commander. He and area commander Yuan Zhi defended Qi Province, were captured by the Qin rebel Mozhe Tiansheng, and Gongxi died in Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 文德後自漢中入統汧隴，[12]遂有陰平、武興之地，後為劉義隆荊州刺史劉義宣所殺。

translations.literal: Later Wende from Hanzhong entered and unified Qian and Long,[12] thereby gaining the lands of Yinping and Wuxing; later he was killed by Liu Yilong's Inspector of Jing Province, Liu Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wende later marched from Hanzhong to take Qian and Long,[12] seized Yinping and Wuxing, and was eventually killed by Liu Yixuan, Liu Yilong's inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 保宗之執也，子元和奔義隆，以為武都、白水太守。

translations.literal: When Baozong was seized, his son Yuanhe fled to Yilong and was made Administrator of Wudu and Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozong was captured, his son Yuanhe fled to Yilong, who appointed him administrator of Wudu and Baishui.

sentences.zh: 元和據城歸順，高宗嘉之，拜征南大將軍、武都王，內徙京師。

translations.literal: Yuanhe held the city and submitted; Emperor Gaozong commended this and appointed him General Who Campaigns South and King of Wudu, moving him inward to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe surrendered the city. Emperor Gaozong praised his submission, made him General Who Campaigns South and King of Wudu, and resettled him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 元和從叔僧嗣復自稱武都王於葭蘆。

translations.literal: Yuanhe's younger uncle Sengsi again styled himself King of Wudu at Jialu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe's uncle Sengsi once more proclaimed himself King of Wudu at Jialu.

sentences.zh: 僧嗣死，從弟文度自立為武興王，遣使歸順，顯祖授文度武興鎮將。

translations.literal: When Sengsi died, his younger cousin Wendu established himself as King of Wuxing, sent envoys to submit, and Emperor Xianzu invested Wendu as Garrison Commander of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengsi died, his cousin Wendu declared himself King of Wuxing and sent envoys to submit. Emperor Xianzu appointed Wendu garrison commander of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 既而復叛。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，征西將軍皮歡喜攻葭蘆破之，斬文度首。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, General Who Campaigns West Pi Huanxi attacked Jialu, broke it, and beheaded Wendu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, General Who Campaigns West Pi Huanxi stormed Jialu, defeated Wendu, and took his head.

sentences.zh: 文度弟弘，小名鼠，犯顯祖廟諱，以小名稱。

translations.literal: Wendu's younger brother Hong, whose pet name was Shu, violated the taboo of Emperor Xianzu's temple name and was called by his pet name.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu's younger brother Hong, nicknamed Shu, bore a name that violated Emperor Xianzu's taboo and was known only by that nickname.

sentences.zh: 鼠自為武興王，遣使奉表謝罪，貢其方物，高祖納之。

translations.literal: Shu established himself as King of Wuxing, sent envoys with a memorial begging pardon, and presented local products; Emperor Xiaowen accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu proclaimed himself King of Wuxing, sent envoys to beg forgiveness and offer tribute, and Emperor Xiaowen received him back.

sentences.zh: 鼠遣子苟奴入侍，拜鼠都督、南秦州刺史、征西將軍、西戎校尉、武都王。

translations.literal: Shu sent his son Gounu to serve at court; Shu was appointed Area Commander, Inspector of Southern Qin Province, General Who Campaigns West, Colonel of the Western Rong, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent his son Gounu to the court as a hostage and was invested area commander, inspector of Southern Qin, general who campaigns west, colonel of the Western Rong, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 鼠死，從子後起統任，高祖復以鼠爵授之。

translations.literal: When Shu died, his younger cousin Houqi took charge of affairs; Emperor Xiaowen again invested him with Shu's titles.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu died, his cousin Houqi succeeded him, and Emperor Xiaowen confirmed him in Shu's titles.

sentences.zh: 鼠子集始為白水太守，後起死，以集始為征西將軍、武都王。

translations.literal: Shu's son Jishi was Administrator of Baishui; when Houqi died, Jishi was made General Who Campaigns West and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's son Jishi had been administrator of Baishui. When Houqi died, Jishi was appointed General Who Campaigns West and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 集始後朝于京師，拜都督、南秦州刺史、安南大將軍、領護南蠻校尉、漢中郡侯、武興王，賜以車旗戎馬錦綵繒纊等。

translations.literal: Later Jishi came to court at the capital and was appointed Area Commander, Inspector of Southern Qin Province, General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel Protecting the Southern Man, Marquis of Hanzhong Commandery, and King of Wuxing, and was granted chariots, banners, military horses, brocades, silk, and felt.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi later visited the capital and received the titles area commander, inspector of Southern Qin, general who pacifies the south, colonel protecting the southern Man, marquis of Hanzhong, and King of Wuxing, along with chariots, banners, horses, brocades, silks, and felt.

sentences.zh: 尋還武興，進號鎮南將軍，加督寧、湘等五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Wuxing and was promoted to General Who Guards the South, with added supervision of military affairs in Ning, Xiang, and five other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Wuxing, was promoted to General Who Guards the South, and was given supervisory authority over military affairs in Ning, Xiang, and five other provinces.

sentences.zh: 後仇池鎮將楊靈珍襲破武興，集始遂入蕭賾。

translations.literal: Later the garrison commander of Chouchi, Yang Lingzhen, raided and broke Wuxing; Jishi then entered the domain of Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Lingzhen, the Chouchi garrison commander, attacked and overran Wuxing, and Jishi fled into Xiao Ze's territory.

translations.literal: Textual note 13.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 13.

sentences.zh: 景明初，集始來降，還授爵位，歸守武興。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Jishi came to surrender; his titles were restored and he returned to guard Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era Jishi submitted again, had his titles restored, and returned to hold Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 死，子紹先立，拜都督、南秦州刺史、征虜將軍、漢中郡公、武興王；

translations.literal: When he died, his son Shaoxian succeeded and was appointed Area Commander, Inspector of Southern Qin Province, General Who Captures the Barbarians, Duke of Hanzhong Commandery, and King of Wuxing;
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Shaoxian succeeded and was made area commander, inspector of Southern Qin, general who captures the barbarians, duke of Hanzhong, and King of Wuxing;

sentences.zh: 贈集始車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，諡安王。

translations.literal: Jishi was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Commander with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and the posthumous title King An.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi was posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry and grand commander with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title King An.

sentences.zh: 紹先年幼，委事二叔集起、集義。

translations.literal: Shaoxian was young and entrusted affairs to his two uncles Jiqie and Jiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian was still a boy and left government to his uncles Jiqie and Jiyi.

sentences.zh: 夏侯道遷以漢中歸順也，蕭衍白馬戍主尹天保率眾圍之。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Daoyian submitted Hanzhong, Yin Tianbao, commandant of Xiao Yan's Baima garrison, led troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Daoyian surrendered Hanzhong, Yin Tianbao, the commandant of Baima under Xiao Yan, marched to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 道遷求援於集起、集義，二人貪保邊藩，不欲救之，唯集始弟集朗心願立功，率眾破天保，全漢川，集朗之力也。

translations.literal: Daoyian sought aid from Jiqie and Jiyi; the two men, greedy to preserve their border fief, did not wish to rescue him. Only Jishi's younger brother Jilang, eager to win merit, led troops and broke Tianbao, saving Han River valley—it was Jilang's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyian asked Jiqie and Jiyi for help, but they wanted only to hold their frontier domain and refused to march. Jishi's brother Jilang alone wished to earn glory, routed Tianbao, and saved the Han River region—credit belonged to Jilang.

sentences.zh: 集義見梁益既定，恐武興不得久為外藩，遂扇動諸氐，推紹先僭稱大號，集起、集義並稱王，外引蕭衍為援。

translations.literal: When Jiyi saw that Liang and Yi were already settled, he feared Wuxing could not long remain an outer fief; he therefore stirred up the Di clans, had Shaoxian usurp a grand title, and Jiqie and Jiyi both styled themselves kings, seeking aid from Xiao Yan abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Liang and Yi firmly under Wei control, Jiyi feared Wuxing could not remain a frontier kingdom. He incited the Di, had Shaoxian proclaim himself emperor, and he and Jiqie both took royal titles while calling on Xiao Yan for support.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍邢巒遣建武將軍傅竪眼攻武興，克之，執紹先送于京師，遂滅其國，以為武興鎮，復改鎮為東益州。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Xing Luan sent General Who Establishes Martial Prowess Fu Shuyan to attack Wuxing, took it, seized Shaoxian and sent him to the capital, and extinguished the state; it was made the Wuxing garrison and later changed again to Eastern Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the West Xing Luan sent Fu Shuyan to storm Wuxing, captured Shaoxian and sent him to the capital, and destroyed the kingdom. The territory became the Wuxing garrison and was later reorganized as Eastern Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 前後鎮將唐法樂，刺史杜纂、邢豹，以威惠失衷，氐豪仇石柱等相率反叛。

translations.literal: Successive garrison commanders Tang Fale and inspectors Du Zuan and Xing Bao, through imbalance of severity and kindness, caused Di chieftains such as Qiu Shizhu to rebel together in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commanders Tang Fale and the inspectors Du Zuan and Xing Bao governed with uneven severity and kindness, and Di leaders including Qiu Shizhu rose in rebellion one after another.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以西南為憂。

translations.literal: The court was troubled about the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew anxious about the southwest.

sentences.zh: 正光中，詔魏子建為刺史，以恩信招撫，風化大行，遠近款附，如內地焉。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era an edict made Wei Zijian inspector; through kindness and trust he won people over, and transforming influence spread widely. Near and far submitted in good faith, as if it were inner territory.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguang an edict appointed Wei Zijian inspector. He won people with kindness and trust until his influence reached far and wide, and the region submitted as peacefully as the heartland.

sentences.zh: 後唐永代子建為州，未幾，氐人悉反，永棄城東走，自此復為氐地。

translations.literal: Later Tang Yong replaced Zijian as inspector; before long the Di all rebelled, Yong abandoned the city and fled east, and from then on it again became Di territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong later replaced Zijian as inspector, but soon every Di clan revolted. Yong abandoned the city and fled eastward, and the region once again became Di land.

sentences.zh: 其後，紹先奔還武興，復自立為王。

translations.literal: Afterward Shaoxian fled back to Wuxing and again established himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian later escaped back to Wuxing and proclaimed himself king again.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾，本遼東鮮卑徒河涉歸子也。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun was originally a son of Shegui of the Xianbei of Tuhe in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was originally the son of Shegui, a Xianbei chieftain of Tuhe in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 涉歸一名弈洛韓，有二子，庶長曰吐谷渾，少曰若洛廆。

translations.literal: Shegui, also called Yiluohan, had two sons: the elder by a concubine was Tuyuhun, the younger was Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui, also known as Yiluohan, had two sons—the elder, born to a concubine, was Tuyuhun, and the younger was Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 涉歸死，若洛廆代統部落，別為慕容氏。

translations.literal: When Shegui died, Murong Hui succeeded to command the tribe and separately became the Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: After Shegui died, Murong Hui took command of the tribe and founded the separate Murong line.

sentences.zh: 涉歸之存也，分戶七百以給吐谷渾。

translations.literal: While Shegui was alive, he allotted seven hundred households to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: During Shegui's lifetime he assigned seven hundred households to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾與若洛廆二部馬鬬相傷，若洛廆怒，遣人謂吐谷渾曰：「先公處分，與兄異部，何不相遠，而馬鬬相傷！」

translations.literal: Horses from Tuyuhun's and Murong Hui's two divisions fought and injured one another; Murong Hui was angry and sent someone to tell Tuyuhun: "The former lord divided the allotments and gave brother a separate division—why do you not keep far apart, yet make the horses fight and injure one another!"
translations.idiomatic: Stallions from Tuyuhun's and Murong Hui's camps brawled and wounded one another. Murong Hui flew into a rage and sent a messenger to Tuyuhun: "Our father split our herds and set you apart—why do you not keep your distance instead of letting the horses fight!"

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾曰：「馬是畜耳，食草飲水，春氣發動，所以鬬。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun said: "Horses are only beasts; they eat grass and drink water, and when spring qi stirs they fight.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun replied: "Horses are animals—they graze and drink, and when spring stirs them they fight.

sentences.zh: 鬬在馬而怒及人，乖別甚易，今當去汝萬里之外。」

translations.literal: The fight is in the horses yet anger reaches men; to split apart is very easy—now I shall go ten thousand li from you."
translations.idiomatic: The quarrel belongs to the horses, yet wrath falls on men. Parting is easy enough; I shall now take my people ten thousand li away from you."

sentences.zh: 若洛廆悔，遣舊老及長史七那樓追謝留之。

translations.literal: Murong Hui regretted it and sent old retainers and Chief Clerk Qina Lou to pursue, apologize, and detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui repented and sent elder clansmen and his chief clerk Qina Lou to overtake him, apologize, and ask him to stay.

sentences.zh: [14]吐谷渾曰：「我乃祖以來，樹德遼右，先公之世，卜筮之言，云有二子當享福祚，並流子孫。

translations.literal: [14]Tuyuhun said: "From my ancestors onward we planted virtue in the right of Liaodong; in the former lord's time divination said two sons would enjoy fortune and rank, and both would pass blessing to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: [14]Tuyuhun answered: "Since our forefathers we have built merit in eastern Liaodong. In our father's day the oracle promised two sons who would flourish and leave fortune to their descendants.

sentences.zh: 我是卑庶，理無並大，今以馬致乖，殆天所啟。

translations.literal: I am lowborn; by principle there is no sharing greatness; now because of horses we are estranged—perhaps Heaven opens the way.
translations.idiomatic: I am the younger son and by right cannot share equal greatness. If a horse fight drives us apart, perhaps Heaven itself has opened the way.

sentences.zh: 諸君試驅馬令東，馬若還東，我當隨去。」

translations.literal: Gentlemen, try driving the horses east; if the horses return east, I shall follow and go."
translations.idiomatic: Try driving the herds east—if they turn back east, I will follow you home."

sentences.zh: 即令從騎擁馬令回，數百步，欻然悲鳴，突走而西，聲若頹山，如是者十餘輩，一回一迷。

translations.literal: He then ordered his mounted followers to crowd the horses and turn them back; after several hundred paces they suddenly wailed, broke away and ran west, their sound like a collapsing mountain—more than ten times this happened, each turn ending in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He had his riders herd the horses around, but after a few hundred paces they suddenly whinnied in grief, bolted westward with a sound like falling mountains, and did so more than ten times—each attempt ending in chaos.

sentences.zh: 樓力屈，乃跪曰：「可汗，此非復人事。」

translations.literal: Lou's strength gave out; he then knelt and said: "Khan, this is no longer a matter of human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Qina Lou was overcome and knelt, saying: "Khan, this is no longer within men's power."

sentences.zh: 渾謂其部落曰：「我兄弟子孫並應昌盛，廆當傳子及曾玄孫，其間可百餘年，我及玄孫間始當顯耳。」

translations.literal: Tuyuhun said to his tribe: "My brother's descendants and mine should both flourish; Hui will pass the throne to son and to great-great-grandson—between them may be more than a hundred years. Between me and my great-great-grandson's line glory will only then appear."
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun told his people: "Both our lines are destined to prosper. Hui's house will reign for more than a hundred years through son and great-great-grandson, while my line will not shine until the time of my distant heirs."

sentences.zh: 於是遂西附陰山，後假道上隴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attached himself to the west at Yin Mountain, and later borrowed the road to ascend Long.
translations.idiomatic: With that he moved west to Yin Mountain and later passed through Long by borrowed routes.

sentences.zh: 若洛廆追思吐谷渾，作阿干歌，徒河以兄為阿干也。

translations.literal: Murong Hui, remembering Tuyuhun, composed the A'gan Song; in Tuhe one calls an elder brother a'gan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui, longing for Tuyuhun, composed the A'gan Song—in Tuhe speech an elder brother is called a'gan.

sentences.zh: 子孫僭號，以此歌為輦後鼓吹大曲。

translations.literal: Their descendants who usurped titles took this song as the great court music played behind the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers who took royal titles made the song the grand processional music played behind the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾遂徙上隴，止於枹罕暨甘松，南界昂城、龍涸，從洮水西南極白蘭數千里中，逐水草，廬帳而居，以肉酪為糧。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun then moved up onto Long, stopping at Baohan and Gansong; on the south the border was Angcheng and Longhu; from the southwest along the Tao River to Bailan for several thousand li they followed grass and water, dwelling in felt tents, and took meat and curds as provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun then migrated onto Long, settling at Baohan and Gansong with southern borders at Angcheng and Longhu. For thousands of li from the Tao River southwest to Bailan they followed pasture and water, lived in felt tents, and lived on meat and curds.

sentences.zh: 西北諸種謂之阿柴虜。

translations.literal: The various tribes of the northwest called them the Achai barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern peoples called them the Achai barbarians.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾死，有子六十人。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun died he had sixty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun left sixty sons at his death.

sentences.zh: 長子吐延，身長七尺八寸，勇力過人，性刻暴，為昂城羌酋姜聰所刺。

translations.literal: The eldest son Tuyan was seven feet eight inches tall, surpassing others in courage and strength, harsh and violent by nature, and was stabbed by Jiang Cong, chieftain of the Angcheng Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tuyan stood seven feet eight inches tall, excelled in courage and strength, and was fierce and brutal by nature. He was assassinated by Jiang Cong, chieftain of the Angcheng Qiang.

sentences.zh: 劍猶在體，呼子葉延，語其大將紇拔埿曰：「吾氣絕，棺斂訖，便速去保白蘭，地既險遠，又土俗懦弱，易控御。

translations.literal: The sword still in his body, he called his son Yeyan and told his great general Heba Kun: "When my breath ends, after the coffin is closed, go quickly to hold Bailan—the land is both perilous and remote, and the local customs are weak and easily controlled.
translations.idiomatic: With the blade still in him he summoned his son Yeyan and told his great general Heba Kun: "When I die, seal my coffin and at once withdraw to hold Bailan. The place is rugged and far away, and the people there are timid and easy to rule.

sentences.zh: 葉延小兒，欲授餘人，恐倉卒終不能相制。

translations.literal: Yeyan is a small child; if I wished to give the remainder to another man, I fear that in haste in the end he could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Yeyan is only a boy. If I handed power to someone else, I fear no one could keep control in a crisis.

sentences.zh: 今以葉延付汝，竭股肱之力以輔之。

translations.literal: Now I entrust Yeyan to you—exhaust the strength of your arms and legs to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: I now place Yeyan in your hands—give him the full strength of your service.

sentences.zh: 孺子得立，吾無恨也。」

translations.literal: If the child can be established, I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: If the boy can hold the throne, I will die content."

sentences.zh: 抽劍而死。

translations.literal: He drew out the sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled free the sword and died.

sentences.zh: 有子十二人。

translations.literal: He had twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve sons survived him.

sentences.zh: 葉延少而勇果，年十歲，縛草為人，號曰姜聰，每旦輒射之，射中則嘷叫泣涕。

translations.literal: Yeyan was young yet brave and resolute; at age ten he bound straw into the shape of a man, called it Jiang Cong, and every morning shot at it—when he hit it he would howl and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Yeyan was young but bold and resolute. At ten he fashioned a straw figure named Jiang Cong and shot at it each morning; whenever he hit the mark he wailed and wept.

sentences.zh: 其母曰：「讎賊諸將已屠膾之，汝年小，何煩朝朝自苦。」

translations.literal: His mother said: "The enemy chieftains have already minced him— you are young; why trouble yourself morning after morning with self-torment?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother said: "The enemy leaders have already cut Jiang Cong to pieces. You are only a child—why torment yourself every morning?"

sentences.zh: 葉延嗚咽若不自勝，答母曰：「誠知無益，然罔極之心，不勝其痛。」

translations.literal: Yeyan sobbed as if unable to bear it and answered his mother: "I truly know it is of no use, yet the heart of boundless grief cannot overcome the pain."
translations.idiomatic: Yeyan wept as though crushed and answered: "I know it does no good, but grief for my father is more than I can bear."

sentences.zh: 性至孝，母病三日不食，葉延亦不食。

translations.literal: By nature he was supremely filial; when his mother was ill and did not eat for three days, Yeyan also did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial: when his mother fell ill and fasted for three days, Yeyan fasted with her.

sentences.zh: 頗視書傳，自謂曾祖弈洛韓始封昌黎公，吾為公孫之子，案禮，公孫之子得以王父字為氏，遂以吐谷渾為氏焉。

translations.literal: He looked somewhat to books and records and said to himself that his great-grandfather Yiluohan was first enfeoffed Duke of Changli; he was the son of a duke's grandson, and according to ritual a duke's grandson's son may take his grandfather's style as clan name—therefore he took Tuyuhun as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: He read books and concluded that his great-grandfather Yiluohan had first been enfeoffed as Duke of Changli. As a grandson of that house, he held that ritual allowed him to take his grandfather's name as a clan—and so he adopted Tuyuhun as his surname.

sentences.zh: 葉延死，子碎奚立，性淳謹，三弟專權，碎奚不能制，諸大將共誅之。

translations.literal: When Yeyan died his son Suixi succeeded; Suixi was simple and careful, but three younger brothers monopolized power and Suixi could not control them—the great generals jointly executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yeyan died his son Suixi succeeded. Suixi was honest and cautious, but three younger brothers seized power and he could not restrain them, so the senior commanders put the three to death together.

sentences.zh: 奚憂哀不復攝事，遂立子視連為世子，委之事，號曰「莫賀郎」，華言父也。

translations.literal: Suixi, grieving and sorrowful, no longer handled affairs; he then established his son Shilian as heir and entrusted affairs to him, calling him "Mohelang"—in Chinese speech, "father."
translations.idiomatic: Overcome by grief, Suixi ceased to govern and installed his son Shilian as heir, handing him the reins and calling him Mohelang—"father" in their tongue.

sentences.zh: 碎奚遂以憂死。

translations.literal: Suixi then died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Suixi soon died of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 視連立，以父憂思，不遊娛酣宴。

translations.literal: When Shilian succeeded, because of his father's grief and brooding he did not roam for pleasure or hold feasts.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shilian took power he shunned pleasure and banquets out of mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 十五年，死，弟視羆立。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; his younger brother Shipi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of his reign, and his brother Shipi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: [17]死，子樹洛干等並幼，弟烏紇提立而妻樹洛干母，生二子慕璝、利延。

translations.literal: [17]When he died, his sons Shuluogan and the others were all young; his younger brother Wuheti succeeded and married Shuluogan's mother, begetting two sons, Murong Gui and Liyan.
translations.idiomatic: [17]After his death Shuluogan and the other sons were still children. His brother Wuheti took the throne and married Shuluogan's mother, fathering Murong Gui and Liyan.

sentences.zh: [18]烏紇提一名大孩，死，樹洛干立，自號車騎將軍，是歲晉義熙初也。

translations.literal: [18]Wuheti, also called Daha, died; Shuluogan succeeded and styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry—it was the beginning of the Yixi era of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: [18]Wuheti, also known as Daha, died, and Shuluogan succeeded, taking the title General of Chariots and Cavalry—in the first year of Jin's Yixi era.

sentences.zh: 樹洛干死，弟阿豺立，自號驃騎將軍、沙州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shuluogan died his younger brother Ache succeeded and styled himself General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Sha Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuluogan died his brother Ache took power, styling himself General of Agile Cavalry and inspector of Sha Province.

sentences.zh: 部內有黃沙，周回數百里，不生草木，因號「沙州」。

translations.literal: Within the territory there was yellow sand encircling several hundred li where no grass or trees grew; therefore it was called "Sha Province."
translations.idiomatic: A belt of yellow sand hundreds of li across where nothing grew gave the region the name "Sha Province."

sentences.zh: 阿豺兼并羌氐，地方數千里，號為強國。

translations.literal: Ache annexed the Qiang and Di and held territory of several thousand li, styled a powerful state.
translations.idiomatic: Ache absorbed Qiang and Di peoples and ruled several thousand li of land, becoming a powerful kingdom.

sentences.zh: 田于西強山，觀墊江源，問於羣臣曰：「此水東流，有何名？

translations.literal: He hunted fields on Xiqiang Mountain, viewed the source of the Dian River, and asked his ministers: "This water flows east—what is its name?
translations.idiomatic: While hunting on Xiqiang Mountain he looked upon the source of the Dian River and asked his ministers: "This stream runs east—what is it called?

sentences.zh: 由何郡國入何水也？」

translations.literal: Through what commanderies and kingdoms does it enter what river?"
translations.idiomatic: Through which commanderies and kingdoms does it flow, and into what river does it empty?"

sentences.zh: 其長史曾和曰：「此水經仇池，過晉壽，出宕渠，號墊江，至巴郡入江，度廣陵會於海。」

translations.literal: His chief clerk Zeng He said: "This water passes Chouchi, crosses Jinsou, exits Dangqu, is called the Dian River, reaches Ba Commandery and enters the Yangzi, crosses Guangling and meets the sea."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zeng He answered: "It passes Chouchi, crosses Jinsou, leaves Dangqu as the Dian River, reaches Ba Commandery and joins the Yangzi, then passes Guangling and reaches the sea."

sentences.zh: 阿豺曰：「水尚知有歸，吾雖塞表小國，而獨無所歸乎？」

translations.literal: Ache said: "Even water knows where to return—though I am a small state beyond the frontier, am I alone without a place to return?"
translations.idiomatic: Ache said: "If even a river knows its way home, can a small frontier kingdom like ours have nowhere to belong?"

sentences.zh: 遣使通劉義符，獻其方物，義符封為澆河公。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to communicate with Liu Yifu and presented local products; Yifu enfeoffed him Duke of Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Liu Yifu with tribute, and Yifu enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 未及拜受，劉義隆元嘉三年又加除命。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the investiture and accept it, in the third year of Yuanjia Liu Yilong again added further appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could receive the title, Liu Yilong added new honors in the third year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 又將遣使朝貢，會暴病，臨死召諸子弟告之曰：「先公車騎捨其子虔以大業屬吾，吾豈敢忘先公之舉而私於緯代，其以慕璝繼事。」

translations.literal: He was again about to send envoys to pay court tribute when he suddenly fell gravely ill; on his deathbed he summoned his sons and younger brothers and told them: "The former lord, General of Chariots and Cavalry, set aside his son Qian and entrusted the great enterprise to me—how could I dare forget the former lord's act and favor Weidai privately? Let Murong Gui succeed to affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He was preparing another tribute mission when he fell suddenly ill. Dying, he gathered his sons and brothers and said: "General of Chariots and Cavalry passed over his son Qian and gave me the realm—I cannot betray that choice for Weidai's sake. Let Murong Gui succeed."

sentences.zh: 阿豺有子二十人，緯代，長子也。

translations.literal: Ache had twenty sons; Weidai was the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Ache fathered twenty sons; Weidai, the eldest, stood first among them.

sentences.zh: 阿豺又謂曰：「汝等各奉吾一隻箭，折之地下。」

translations.literal: Ache also said: "Each of you take one of my arrows and break it on the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Ache also told them: "Each of you, take one of my arrows and break it against the ground."

sentences.zh: [19]俄而命母弟慕利延曰：「汝取一隻箭折之。」

translations.literal: [19]Soon he ordered his younger brother by the same mother, Muliyan: "You take one arrow and break it."
translations.idiomatic: [19]Then he told his uterine brother Muliyan: "You—take one arrow and break it."

sentences.zh: 慕利延折之。

translations.literal: Muliyan broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Muliyan snapped it.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「汝取十九隻箭折之。」

translations.literal: He again said: "You take nineteen arrows and break them."
translations.idiomatic: He then said: "Now take nineteen arrows and break them together."

sentences.zh: 延不能折。

translations.literal: Muliyan could not break them.
translations.idiomatic: Muliyan could not snap them.

sentences.zh: 阿豺曰：「汝曹知否？

translations.literal: Ache said: "Do you all understand?
translations.idiomatic: Ache asked: "Do you see?

sentences.zh: 單者易折，眾則難摧，戮力一心，然後社稷可固。」

translations.literal: Alone one is easily broken; gathered many are hard to destroy—only by uniting strength with one heart can the altars of state then be made firm."
translations.idiomatic: One arrow breaks easily; many resist breaking. Only if you stand together can the realm endure."

sentences.zh: 言終而死。

translations.literal: When the words ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: With those words he died.

sentences.zh: 兄子慕璝立。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Murong Gui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Murong Gui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 先是阿豺時，劉義隆命竟未至而死，慕璝又奉表通義隆，義隆又授隴西公。

translations.literal: Earlier in Ache's time Liu Yilong's appointment had not yet arrived when he died; Murong Gui again submitted a memorial to communicate with Yilong, and Yilong again invested him Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: During Ache's reign Liu Yilong's patent had not arrived before he died. Murong Gui sent another memorial to Yilong, who enfeoffed him Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 慕璝招集秦涼亡業之人及羌戎雜夷眾至五六百落，南通蜀漢，北交涼州、赫連，部眾轉盛。

translations.literal: Murong Gui gathered people from Qin and Liang who had lost their livelihoods and mixed tribes of Qiang and Rong to five or six hundred settlements; south he connected with Shu and Han, north he allied with Liang Province and Helian, and his following grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui gathered refugees from Qin and Liang and Qiang and Rong tribes into five or six hundred settlements, opened ties south to Shu and Han and north to Liang Province and Helian, and his power steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，慕璝始遣其侍郎謝大寧奉表歸國，尋討禽赫連定，送之京師。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizu's time Murong Gui first sent his Gentleman of the Palace Xie Daning with a memorial to return to the realm; soon afterward he captured Helian Ding and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Murong Gui first sent his gentleman of the palace Xie Daning with a memorial of submission and soon captured Helian Ding and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，遣使者策拜慕璝為大將軍、西秦王。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu commended this and sent an envoy with a patent appointing Murong Gui Great General and King of Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu praised him and dispatched an envoy to invest Murong Gui as great general and King of Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 慕璝表曰：「臣誠庸弱，敢竭情款，俘禽僭逆，獻捷王府。

translations.literal: Murong Gui memorialized: "Your subject is truly mediocre and weak, yet dares exhaust sincere loyalty, capture the usurping rebel, and present the victory to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui wrote: "I am unworthy, yet I have done my utmost in loyalty, captured a rebel pretender, and offer this victory to the throne.

sentences.zh: 爵秩雖崇而土不增廓，車旗既飾而財不周賞，願垂鑒察，亮其單款。

translations.literal: Though rank and title are lofty, my territory is not enlarged; though chariots and banners are adorned, wealth is not sufficient for rewards—may you look down with clear inspection and illuminate my simple sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: My titles are grand but my lands have not grown; my honors are splendid but I lack wealth to reward my men. I beg Your Majesty to see the sincerity behind my plea.

sentences.zh: 臣頃接寇逆，疆境之人，為賊所抄，流轉東下，今皇化混一，求還鄉土。

translations.literal: Your subject has recently met border rebels; people of the frontier were plundered by the bandits and drifted eastward. Now that imperial transformation unifies all, they seek to return to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck my borders, many frontier people were seized and driven east. Now that the empire is united, they wish to go home.

sentences.zh: 乞佛日連、[20]窟略寒、張華等三人家弱在此，分乖可愍，願并敕遣使，恩洽遐荒，存亡感戴。」

translations.literal: Qifo Rilian,[20] Kuluehan, Zhang Hua, and three other households with weak members here, separated from kin—pitiable in their parting— I beg that edicts and envoys be sent together; grace reaching the far wilds, the living and dead alike would be moved to gratitude."
translations.idiomatic: Qifo Rilian,[20] Kuluehan, Zhang Hua, and three other families have vulnerable kin stranded here, torn from their people—a separation that moves pity. I ask that envoys be sent to reunite them; mercy reaching the remotest lands would win gratitude from the living and the dead alike."

sentences.zh: 世祖詔公卿朝會議答施行。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered the Three Excellencies and ministers to assemble in court council, reply, and carry out the decision.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu ordered the chief ministers to convene, draft a reply, and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫嵩及議郎、博士二百七十九人議曰：「前者有司處以為秦王荒外之君，本非政教所及，來則受之，去則不禁。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhangsun Song together with deliberating officials and academicians, two hundred seventy-nine in all, deliberated: "Earlier the responsible office held that as King of Qin beyond the wilds, he was originally not within the reach of government and teaching—if he came he was received; if he left he was not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhangsun Song and two hundred seventy-nine deliberating officials and academicians reported: "Earlier the ministry held that as a king beyond the frontier he lay outside normal governance—if he came he was welcomed; if he left he was not stopped.

sentences.zh: 皇威遠被，西秦王慕義畏威，稱臣納貢，求受爵號。

translations.literal: Imperial majesty reaches far; the King of Western Qin Murong Gui, admiring righteousness and fearing might, declared himself subject, paid tribute, and sought to receive titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Now imperial power reaches far abroad. Murong Gui, King of Western Qin, admiring our virtue and awed by our might, has submitted, sent tribute, and asked for titles.

sentences.zh: 議者以為古者要荒之君，雖人土眾廣，而爵不擬華夏。

translations.literal: Deliberators held that in antiquity lords of the outer and wild domains, though their people and lands were broad and their populations numerous, did not receive ranks matching those of Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors argued that in antiquity even powerful lords of the outer marches received ranks below those of the Central States.

sentences.zh: 陛下加寵王官，及越常分，容飾車旗，班同上國。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has heaped favor on his kingly offices, exceeding the usual shares, allowed the adornment of chariots and banners, and granted him ranks equal to those of the highest states.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has lavished princely honors upon him, gone beyond ordinary provision, allowed full chariot and banner insignia, and ranked him with the foremost realms.

sentences.zh: 至於繒絮多少，舊典所無，皆當臨時以制豐寡。

translations.literal: As for how much silk floss is given, the old canon has nothing on this; all should be decided on the spot according to abundance or scarcity.
translations.idiomatic: The amount of silk floss owed is nowhere fixed in ancient precedent; such gifts should be adjusted as circumstances warrant.

sentences.zh: 自漢魏以來，撫接荒遐，頗有故事。

translations.literal: Since Han and Wei, in pacifying and receiving the remote wilds, there have been quite a few precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei times, the court's dealings with distant frontier peoples have followed many established precedents.

sentences.zh: 呂后遺單于御車二乘、馬二駟，單于答馬千匹；

translations.literal: Empress Lü sent the Chanyu two imperial chariots and eight horses; the Chanyu replied with a thousand horses;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü sent the Chanyu two royal chariots and eight horses; the Chanyu returned the gift with a thousand horses;

sentences.zh: 其後匈奴和親，敵國遺繒絮不過數百；

translations.literal: Afterward, when the Xiongnu made peace through marriage, silk floss sent between rival states did not exceed several hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Xiongnu made marriage alliances, gifts of silk floss between equal powers rarely exceeded a few hundred rolls;

sentences.zh: 呼韓邪稱臣，身自入朝，始至萬匹。

translations.literal: When Huhanye declared himself subject and personally entered court, it rose to ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Huhanye submitted in person and came to court did the tribute reach ten thousand rolls.

sentences.zh: [21]今西秦王若以土無桑蠶，便當上請，不得言『財不周賞』。

translations.literal: [21] Now if the King of Western Qin says his land has no mulberry or silkworms, he should petition above accordingly and may not speak of 'wealth insufficient for rewards.'
translations.idiomatic: [21] If the King of Western Qin claims his land lacks mulberry and silkworms, he should say so in a formal petition—not plead that his wealth falls short of rewarding his men.

sentences.zh: 昔周室衰微，齊侯小白一匡天下，有賜胙之命，無益土之賞；

translations.literal: In the past, when the house of Zhou declined, Duke Huan of Qi, Xiaobai, once righted the realm under Heaven—he received the command to share sacrificial meat, but no reward of additional lands;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou weakened, Duke Huan of Qi restored order to the realm. He received the right to share the royal sacrifice—but no grant of new territory;

sentences.zh: 晉侯重耳破楚城濮，唯受南陽之田為朝宿之邑。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin, Chong'er, defeated Chu at Chengpu and received only the fields of Nanyang as a lodging place when attending court.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin crushed Chu at Chengpu and received only the fields of Nanyang as lodging for court visits.

sentences.zh: 西秦所致，唯定而已。

translations.literal: What Western Qin presented was only Helian Ding, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: All Western Qin offered was the capture of Helian Ding—nothing else.

sentences.zh: 塞外之人，因時乘便，侵入秦涼，未有經略拓境之勳，爵登上國，統秦、涼、河、沙四州之地，而云『土不增廓』。

translations.literal: A man beyond the passes, seizing the moment and taking advantage, invaded Qin and Liang; he has no merit of grand strategy in expanding borders, yet his rank mounts to an upper state, he holds the four provinces of Qin, Liang, He, and Sha, and yet says 'territory not enlarged.'
translations.idiomatic: A frontier chieftain seized an opening to raid Qin and Liang, yet has won no great merit in conquering new lands. He holds princely rank over Qin, Liang, He, and Sha—and still complains that his territory has not grown.

sentences.zh: 比聖朝於弱周，而自同於五霸，無厭之情，其可極乎？

translations.literal: Comparing the sacred court to weak Zhou, yet equating himself with the Five Hegemons—such insatiable disposition, can it ever reach its limit?
translations.idiomatic: He likens our dynasty to feeble Zhou while placing himself among the Five Hegemons. Can such boundless greed ever be satisfied?

sentences.zh: 西秦王忠款於朝廷，原其本情，必不至此，或左右不敏，因致斯累。

translations.literal: The King of Western Qin is sincerely loyal to the court; judging his original intent, he surely would not go this far—perhaps attendants lacking wisdom caused this burden.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Western Qin is genuinely loyal; he would never mean this himself. Likely unwise advisers have led him astray.

sentences.zh: 檢西秦流人賊時所抄，悉在蒲坂，今既稱藩，四海咸泰，天下一家，可敕秦州送詣京師，隨後遣還。

translations.literal: Examining Western Qin refugees plundered in bandit times, all are at Puban; now that he has declared himself a vassal state and all within the four seas is calm and the realm is one family, Qin Province may be ordered to send them to the capital and afterward dispatch them back.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Western Qin seized in the raids are held at Puban. Now that he submits as a vassal and the empire is at peace, Qin Province should send them to the capital and then home again.

sentences.zh: 所請乞佛三人，昔為賓國之使，來在王庭，國破家遷，即為臣妾，可勿聽許。」

translations.literal: The three Qifo men requested—formerly envoys from Bin, they came to the royal court; when their state was destroyed and families relocated, they became servants and concubines; permission may be withheld."
translations.idiomatic: As for the three Qifo men he requests: they came once as envoys from Bin, stayed at court, and when their state fell became servants here. His request should be refused."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「公卿之議，未為失體。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The ministers' counsel has not lost propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your counsel is not improper.

sentences.zh: 西秦王所收金城、枹罕、隴西之地，彼自取之，朕即與之，便是裂土，何須復廓。

translations.literal: The lands the King of Western Qin took—Jincheng, Fuhan, and Longxi—he seized himself, and I granted them to him; that is already the splitting of territory; why must it be enlarged again?
translations.idiomatic: The King of Western Qin took Jincheng, Fuhan, and Longxi by his own effort, and I confirmed those gains. That is already a territorial grant—why must his borders grow further?

sentences.zh: 西秦款至，綿絹隨使疏數增益之，非一匹而已。」

translations.literal: When Western Qin sends sincere tribute, silk and gauze follow the envoys in frequency and quantity increasing—it is not a single roll alone."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Western Qin sends tribute, we increase the silk and gauze with each mission—far more than a single roll."

sentences.zh: 自是慕璝貢獻頗簡，又通于劉義隆，義隆封為隴西王。

translations.literal: From this Murong Gui's tribute grew rather sparse, and he also opened ties with Liu Yilong, who enfeoffed him King of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Murong Gui's tribute grew sparse, and he also opened ties with Liu Yilong, who enfeoffed him King of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 太延二年，慕璝死，弟慕利延立，詔遣使者策諡慕璝曰惠王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiyan, Murong Gui died; his younger brother Muliyan succeeded; an edict sent envoys to confer posthumous title on Murong Gui as King Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiyan, Murong Gui died and his younger brother Muliyan succeeded him. The court sent envoys to posthumously ennoble Murong Gui as King Hui.

sentences.zh: 後拜慕利延鎮西大將軍、儀同三司，改封西平王；

translations.literal: Later Muliyan was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and given the Three Excellencies' ceremonial parity, and his title was changed to King of Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: Later Muliyan was appointed general who pacifies the west with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and his title was changed to King of Xiping;

sentences.zh: 以慕璝子元緒為撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Murong Gui's son Yuanxu was made General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui's son Yuanxu was appointed general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 時慕利延又通劉義隆，義隆封為河南王。

translations.literal: At that time Muliyan again opened ties with Liu Yilong, who enfeoffed him King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Muliyan again communicated with Liu Yilong, who enfeoffed him King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 世祖征涼州，慕利延懼，遂率其部人西遁沙漠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against Liang Province, Muliyan was afraid and led his tribes west in flight into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched on Liang Province, Muliyan in fear led his people west into the desert.

sentences.zh: 世祖以慕利延兄有禽赫連定之功，遣使宣喻之，乃還。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, because Muliyan's elder brother had the merit of capturing Helian Ding, sent envoys to proclaim and instruct him, and he then returned.
