translations.idiomatic: Because Muliyan's elder brother had captured Helian Ding, Emperor Shizu sent envoys to summon him back, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 後慕利延遣使表謝，書奏，乃下詔褒奬之。

translations.literal: Later Muliyan sent envoys with a memorial of apology; when the memorial was submitted, an edict was issued commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Muliyan sent envoys with a memorial of apology; the emperor accepted it and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 慕利延兄子緯代懼慕利延害己，與使者謀欲歸國，慕利延覺而殺之。

translations.literal: Muliyan's elder brother's son Weidai, fearing Muliyan would harm him, plotted with the envoy to return to the realm; Muliyan discovered this and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Weidai, a nephew of Muliyan, fearing Muliyan would kill him, plotted with the envoy to defect to the Wei court. Muliyan discovered the plot and executed him.

sentences.zh: 緯代弟叱力延等八人逃歸京師，請兵討慕利延。

translations.literal: Weidai's younger brother Chilijyan and seven others fled to the capital and requested troops to punish Muliyan.
translations.idiomatic: Weidai's younger brother Chilijyan and seven others fled to the capital and asked for troops to attack Muliyan.

sentences.zh: 世祖拜叱力延歸義王，詔晉王伏羅率諸將討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu invested Chilijyan as Prince of Guyi, and ordered Prince of Jin Fulu to lead the generals to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu enfeoffed Chilijyan as prince of Guyi and ordered Prince of Jin Fulu to lead the generals against Muliyan.

sentences.zh: 軍至大母橋，慕利延兄子拾寅走河西，伏羅遣將追擊之，斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: When the army reached Damuqiao, Muliyan's elder brother's son Shiyin fled to Hexi; Fulu sent generals in pursuit and beheaded more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Damuqiao, Muliyan's nephew Shiyin fled to Hexi. Fulu sent generals in pursuit and took more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 慕利延走白蘭。

translations.literal: Muliyan fled to Bailan.
translations.idiomatic: Muliyan fled to Bailan.

sentences.zh: 慕利延從弟伏念、長史䳕鳩黎、部大崇娥等率眾一萬三千落歸降。

translations.literal: Muliyan's younger cousin Funian, Chief Clerk Wanjiu Li, tribal elder Chong'e, and others led more than thirteen thousand settlements in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Muliyan's cousin Funian, chief clerk Wanjiu Li, tribal elder Chong'e, and others led thirteen thousand settlements in surrender.

sentences.zh: 後復遣征西將軍、高涼王那等討之於白蘭，慕利延遂入于闐國，殺其王，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Later the court again sent General Who Campaigns West, Prince of Gaoliang Na, and others to attack him at Bailan; Muliyan then entered the state of Khotan, killed its king, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: The court again sent General Who Campaigns West Prince of Gaoliang Na and others against him at Bailan. Muliyan then invaded Khotan, killed its king, and left tens of thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 南征罽賓。

translations.literal: He campaigned south against Kapisa.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south against Kapisa.

sentences.zh: 遣使通劉義隆求援，獻烏丸帽、女國金酒器、胡王金釧等物，義隆賜以牽車。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to Liu Yilong seeking aid, presenting a Wuhuan cap, golden wine vessels from the Land of Women, a golden armlet of the king of the Hu, and other objects; Yilong granted him a carriage for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Liu Yilong seeking aid, offering a Wuhuan cap, golden wine vessels from the Land of Women, a Hu king's golden armlet, and other gifts; Yilong rewarded him with an imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 七年，遂還舊土。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned to his former lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he returned to his former territory.

sentences.zh: 慕利延死，樹洛干子拾寅立，始邑於伏羅川，其居止出入竊擬王者。

translations.literal: When Muliyan died, Shuluogan's son Shiyin succeeded, first establishing his seat at Fuluochuan; in dwelling, coming and going, he secretly modeled himself on a king.
translations.idiomatic: When Muliyan died, Shuluogan's son Shiyin succeeded him and first established his capital at Fuluochuan. In his residence and daily conduct he quietly imitated a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 拾寅奉修貢職，受朝廷正朔，又受劉義隆封爵，號河南王。

translations.literal: Shiyin maintained tribute duties, accepted the court's calendar, and also received enfeoffment from Liu Yilong, taking the title King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin fulfilled tribute obligations, accepted the Wei calendar, and also received titles from Liu Yilong as King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣使拜為鎮西大將軍、沙州刺史、西平王。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent envoys to appoint him General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Sha Province, and King of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent envoys to appoint him general who pacifies the west, inspector of Sha Province, and King of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 後拾寅自恃險遠，頗不恭命，通使于劉彧，獻善馬、四角羊，彧加之官號。

translations.literal: Later Shiyin, relying on his perilous distance, was rather disrespectful of orders, sent envoys to Liu Yu, and presented fine horses and four-horned sheep; Yu added to his titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shiyin, trusting in his remote stronghold, grew insubordinate, sent envoys to Liu Yu, and offered fine horses and four-horned sheep; Yu added further titles.

sentences.zh: [22]高宗時，定陽侯曹安表拾寅今保白蘭，多有金銀牛馬，若擊之，可以大獲。

translations.literal: [22] In the time of Emperor Gaozong, Marquis of Dingyang Cao An memorialized that Shiyin now held Bailan and possessed much gold, silver, cattle, and horses; if attacked, great gains could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: [22] Under Emperor Gaozong, Marquis of Dingyang Cao An reported that Shiyin held Bailan with abundant gold, silver, cattle, and horses—a strike there could yield great spoils.

sentences.zh: 議者咸以先帝忿拾寅兄弟不穆，使晉王伏羅、高涼王那再征之，竟不能克。

translations.literal: Counselors all held that the former emperor resented the discord of Shiyin and his brothers and had Prince of Jin Fulu and Prince of Gaoliang Na campaign against them twice, yet in the end could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors argued that the late emperor, angered by Shiyin and his brothers' disloyalty, had sent Prince of Jin Fulu and Prince of Gaoliang Na against them twice without success.

sentences.zh: 拾寅雖復遠遁，軍亦疲勞。

translations.literal: Though Shiyin again fled far away, the army was also exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shiyin fled far away again, the army was exhausted as well.

sentences.zh: 今在白蘭，不犯王塞，不為人患，非國家之所急也。

translations.literal: Now at Bailan he does not violate the royal frontier and is no harm to men—it is not what the state urgently needs.
translations.idiomatic: Now at Bailan he does not threaten the frontier and poses no danger; this is not an urgent concern for the state.

sentences.zh: 若遣使招慰，必求為臣妾，可不勞而定也。

translations.literal: If envoys are sent to summon and reassure him, he will surely seek to become subject and concubine-state; without labor one may settle it.
translations.idiomatic: If envoys are sent to win him over, he will surely submit as a vassal—and the matter can be settled without war.

sentences.zh: 王者之於四荒，羈縻而已，何必屠其國有其地。

translations.literal: For a king toward the four wilds, loose reins are enough—why must one slaughter his state and possess his land?
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign's dealings with distant peoples need only loose reins—why slaughter their state and seize their land?

sentences.zh: 安曰：「臣昔為澆河戍將，與之相近，明其意勢。

translations.literal: An said: "Your subject was formerly garrison commander at Jiaohe, close to them, and understands their intent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Cao An said: "I was once garrison commander at Jiaohe, near their territory, and I know their situation well.

sentences.zh: 若分軍出其左右，拾寅必走保南山，不過十日，牛馬草盡，人無所食，眾必潰叛，可一舉而定也。」

translations.literal: If troops are divided to emerge on his left and right, Shiyin will surely flee to hold the southern mountains; within ten days at most, cattle and horses will exhaust the grass, men will have nothing to eat, the masses will surely collapse and rebel, and in one stroke it can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Split the army to flank him on both sides and Shiyin will flee into the southern mountains. Within ten days his herds will strip the pasture bare, his people will starve, his followers will break—and he can be taken in one stroke."

sentences.zh: 從之，詔陽平王新成、建安王穆六頭等出南道，南郡公李惠、給事中公孫拔及安出北道以討之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted; an edict ordered Prince of Yangping Xincheng, Prince of Jian'an Muliutou, and others to march by the southern route, and Duke of Nanjun Li Hui, Attendant-in-Ordinary Gongsun Ba, and An by the northern route to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and ordered Prince of Yangping Xincheng and Prince of Jian'an Muliutou south, while Duke of Nanjun Li Hui, Attendant-in-Ordinary Gongsun Ba, and Cao An marched north against Shiyin.

sentences.zh: 拾寅走南山，諸軍濟河追之。

translations.literal: Shiyin fled to the southern mountains; the armies crossed the river in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin fled into the southern mountains and the armies crossed the river in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時軍多病，諸將議賊已遠遁，軍容已振，今驅疲病之卒，要難冀之功，不亦過乎。

translations.literal: At that time the army had many sick; the generals deliberated that the bandits had already fled far, the army's spirit was already roused—now to drive weary and sick soldiers to demand hard-to-hope-for achievement, is that not excessive?
translations.idiomatic: The army was rife with sickness. The generals argued that the enemy had fled far and morale was already high—driving exhausted, sick troops after a doubtful victory would be going too far.

sentences.zh: 眾以為然，乃引還，獲駝馬二十餘萬。

translations.literal: The masses thought this right, and they withdrew; they captured more than two hundred thousand camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed and turned back, capturing more than two hundred thousand camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 顯祖復詔上黨王長孫觀等率州郡兵討拾寅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu again ordered Prince of Shangdang Zhangsun Guan and others to lead provincial and commandery troops to punish Shiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu again ordered Prince of Shangdang Zhangsun Guan and others to lead regional troops against Shiyin.

sentences.zh: 軍至曼頭山，拾寅來逆戰，觀等縱兵擊敗之，拾寅宵遁。

translations.literal: When the army reached Mantou Mountain, Shiyin came to oppose in battle; Guan and the others released troops and defeated him, and Shiyin fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: At Mantou Mountain, Shiyin met them in battle. Guan routed his forces and Shiyin fled by night.

sentences.zh: 於是思悔，復修藩職，遣別駕康盤龍奉表朝貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reflected in regret and again maintained vassal duties, sending Vice Director Kang Panlong with a memorial to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin repented and resumed vassal obligations, sending Vice Director Kang Panlong with tribute to court.

sentences.zh: 顯祖幽之，不報其使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu detained him and did not reply to his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu held him and gave no answer to his envoy.

sentences.zh: 拾寅部落大饑，屢寇澆河，詔平西將軍、廣川公皮歡喜率敦煌、枹罕、高平諸軍為前鋒，司空、上黨王長孫觀為大都督以討之。

translations.literal: Shiyin's tribes suffered great famine and repeatedly raided Jiaohe; an edict ordered General Who Pacifies the West, Duke of Guangchuan Pi Huanxi, to lead the armies of Dunhuang, Fuhan, and Gaoping as vanguard, and Minister of Works, Prince of Shangdang Zhangsun Guan, as grand commander to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin's tribes suffered famine and repeatedly raided Jiaohe. The court ordered General Who Pacifies the West Duke of Guangchuan Pi Huanxi to lead Dunhuang, Fuhan, and Gaoping troops as vanguard, with Minister of Works Prince of Shangdang Zhangsun Guan as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 觀等軍入拾寅境，芻其秋稼，拾寅窘怖，遣子詣軍，表求改過。

translations.literal: When Guan and the others' army entered Shiyin's territory, they cut his autumn grain; Shiyin was cornered in fear and sent his son to the army with a memorial seeking to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's army entered Shiyin's territory and destroyed his autumn harvest. Cornered, Shiyin sent his son with a memorial pleading to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 觀等以聞，顯祖以重勞將士，乃下詔切責之，徵其任子。

translations.literal: Guan and the others reported this; Emperor Xianzu, because the troops had been greatly wearied, issued an edict sternly rebuking him and summoned his hostage son.
translations.idiomatic: Guan reported this to court. Emperor Xianzu, mindful of the army's heavy labors, issued a stern rebuke and demanded a hostage.

sentences.zh: 拾寅遣子斤入侍，顯祖尋遣斤還。

translations.literal: Shiyin sent his son Jin to attend at court; Emperor Xianzu soon sent Jin back.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin sent his son Jin to serve at court; Emperor Xianzu soon sent Jin home again.

sentences.zh: 拾寅後復擾掠邊人，遣其將良利守洮陽、枹罕所統，枹罕鎮將、西郡公楊鍾葵貽拾寅書以責之。

translations.literal: Later Shiyin again harassed and plundered frontier people; he sent his general Liangli to hold what Taoyang and Fuhan commanded, and Fuhan Garrison Commander, Duke of Xijun Yang Zhongkui, sent Shiyin a letter rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin again raided the frontier and sent his general Liangli to hold Taoyang and Fuhan. Yang Zhongkui, garrison commander of Fuhan and Duke of Xijun, wrote to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 拾寅表曰：「奉詔聽臣還舊土，故遣良利守洮陽，若不追前恩，求令洮陽貢其土物。」

translations.literal: Shiyin memorialized: "Obeying the edict allowing your subject to return to former lands, I therefore sent Liangli to hold Taoyang; if former grace is not pursued, I ask that Taoyang be allowed to pay tribute in local goods."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin wrote: "By your edict permitting my return to our former lands, I sent Liangli to hold Taoyang. If you will not press old grievances, I ask that Taoyang be allowed to send local tribute."

sentences.zh: 辭旨懇切，顯祖許之。

translations.literal: The wording was earnest; Emperor Xianzu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: His plea was earnest, and Emperor Xianzu agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是歲修職貢。

translations.literal: From this he paid annual tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he sent tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，拾寅死，子度易侯立，遣其侍郎時真貢方物，提上表稱嗣事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, Shiyin died; his son Duyihou succeeded, sent his Gentleman of the Palace Shizhen with regional products in tribute, and submitted a memorial claiming succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe, Shiyin died. His son Duyihou succeeded, sent Gentleman of the Palace Shizhen with tribute, and memorialized to announce his succession.

sentences.zh: [23]後度易侯伐宕昌，詔讓之，賜錦綵一百二十匹，喻令悛改，所掠宕昌口累部送時還。

translations.literal: [23] Later Duyihou attacked Chouchi; an edict rebuked him, granted a hundred twenty rolls of brocade and silk, instructed him to repent and reform, and ordered the Chouchi people and livestock he had seized to be sent back at once.
translations.idiomatic: [23] Later Duyihou attacked Chouchi. The court rebuked him, granted a hundred and twenty rolls of brocade and silk, urged repentance, and ordered the Chouchi captives and livestock returned at once.

sentences.zh: 易侯並奉詔。

translations.literal: Yihou obeyed the edict in both matters.
translations.idiomatic: Duyihou obeyed both commands.

sentences.zh: 死，子伏連籌立。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Fulianchou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Fulianchou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲令入朝，表稱疾病，輒修洮陽、泥和城而置戍焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu wished to have him enter court; he memorialized claiming illness and immediately repaired Taoyang and Nihe cities and placed garrisons there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu wanted him to come to court, but he pleaded illness and at once fortified Taoyang and Nihe and posted garrisons there.

sentences.zh: 文明太后崩，使人告凶，伏連籌拜命不恭，有司請伐之，高祖不許。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, envoys were sent to announce the bereavement; Fulianchou received the command without respect, and the responsible office requested a campaign against him, but Emperor Gaozu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, the court sent envoys to announce the mourning. Fulianchou received the news disrespectfully; officials urged an attack, but Emperor Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 羣臣以其受詔不敬，不宜納所獻。

translations.literal: Ministers held that because he received the edict without reverence, what he offered should not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued that because he had been disrespectful in receiving the edict, his tribute should be refused.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「拜受失禮，乃可加以告責，[24]所獻土毛，乃是臣之常道，杜棄所獻，便是絕之，縱欲改悔，其路無由矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Failure in ritual when receiving condolences can be met with rebuke and reproof,[24] but the regional products offered are a subject's constant duty; to reject what is offered is to cut him off— even if he wished to repent, there would be no path for it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: "Improper mourning etiquette deserves rebuke,[24] but tribute of local goods is a vassal's ordinary duty. To reject it is to sever ties—and then even repentance would have no avenue."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕在哀疚之中，未有征討，而去春枹罕表，取其洮陽、泥和二戍。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I am in the midst of mourning grief and have not yet undertaken campaigns, yet last spring the Fuhan memorial took back the two garrisons of Taoyang and Nihe.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "While I am still in mourning and have not yet marched to war, last spring the Fuhan garrison reported that he had retaken the garrisons at Taoyang and Nihe.

sentences.zh: 時以此既邊將之常，即便聽許。

translations.literal: At the time, because this was already the frontier generals' usual practice, permission was immediately granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was treated as routine frontier business, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 及偏師致討，二戍望風請降，執訊二千餘人，又得婦女九百口。

translations.literal: When a detached force was sent to punish him, the two garrisons surrendered at the first wind; prisoners taken numbered more than two thousand, and nine hundred women were also captured.
translations.idiomatic: When a punitive force was sent, both garrisons surrendered at once. More than two thousand captives were taken, along with nine hundred women.

sentences.zh: 子婦可悉還之。」

translations.literal: Daughters-in-law may all be returned."
translations.idiomatic: The daughters-in-law among them may all be sent home."

sentences.zh: 伏連籌乃遣世子賀魯頭朝于京師，禮錫有加，拜伏連籌使持節、都督西垂諸軍事、征西將軍、領護西戎中郎將、西海郡開國公、吐谷渾王，麾旗章綬之飾皆備給之。

translations.literal: Fulianchou then sent his heir Helutou to attend court at the capital; ritual gifts were added, and Fulianchou was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in the Western March, General Who Campaigns West, Chief Protector of the Western Rong Central Command, Duke of Xihai with an open state, King of Tuyuhun—with banners, flags, seals, and cords all fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Fulianchou then sent his heir Helutou to court. The emperor honored him with rich gifts and invested Fulianchou as bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs on the western march, general who campaigns west, chief protector of the western Rong, Duke of Xihai, and King of Tuyuhun—with full insignia of banners, seals, and cords.

sentences.zh: 後遣兼員外散騎常侍張禮使於伏連籌，伏連籌謂禮曰：「昔與宕昌通和，恒見稱大王，己則自名，今忽名僕而拘執此使，將命偏師往問其意。」

translations.literal: Later Assistant Supernumerary Palace Attendant Zhang Li was sent as envoy to Fulianchou; Fulianchou said to Li: "Formerly I was at peace with Chouchi; I was always addressed as great king while naming myself—now suddenly you call me servant and detain this envoy; I will order a detached force to ask your intent."
translations.idiomatic: Later Assistant Supernumerary Palace Attendant Zhang Li was sent to Fulianchou, who told him: "When I was at peace with Chouchi, you always called me great king while I used my own name. Now you suddenly call me servant and detain this envoy—I will send a force to ask your meaning."

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「君與宕昌並為魏藩，而比輒有興動，殊違臣節。

translations.literal: Li said: "You and Chouchi are both Wei vassals on the frontier, yet you repeatedly take aggressive action—this greatly violates the duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Li replied: "You and Chouchi are both Wei frontier vassals, yet you keep stirring trouble—this is a grave breach of subjecthood.

sentences.zh: 當發之日，宰輔以為君若反迷知罪，則克保藩業，脫守愚不改，則禍難將至。」

translations.literal: On the day of departure, the chief ministers held that if you turn back from error and know your guilt, you can preserve your vassal estate; if you stubbornly hold to folly unchanged, calamity and disaster will soon arrive."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left, the chief ministers judged that if Fulianchou recognized his fault he could keep his realm—but if he persisted in folly, disaster would follow."

sentences.zh: 伏連籌遂默然。

translations.literal: Fulianchou then fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Fulianchou said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，遣使赴哀，盡其誠敬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died, he sent envoys to mourn and fully showed sincerity and respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu died, he sent envoys to mourn with full sincerity and respect.

sentences.zh: 伏連籌內修職貢，外并戎狄，塞表之中，號為強富。

translations.literal: Fulianchou internally maintained tribute duties and externally annexed Rong and Di; among the frontier regions he was called strong and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Fulianchou maintained tribute at home and conquered neighboring Rong and Di tribes; on the frontier he was accounted powerful and wealthy.

sentences.zh: 準擬天朝，樹置官司，稱制諸國，以自誇大。

translations.literal: Modeling himself on the heavenly court, he established official posts, assumed authority over the states, and thereby glorified himself.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled his court on the imperial government, set up offices, and claimed dominion over neighboring states to aggrandize himself.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，詔責之曰：「梁州表送卿報宕昌書，梁彌邕與卿並為邊附，語其國則隣藩，論其位則同列，而稱書為表，名報為旨，有司以國有常刑，殷勤請討。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Shizong's reign, an edict rebuked him: "Liang Province has forwarded your reply to Chouchi; Liang Miyou and you are both frontier dependents—speaking of your states you are neighboring vassals, speaking of your ranks you are equals—yet you call your letter a memorial and name your reply an instruction; the responsible office, citing the state's fixed punishments, earnestly requests a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign an edict rebuked him: "Liang Province has forwarded your letter to Chouchi. You and Liang Miyou are both frontier vassals—neighbors in status and equals in rank—yet you style your letter a memorial and your reply an instruction. Officials, citing the law, urgently recommend an attack.

sentences.zh: 朕慮險遠多虞，輕相構惑，故先宣此意，善自三思。」

translations.literal: I consider that perilous distance holds many uncertainties and lightly setting discord in motion is unwise; therefore I first proclaim this intent—think carefully three times."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in such remote country small provocations could spiral out of control, so I warn you first—think hard before you act."

sentences.zh: 伏連籌上表自申，辭誠懇至。

translations.literal: Fulianchou submitted a memorial in his own defense; the wording was sincerely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Fulianchou submitted a memorial in his own defense, earnest and sincere.

sentences.zh: 終世宗世至于正光，犛牛蜀馬及西南之珍無歲不至。

translations.literal: From Emperor Shizong's time until Zhengguang, yak, horses from Shu, and treasures of the southwest came every year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Shizong's reign through Zhengguang, yaks, Shu horses, and treasures of the southwest arrived every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 後秦州城人莫折念生反，河西路絕，涼州城人萬于菩提等東應念生，[25]囚刺史宋穎。

translations.literal: Later Qin Province city men Mo Zheniansheng rebelled, the Hexi road was cut off, and Liang Province city men Wan Yu Puti and others responded to Niansheng in the east,[25] imprisoning Inspector Song Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mo Zheniansheng rebelled in Qin Province and cut the Hexi route. Wan Yu Puti and other men of Liang Province city joined Niansheng in the east,[25] imprisoning Inspector Song Ying.

sentences.zh: 穎密遣求援於伏連籌，伏連籌親率大眾救之，遂獲保全。

translations.literal: Ying secretly sent to seek aid from Fulianchou; Fulianchou personally led a great host to rescue him, and he was thereby fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ying secretly appealed to Fulianchou, who led a large force in person to rescue him and preserved the province.

sentences.zh: 自爾以後，關徼不通，貢獻路絕。

translations.literal: From then on the frontier passes were not open and the tribute road was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: After that the frontier passes closed and tribute ceased.

sentences.zh: 伏連籌死，子夸呂立，始自號為可汗，居伏俟城，在青海西十五里，雖有城郭而不居，恒處穹廬，隨水草畜牧。

translations.literal: When Fulianchou died, his son Kuailü succeeded, first styling himself khan and dwelling at Fuhou City, fifteen li west of Qinghai; though there were walls and towns he did not dwell in them, always staying in felt tents and following grass and water to pasture livestock.
translations.idiomatic: When Fulianchou died, his son Kuailü succeeded and first took the title khan, establishing himself at Fuhou City fifteen li west of Qinghai. Though he had walled towns he did not live in them, always dwelling in felt tents and moving with pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 其地東西三千里，南北千餘里。

translations.literal: His territory was three thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: His domain stretched three thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.

sentences.zh: 官有王公、僕射、尚書及郎將、將軍之號。

translations.literal: Offices included prince, vice director, secretary, and titles of commandant, general, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His offices included princes, vice directors, secretaries, and ranks such as commandants and generals.

sentences.zh: 夸呂椎髻毦珠，以皂為帽，坐金師子牀。

translations.literal: Kuailü wore his hair in a topknot with yak-tail beads, used black for his cap, and sat on a golden lion couch.
translations.idiomatic: Kuailü wore a topknot adorned with yak-tail beads, a black cap, and sat on a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 號其妻為「恪尊」，衣織成裙，披錦大袍，辮髮於後，首戴金花冠。

translations.literal: He called his wife 'Kezun'; she wore woven skirts, draped a brocade great robe, braided her hair behind, and on her head wore a golden flower crown.
translations.idiomatic: He addressed his wife as 'Kezun.' She wore woven skirts and a brocade great robe, braided her hair behind, and crowned herself with a golden flower diadem.

sentences.zh: 其俗：丈夫衣服略同於華夏，多以羅冪為冠，亦以繒為帽；

translations.literal: Their customs: men's clothing was roughly the same as Huaxia; many used gauze veils for caps, and some also used silk for caps;
translations.idiomatic: In custom, men's dress resembled that of Huaxia; many wore gauze veils as caps, and some wore silk caps;

sentences.zh: 婦人皆貫珠貝，束髮，以多為貴。

translations.literal: Women all strung pearls and shells and bound their hair; having many was prized.
translations.idiomatic: Women strung pearls and shells in their hair; the more they wore, the higher their status.

sentences.zh: 兵器有弓刀甲矟。

translations.literal: Weapons included bows, swords, armor, and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms were bows, swords, armor, and spears.

sentences.zh: 國無常賦，須則稅富室商人以充用焉。

translations.literal: The state had no fixed levies; when need arose it taxed wealthy households and merchants to fill expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: The state levied no fixed taxes; when funds were needed it taxed wealthy households and merchants.

sentences.zh: 其刑罰：殺人及盜馬者死，餘則徵物以贖罪，亦量事決杖；

translations.literal: Its punishments: those who killed persons and stole horses were put to death; for the rest goods were levied to redeem crimes, and beating was also applied according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Their legal code prescribed death for murder and horse theft; lesser offenses could be redeemed with goods, and corporal punishment was meted out according to the severity of the crime.

sentences.zh: 刑人，必以氈蒙頭，持石從高擊之。

translations.literal: When punishing persons, they necessarily covered the head with felt and struck it by holding a stone from on high.
translations.idiomatic: When executing a criminal, they always covered his head with felt and crushed it with a stone dropped from a height.

sentences.zh: 父兄死，妻後母及嫂等，與突厥俗同。

translations.literal: When fathers and elder brothers died, they took stepmothers and elder brothers' wives, the same as Turkic custom.
translations.idiomatic: After a father or elder brother died, they married their stepmother or sisters-in-law—a custom shared with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 至于婚，貧不能備財者，輒盜女去。

translations.literal: As for marriage, those poor and unable to prepare wealth simply stole girls away.
translations.idiomatic: As for marriage, men too poor to assemble bride-price simply abducted girls.

sentences.zh: 死者亦皆埋殯。

translations.literal: The dead also were all buried and laid in coffins.
translations.idiomatic: They buried and coffined their dead like settled peoples.

sentences.zh: 其服制，葬訖則除之。

translations.literal: Their mourning garb—when burial was finished it was cast off.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress was worn only until the burial was complete, then discarded.

sentences.zh: 性貪婪，忍於殺害。

translations.literal: By nature greedy, long-suffering in killing.
translations.idiomatic: They were greedy by nature and callous about killing.

sentences.zh: 好射獵，以肉酪為糧。

translations.literal: Fond of mounted hunting, with meat and curds as provisions.
translations.idiomatic: They loved hunting on horseback and lived on meat and fermented milk.

sentences.zh: 亦知種田，大麥、粟、豆，然其北界氣候多寒，唯得蕪菁、大麥，故其俗貧多富少。

translations.literal: They also knew how to plant fields—barley, millet, beans—yet on their northern border the climate was mostly cold; only turnips and barley could be had, so their custom had many poor and few rich.
translations.idiomatic: They also cultivated barley, millet, and beans, but the northern frontier was too cold for most crops; only turnips and barley would grow, leaving most of the people poor and only a few wealthy.

sentences.zh: 青海周回千餘里，海內有小山，每冬冰合後，以良牝馬置此山，至來春收之，馬皆有孕，所生得駒，號為龍種，必多駿異。

translations.literal: Qinghai Lake circled for more than a thousand li; inside the lake was a small hill; each winter after the ice formed, fine mares were set on this hill; when come spring they were gathered, the mares all had conceived, and the foals born were called "dragon-seed" and were often outstanding and unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Lake measures over a thousand li around. There is a small islet in the lake: each winter, once the ice had frozen solid, they would leave choice mares on it, and when they collected them in spring every mare was in foal. The colts born there were called "dragon stock," and they were almost always fine and exceptional beasts.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾嘗得波斯草馬，放入海，因生驄駒，能日行千里，世傳青海驄者是也。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun once obtained Persian grass horses, released them into the lake, and thereby produced piebald foals able to travel a thousand li in a day—what the age transmitted as Qinghai piebald is this.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun once obtained steppe horses from Persia and turned them loose on the lake, producing piebald colts famed for running a thousand li in a day—the legendary Qinghai piebald.

sentences.zh: 土出犛牛、馬，多鸚鵡，饒銅、鐵、朱沙。

translations.literal: The land produced yak, horses; many parrots; rich in copper, iron, and cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: The region yielded yaks and horses and teemed with parrots; copper, iron, and cinnabar were abundant.

sentences.zh: 地兼鄯善、且末。

translations.literal: The territory included Shanshan and Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands incorporated the former kingdoms of Shanshan and Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 興和中，齊獻武王作相，招懷荒遠，蠕蠕既附於國，夸呂遣使致敬。

translations.literal: In Xinghe, Prince Xianwu of Qi served as chancellor, winning over the distant wilds; Rouran having already attached to the state, Kouelü sent envoys to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era, Prince Xianwu of Qi took power as chief minister and courted far-flung peoples. After the Rouran submitted to the Wei, Kouelü sent envoys to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 獻武王喻以大義，徵其朝貢，夸呂乃遣使人趙吐骨真假道蠕蠕頻來，又薦其從妹，靜帝納以為嬪。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu instructed in the great righteousness and summoned tribute; Kouelü then sent the envoy Zhao Tugujia by way of the Rouran to come repeatedly, and also recommended his cousin—a girl the Emperor Jing took as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu lectured Kouelü on imperial duty and demanded tribute. Kouelü then sent an envoy, Zhao Tugujia, via Rouran territory on repeated missions, and offered his cousin in marriage; Emperor Jing took her as a palace consort.

sentences.zh: 遣員外散騎常侍傅靈㯹使於其國。

translations.literal: He dispatched Attendant Within and Outside the Palace Fu Linggui as envoy to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent the Attendant Within and Outside the Palace, Fu Linggui, as envoy to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 夸呂又請婚，乃以濟南王匡孫女為廣樂公主以妻之。

translations.literal: Kouelü again requested marriage; thereupon a granddaughter of Prince Kuang of Jinan was made Princess Guangyue and given as wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Kouelü asked for another marriage alliance, the Wei bestowed a granddaughter of Prince Kuang of Jinan as Princess Guangyue and sent her as his bride.

sentences.zh: 此後朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: After this tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions continued without interruption thereafter.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾北有乙弗勿敵國。

translations.literal: North of Tuyuhun was the state of Yifu Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: North of Tuyuhun lay the land of the Yifu Wudi.

sentences.zh: 俗風與吐谷渾同。

translations.literal: Their customs and air were the same as Tuyuhun's.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs matched those of the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 不識五穀，唯食魚及蘇子。

translations.literal: They did not know the five grains; they ate only fish and Perilla seeds.
translations.idiomatic: They knew nothing of grain agriculture and subsisted on fish and Perilla seeds.

sentences.zh: 蘇子狀若中國苟𣏌子。

translations.literal: Perilla seeds in form resembled China's goukou seeds.
translations.idiomatic: Perilla seeds looked much like the hemp seeds grown in China.

sentences.zh: 北又有阿蘭國。

translations.literal: Further north was also the state of Alan.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north lay the country of the Alans.

sentences.zh: 與鳥獸同，不知鬬戰，忽見異人，舉國便走。

translations.literal: Same as birds and beasts, they did not know combat; suddenly seeing strange people, the whole country fled.
translations.idiomatic: They lived like wild animals and knew nothing of warfare; at the first sight of strangers the entire people would flee.

sentences.zh: 土無所出，大養羣畜。

translations.literal: The land produced nothing; they greatly raised herds in flocks.
translations.idiomatic: The soil yielded almost nothing; they lived by pasturing vast herds.

sentences.zh: 體輕工走，逐之不可得。

translations.literal: Their bodies were light and skilled at running; pursued, they could not be caught.
translations.idiomatic: They were light-footed runners whom pursuers could never overtake.

sentences.zh: 北又有女王國。

translations.literal: North also was a women's-kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north still lay a women's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 以女為主，人所不至，其傳云然。

translations.literal: With women as rulers—no one reached it; the tradition says so.
translations.idiomatic: It was ruled by women and lay beyond human reach—or so legend had it.

sentences.zh: 宕昌羌者，其先蓋三苗之胤，周時與庸、蜀、微、盧等八國從武王滅商，漢有先零、燒當等，世為邊患。

translations.literal: The Dangchang Qiang—their forebears were probably descendants of the Three Miao; in Zhou times with Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu, and the eight states they followed King Wu to destroy Shang; in Han there were Xianling, Shaodang, and the like, for generations border afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: The Dangchang Qiang traced their origins to the Three Miao. In Zhou times they were among eight tribes—along with Yong, Shu, Wei, and Lu—that joined King Wu's campaign against the Shang. Han records mention the Xianling and Shaodang clans, who had been frontier troublemakers for generations.

sentences.zh: 其地東接中華，西通西域，南北數千里，姓別自為部落，酋帥皆有地分，不相統攝，宕昌即其一也。

translations.literal: Their territory east joined the Middle Kingdom, west connected the Western Regions, north-south several thousand li; surnames split into separate tribes, chieftains each had land divisions, not ruling one another—Dangchang was one of these.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands stretched from the Chinese frontier west to the Western Regions, several thousand li north to south. Each clan formed its own tribe under chiefs who held separate territories without a common overlord; Dangchang was one such group.

sentences.zh: 俗皆土著，居有屋宇，其屋織犛牛尾及羖羊毛覆之。

translations.literal: Their custom was all sedentary; dwellings had houses, and the houses wove yak tails and goat-and-sheep wool to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: They were settled agriculturalists who lived in permanent dwellings roofed with woven yak hair and wool.

sentences.zh: 國無法令，又無徭賦。

translations.literal: The state had no laws and ordinances, and also no corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: The community had neither written law nor regular taxation.

sentences.zh: 惟戰伐之時，乃相屯聚，不然則各事生業，不相往來。

translations.literal: Only when waging war did they gather together; otherwise each pursued livelihood, not interacting.
translations.idiomatic: Only in wartime did they mass together; in peacetime each household tended its own affairs in isolation.

sentences.zh: 皆衣裘褐。

translations.literal: All wore fur and coarse cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone dressed in furs and homespun wool.

sentences.zh: 牧養犛牛、羊、豕以供其食。

translations.literal: They herded and raised yak, sheep, pigs to supply their food.
translations.idiomatic: They raised yaks, sheep, and pigs for food.

sentences.zh: [26]父子、伯叔、兄弟死者，即以繼母、世叔母及嫂、弟婦等為妻。

translations.literal: [26] When fathers and sons, paternal uncles, and brothers died, they took stepmothers, paternal uncles' widows, sisters-in-law, and younger brothers' wives as wives.
translations.idiomatic: [26] When a father, uncle, or brother died, his widow—whether stepmother, aunt by marriage, sister-in-law, or sister of a deceased younger brother—might be taken as wife.

sentences.zh: [27]俗無文字，但候草木榮落，記其歲時。

translations.literal: [27] Their custom had no writing; they only watched plants' flourish and wither to record the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: [27] They had no written language and reckoned the year by watching when plants bloomed and faded.

sentences.zh: 三年一相聚，殺牛羊以祭天。

translations.literal: Every three years they gathered once, slaughtered cattle and sheep to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once every three years they assembled to slaughter cattle and sheep in sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有梁懃者，世為酋帥，得羌豪心，乃自稱王焉。

translations.literal: There was one Liang Qin, for generations a chieftain, who won the hearts of Qiang magnates and thereupon styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: A chieftain named Liang Qin, whose family had long led the tribe, won over the Qiang nobles and declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 懃孫彌忽，世祖初，遣子彌黃奉表求內附，世祖嘉之，遣使拜彌忽為宕昌王，賜彌黃爵甘松侯。

translations.literal: Qin's grandson Mihuo—at the start of Emperor Shizu's reign sent his son Mihuang with a memorial seeking internal attachment; Shizu approved, sent envoys to invest Mihuo as King of Dangchang, and bestowed on Mihuang the title Marquis of Gansong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's grandson Mihuo submitted early in Emperor Shizu's reign, sending his son Mihuang with a petition to join the Wei. Shizu was pleased: he enfeoffed Mihuo as King of Dangchang and gave Mihuang the title Marquis of Gansong.

sentences.zh: 彌忽死，孫虎子立。

translations.literal: Mihuo died; grandson Huzi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Mihuo died, his grandson Huzi took the throne.

sentences.zh: 其地自仇池以西，東西千里，席水以南，[28]南北八百里，地多山阜，人二萬餘落。

translations.literal: Its territory from Chou Pool westward, east-west a thousand li, south of the Xi River, [28] north-south eight hundred li; the land mostly hills and mounds; people more than twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain ran a thousand li east to west from Chou Pool and eight hundred li north to south below the Xi River, [28] a country of hills supporting more than twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 世修職貢，頗為吐谷渾所斷絕。

translations.literal: For generations they maintained tribute duty, yet were often cut off by Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: They had long sent tribute to the court, though Tuyuhun frequently blocked their missions.

sentences.zh: 虎子死，彌治立。

translations.literal: Huzi died; Mizhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Huzi died, Mizhi came to power.

sentences.zh: 虎子弟羊子先奔吐谷渾，吐谷渾遣兵送羊子，欲奪彌治位。

translations.literal: Huzi's younger kinsman Yangzi first fled to Tuyuhun; Tuyuhun sent troops escorting Yangzi, intending to seize Mizhi's position.
translations.idiomatic: Huzi's cousin Yangzi had fled to Tuyuhun, which now sent troops to escort him home and wrest the throne from Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 彌治遣使請救，顯祖詔武都鎮將宇文生救之，羊子退走。

translations.literal: Mizhi sent envoys requesting rescue; Emperor Xianzu ordered Wudu garrison commander Yuwen Sheng to save them; Yangzi withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi appealed for help, and Emperor Xianzu ordered Yuwen Sheng, the commander at Wudu, to intervene; Yangzi retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 彌治死，子彌機立，遣其司馬利住奉表貢方物。

translations.literal: Mizhi died; son Miji succeeded and sent his Chief Clerk Lizhu with a memorial presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: After Mizhi's death his son Miji took over and sent Chief Clerk Lizhu with tribute goods and a letter of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 楊文度之叛，圍武都，彌機遣其二兄率眾救武都，破走文度。

translations.literal: When Yang Wendu rebelled and besieged Wudu, Miji dispatched his two elder brothers leading troops to rescue Wudu, routing and driving off Wendu.
translations.idiomatic: During Yang Wendu's rebellion, when he besieged Wudu, Miji sent his two elder brothers with an army to relieve the city and drive Wendu off.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，遣使子橋表貢朱沙、雌黃、白石膽各一百斤。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time, they sent the envoy Ziqiao with a memorial presenting cinnabar, orpiment, and white stone gall each one hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozu they sent Ziqiao to present a hundred jin each of cinnabar, orpiment, and white copper sulfate.

sentences.zh: 自此後，歲以為常，朝貢相繼。

translations.literal: From this afterward, yearly it became constant; tribute missions followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute became an annual obligation, sent year after year without fail.

sentences.zh: 後高祖遣鴻臚劉歸、謁者張察拜彌機征南大將軍、西戎校尉、梁益二州牧、河南公、宕昌王。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu sent Grand Herald Liu Gui and Usher Zhang Cha to invest Miji as General Who Conquers the South, Commandant of the Western Rong, Governor of Liang and Yi provinces, Duke of Henan, and King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Gaozu dispatched Liu Gui of the Grand Herald's office and Usher Zhang Cha to appoint Miji General Who Conquers the South, Western Rong Commandant, governor of Liang and Yi provinces, Duke of Henan, and King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 後朝于京師，殊無風禮。

translations.literal: Later when paying court at the capital, utterly without courtly decorum.
translations.idiomatic: When he later visited the capital, he showed almost no understanding of court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 朝罷，高祖顧謂左右曰：「『夷狄之有君，不如諸夏之亡也』。

translations.literal: Court finished, Emperor Gaozu turned and said to attendants: "'Barbarians with lords are not equal to the Central States without them.
translations.idiomatic: After the audience ended, Emperor Gaozu turned to those beside him and said: "'Barbarians who keep their rulers are still not the equal of the Central Lands without them.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王雖為邊方之主，乃不如中國一吏。」

translations.literal: The King of Dangchang though a lord of the border regions was indeed not equal to one official of the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Though he ruled a border kingdom, the King of Dangchang was less polished than a single petty clerk of China."

sentences.zh: 於是改授領護西戎校尉、靈州刺史，王如故，賜以車騎、戎馬、錦綵等，遣還國。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned to serve as Protector Commandant of the Western Rong, Inspector of Ling Province; the kingship remained as before; he was granted chariots, horses, war mounts, brocade silks, and the like, and sent back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, Miji was given a new appointment as Protector Commandant of the Western Rong and Inspector of Ling Province while retaining his royal title. He received chariots, horses, war mounts, and brocades as gifts, then was sent home.

sentences.zh: 高昌者，車師前王之故地，漢之前部地也。

translations.literal: Gaochang—it was the former territory of the King of Front Cheshi, Han's "Front Division" land.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang occupied the old domain of the Front Cheshi kingdom, what Han sources called the "Eastern Division" territory.

sentences.zh: 東西二千里，南北五百里，四面多大山。

translations.literal: East-west two thousand li, north-south five hundred li; on four sides many great mountains.
translations.idiomatic: It stretched two thousand li east to west and five hundred li north to south, ringed by high mountains on every side.

sentences.zh: 或云昔漢武遣兵西討，師旅頓弊其中，尤困者因住焉。

translations.literal: Some say in olden days Emperor Wu of Han sent troops west to campaign; armies halted and exhausted within it, and those especially distressed therefore settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when Emperor Wu sent his armies west, exhausted troops stranded there gave up the campaign and settled for good.

sentences.zh: 地勢高敞，人庶昌盛，因云「高昌」。

translations.literal: The terrain was high and open, population flourishing—therefore called "Gaochang" [High and Flourishing].
translations.idiomatic: The land was high and open and its people thrived, which is why it was called Gaochang—"Lofty and Flourishing."

sentences.zh: 亦云其地有漢時高昌壘，故以為國號。

translations.literal: Also it is said the land had a Han-era Gaochang fort, therefore taken as the state name.
translations.idiomatic: Others say the name came from a Han-period fortress called Gaochang that once stood there.

sentences.zh: 東去長安四千九百里，漢西域長史、戊己校尉並居於此。

translations.literal: East from Chang'an four thousand nine hundred li; Han's Chief Commandant of the Western Regions and the Wuji Colonel both dwelt here.
translations.idiomatic: It lay forty-nine hundred li east of Chang'an, where Han stationed both the Chief Commandant for the Western Regions and the Wuji Colonel.

sentences.zh: 晉以其地為高昌郡，張軌、呂光、沮渠蒙遜據河西，皆置太守以統之。

translations.literal: Jin made its land Gaochang Commandery; Zhang Gui, Lü Guang, and Juqu Mengxun holding Hexi all set prefects to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin organized the area as Gaochang Commandery, and successive rulers of Hexi—Zhang Gui, Lü Guang, and Juqu Mengxun among them—appointed governors to control it.

sentences.zh: 去敦煌十三日行。

translations.literal: From Dunhuang thirteen days' journey.
translations.idiomatic: It was thirteen days' travel from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 國有八城，皆有華人。

translations.literal: The state had eight cities, all with Chinese people.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom comprised eight walled towns, each with a Chinese population.

sentences.zh: 地多石磧。

translations.literal: The land mostly stony desert.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the terrain was gravelly wasteland.

sentences.zh: 氣候溫暖，厥土良沃，穀麥一歲再熟，宜蠶，多五果，又饒漆。

translations.literal: Climate warm; its soil good and fertile; grain and wheat twice ripe in one year; suitable for silkworms; many of the five fruits; also rich in lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the stony ground, the climate was mild and the soil fertile: grain ripened twice a year, silk could be raised, orchards flourished, and lacquer trees were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 有草名羊刺，其上生蜜而味甚佳。

translations.literal: There was a grass called "sheep thorn"; on it honey grew and the taste was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: A plant called "sheep thorn" bore a honey-like substance of excellent flavor.

sentences.zh: 引水溉田。

translations.literal: They drew water to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Irrigation channeled water to the fields.

sentences.zh: 出赤鹽，其味甚美。

translations.literal: It produced red salt, the taste very fine.
translations.idiomatic: The region yielded red salt prized for its flavor.

sentences.zh: 復有白鹽，其形如玉，高昌人取以為枕，貢之中國。

translations.literal: There was also white salt, its form like jade; people of Gaochang took it to make pillows and presented them to the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: White salt, translucent as jade, was carved into pillows the Gaochang people sent as tribute to China.

sentences.zh: 多蒲萄酒。

translations.literal: Much grape wine.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was abundant.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，兼信佛法。

translations.literal: Their custom served Heaven gods, and simultaneously believed Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped Heaven while also practicing Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 國中羊馬，牧在隱僻處以避寇，非貴人不知其處。

translations.literal: Sheep and horses of the state were pastured in hidden secluded places to avoid raiders; unless a noble, one did not know the places.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock were hidden in secluded pastures to evade raiders; only the elite knew where they were kept.

sentences.zh: 北有赤石山。

translations.literal: North was Red Stone Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north stood Red Stone Mountain.

sentences.zh: 七十里有貪汗山，[29]夏有積雪，此山北鐵勒界也。

translations.literal: Seventy li away was Greedy Sweat Mountain, [29] snow accumulated in summer; north of this mountain was the Tiele border.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy li distant loomed Greedy Sweat Mountain, [29] snow-clad even in summer; beyond it lay Tiele territory.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，有闞爽者，自為高昌太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizu's time there was Kan Shuang, who on his own served as Prefect of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu a local leader named Kan Shuang installed himself as prefect of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 太延中，遣散騎侍郎王恩生等使高昌，為蠕蠕所執。

translations.literal: In Taiyan, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Wang Ensheng and others were sent as envoys to Gaochang and were seized by the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan era Wei sent Wang Ensheng, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, to Gaochang, but Rouran forces captured the party en route.

sentences.zh: 真君中，爽為沮渠無諱所襲，奪據之。

translations.literal: In Zhenjun, Shuang was raided by Juqu Wuhui and the territory seized.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun era Juqu Wuhui attacked Kan Shuang and took Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 無諱死，弟安周代立，和平元年，為蠕蠕所并。

translations.literal: Wuhui died; younger brother Anzhou replaced him as ruler; in the first year of Heping, they were annexed by the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuhui died his brother Anzhou succeeded, but in the first year of Heping the Rouran absorbed the kingdom entirely.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕以闞伯周為高昌王，其稱王自此始也。

translations.literal: The Rouran made Kan Bozhou King of Gaochang; the title of king from this began.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran enthroned Kan Bozhou as King of Gaochang—the first time the state had a sovereign who bore that title.

sentences.zh: 太和初，伯周死，子義成立，歲餘，為其兄首歸所殺，自立為高昌王。

translations.literal: At the start of Taihe, Bozhou died; son Yicheng succeeded; after a year more he was killed by his elder brother Shougui, who set himself up as King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era Bozhou died and his son Yicheng reigned, but little over a year later his elder brother Shougui murdered him and took the throne as King of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 五年，高車王可至羅殺首歸兄弟，[30]以敦煌人張孟明為王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Gaoche king Kebuolo killed the Shougui brothers, [30] and made Zhang Mengming of Dunhuang king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Gaoche king Kebuolo slew Shougui and his kin [30] and installed Zhang Mengming of Dunhuang as king.

sentences.zh: 後為國人所殺，立馬儒為王，以鞏顧禮、麴嘉為左右長史。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by men of the state; Ma Ru was raised as king, with Gong Guli and Qu Jia as Left and Right Chief Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The locals soon killed Zhang Mengming and made Ma Ru king, appointing Gong Guli and Qu Jia as his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遣司馬王體玄奉表朝貢，請師迎接，求舉國內徙。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Chief Commander Wang Tixuan was sent with a memorial to pay court tribute, requesting army escort, seeking to move the whole state inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Chief Commander Wang Tixuan came with a petition offering tribute and begging Wei to send troops to resettle the entire kingdom within the empire.

sentences.zh: 高祖納之，遣明威將軍韓安保率騎千餘赴之，割伊吾五百里，以儒居之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu accepted; dispatched Bright Might General Han Anbao leading more than a thousand cavalry to go to them; carved out five hundred li of Yiwu for Ru to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu agreed and sent Bright Might General Han Anbao with a thousand cavalry, setting aside five hundred li of Yiwu territory for Ma Ru and his people.

sentences.zh: 至羊榛水，儒遣禮、嘉率步騎一千五百迎安保，去高昌四百里而安保不至。

translations.literal: Reaching Sheep Hazel Water, Ru sent Guli and Jia leading fifteen hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome Anbao; four hundred li from Gaochang, yet Anbao did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Ru reached Sheep Hazel Creek he dispatched Guli and Jia with fifteen hundred troops to meet Han Anbao, but though they marched four hundred li from Gaochang, the Wei force never appeared.

sentences.zh: 禮等還高昌，安保亦還伊吾。

translations.literal: Guli and the others returned to Gaochang; Anbao also returned to Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Guli and his party turned back to Gaochang, and Anbao retreated to Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 安保遣使韓興安等十二人使高昌，儒復遣顧禮將其世子義舒迎安保。

translations.literal: Anbao dispatched the envoy Han Xing'an and twelve others to Gaochang; Ru again sent Guli leading his heir Yishu to welcome Anbao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Anbao then sent twelve envoys led by Han Xing'an to Gaochang, and Ma Ru responded by dispatching Guli with his heir Yishu to greet the relief column once more.

sentences.zh: 至白棘城，去高昌百六十里，而高昌舊人情戀本土，不願東遷，相與殺儒而立麴嘉為王。

translations.literal: Reaching White Thorn City, one hundred sixty li from Gaochang, yet the old residents of Gaochang cherished their native land and did not wish to move east; together they killed Ru and raised Qu Jia as king.
translations.idiomatic: At White Thorn Fort, still one hundred sixty li from Gaochang, the local people—unwilling to abandon their homeland for an eastern resettlement—rose up, killed Ma Ru, and enthroned Qu Jia instead.

sentences.zh: 嘉字靈鳳，金城榆中人。

translations.literal: Jia's style Lingfeng, a man of Yuzhong in Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia, courtesy name Lingfeng, was a native of Yuzhong in Jincheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 既立，又臣于蠕蠕那蓋。

translations.literal: Once established, he again submitted as vassal to the Rouran chieftain Nagai.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, he submitted to the Rouran leader Nagai.

sentences.zh: 顧禮與義舒隨安保至洛陽。

translations.literal: Guli and Yishu followed Anbao to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Guli and Yishu accompanied Han Anbao to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕主伏圖為高車所殺，嘉又臣高車。

translations.literal: When the Rouran lord Futu was killed by the Gaoche, Jia again submitted to the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: After the Rouran chief Futu was killed by the Gaoche, Qu Jia transferred his allegiance to them.

sentences.zh: 初前部胡人悉為高車所徙，入於焉耆，焉耆又為嚈噠所破滅，國人分散，眾不自立，請王於嘉。

translations.literal: At first the Front Division Hu people were all moved by the Gaoche into Yanqi; Yanqi was also destroyed by the Yeda; the state's people scattered; the multitude could not establish themselves and requested a king from Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Gaoche had relocated the Front Cheshi population into Karasahr; when the Hephthalites destroyed Karasahr the people were scattered and leaderless, and they asked Qu Jia to send a king.

sentences.zh: 嘉遣第二子為焉耆王以主之。

translations.literal: Jia dispatched his second son to be King of Yanqi to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia sent his second son to rule Karasahr as its king.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，[31]嘉遣兄子私署左衞將軍、田地太守孝亮朝京師，仍求內徙，乞軍迎援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping, [31] Jia dispatched elder brother's son privately appointed Left Guard General, Prefect of Tiandi, Xiaoliang to pay court at the capital, still requesting internal relocation, begging army escort and aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongping, [31] Qu Jia sent his nephew Xiaoliang—who held the titles Left Guard General and Prefect of Tiandi—to court with another plea for resettlement and a request for military escort.

sentences.zh: 於是遣龍驤將軍孟威發涼州兵三千人迎之，至伊吾，失期而反。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dragon Quelling General Meng Wei was dispatched, mobilizing three thousand Liangzhou troops to welcome them; reaching Yiwu, missing the deadline, they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The court responded by sending Dragon Quelling General Meng Wei with three thousand Liangzhou troops, but he reached only as far as Yiwu before giving up and returning without them.

sentences.zh: 於後十餘遣使，獻珠像、白黑貂裘、名馬、鹽枕等，款誠備至，惟賜優旨，卒不重迎。

translations.literal: Afterward on more than ten occasions envoys were sent, presenting pearl statues, white and black sable furs, famous horses, salt pillows, and the like; sincerity full and complete—only gracious edicts were bestowed; in the end they were not escorted again.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next dozen missions his envoys brought pearl images, sable furs, fine horses, and salt pillows, each delegation more earnest than the last—but the court replied only with kind words and never sent another escort.

sentences.zh: 三年，嘉遣使朝貢，世宗又遣孟威使詔勞之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Jia sent envoys to pay tribute; Emperor Shizong again dispatched Meng Wei as envoy to announce edicts and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Qu Jia sent tribute again, and Emperor Shizong once more sent Meng Wei with imperial commendations.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，以嘉為持節、平西將軍、瓜州刺史、泰臨縣開國伯，私署王如故。

translations.literal: In Yan-chang, Jia was made Bearer of the Staff, Pacifier of the West General, Governor of Guazhou, Baron who Founded the State of Tailin County—private investiture as king as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yan-chang era the court appointed Qu Jia Staff Bearer, Pacifier of the West General, governor of Guazhou, and Baron of Tailin, while allowing him to retain his unofficial royal title.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiping, envoys were sent to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiping era he sent envoys to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿地隔關山，境接荒漠，頻請朝援，徙國內遷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your land is cut off by pass mountains; your border touches the desert wilderness; repeatedly you request court aid to move the state inward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your territory lies beyond the mountain passes, bordering barren desert; you have repeatedly asked for imperial aid in resettling your people inland.

sentences.zh: 雖來誠可嘉，即於理未帖。

translations.literal: Though your coming sincerity is praiseworthy, as to principle it does not fit.
translations.idiomatic: Your earnestness is admirable, but the request itself is not sound policy.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 彼之甿庶，是漢魏遺黎，自晉氏不綱，因難播越，成家立國，世積已久。

translations.literal: Those common people there are remnant people left from Han and Wei; since the Jin house lost governance, through hardship they scattered abroad, formed families and established a state—the generations accumulated long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Your people are descendants of Han and Wei refugees who, after the Jin dynasty fell into disorder, fled hardship and settled there; they have built homes and founded a state over many generations.

sentences.zh: 惡徙重遷，人懷戀舊，今若動之，恐異同之變，爰在肘腋，不得便如來表。」

translations.literal: They hate forced relocation and repeated moves; people cherish attachment to the old lands; if now they are moved, I fear change of discord and accord—it would be upon the elbow and armpit; cannot conveniently grant your memorial as requested."
translations.idiomatic: People resist uprooting and yearn for their old home; forced relocation could spark unrest right at our frontier. We cannot grant your request as written."

sentences.zh: 神龜元年冬，孝亮復表求援內徙，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: In winter of the first year of Shengui, Xiaoliang again memorialized begging aid for inward relocation; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the first year of Shengui, Xiaoliang petitioned again for escort to resettle inland, and the court again refused.

sentences.zh: 正光元年，肅宗遣假員外將軍趙義等使於嘉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengguang, Emperor Suzong sent Acting Irregular Attendant General Zhao Yi and others as envoys to Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengguang, Emperor Suzong dispatched Acting Irregular Attendant General Zhao Yi and others as envoys to Qu Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘉朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: Jia paid court tribute without cessation.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia's tribute missions never ceased.

sentences.zh: 又遣使奉表，自以邊遐，不習典誥，求借五經、諸史，并請國子助教劉變以為博士，[32]肅宗許之。

translations.literal: Again envoys were sent with a memorial; on his own view as border remote, unskilled in canonical edicts, he requested to borrow the Five Classics and various histories, and also requested Imperial University Assistant Instructor Liu Bian to serve as Erudite, [32] Suzong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another embassy explaining that, isolated on the frontier, he lacked familiarity with classical court usage and asked to borrow the Five Classics and standard histories—and also requested Imperial University instructor Liu Bian as a teaching master. [32] Emperor Suzong approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉死，贈鎮西將軍、涼州刺史，子堅立。

translations.literal: Jia died; posthumously gifted Enfeoffed West General, Inspector of Liang Province; son Jian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Jia died the court posthumously granted him the title Enfeoffed West General and inspector of Liang Province; his son Jian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 於後，關中賊亂，使命遂絕。

translations.literal: Afterward, Guanzhong bandits rebelled; envoy missions then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, rebellion swept Guanzhong and communication with the court broke off entirely.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，堅遣使朝貢，除平西將軍、瓜州刺史、泰臨縣伯，王如故，又加衞將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Putai, Jian sent envoys to pay tribute; appointed Pacifier of the West General, Governor of Guazhou, Baron of Tailin County, kingship as before; again added Guardian General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai, Jian resumed tribute missions; the court appointed him Pacifier of the West General, governor of Guazhou, and Baron of Tailin while confirming his royal rank and adding the title Guardian General.

sentences.zh: 至永熙中，特除儀同三司，進為郡公。

translations.literal: Reaching Yongxi, specially appointed Three Excellencies of Identical Rank; advanced to Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he was specially promoted to Three Excellencies of Identical Rank and raised to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 後遂隔絕。

translations.literal: Afterward then cut off in isolation.
translations.idiomatic: Contact with the court was lost after that.

sentences.zh: 鄧至者，白水羌也，世為羌豪，因地名號，自稱鄧至。

translations.literal: Dengzhi—they were White Water Qiang; for generations tribal chieftains of the Qiang; taking the place name as title, they called themselves Dengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Dengzhi were a branch of the White Water Qiang; for generations they had been Qiang chieftains and took their name from their homeland.

sentences.zh: 其地自亭街以東，平武以西，汶嶺以北，宕昌以南。

translations.literal: Their land from Ting Street east, Pingwu west, Wen Ridge north, Dangchang south.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory extended east to Ting Street, west to Pingwu, north to Wen Ridge, and south to Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 土風習俗，亦與宕昌同。

translations.literal: Local custom and practices likewise the same as Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs closely matched those of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 其王像舒治遣使內附，高祖拜龍驤將軍、鄧至王，[33]遣貢不絕。

translations.literal: Their king Xiang Shuzhi sent envoys to submit inward; Emperor Gaozu invested Dragon Quelling General, King of Dengzhi, [33] tribute missions without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Their king Xiang Shuzhi sent envoys to submit; Emperor Gaozu made him Dragon Quelling General and King of Dengzhi, [33] and tribute missions continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 鄧至之西有赫羊等二十國，時遣使朝貢，朝廷皆授以雜號將軍、子男、渠帥之名。

translations.literal: West of Dengzhi were Heyang and twenty other states; from time to time sending envoys to pay tribute; the court all granted miscellaneous-title general, viscount and baron, and chieftain names.
translations.idiomatic: West of Dengzhi lay Heyang and some twenty other states that periodically sent tribute; the court responded by granting them assorted military titles and ranks from viscount to chieftain.

sentences.zh: 蠻之種類，蓋盤瓠之後，其來自久。

translations.literal: The Man tribes—in kind they were descendants of Panhu; their coming from long ago.
translations.idiomatic: The Man peoples were said to be descendants of Panhu and had dwelt in the region since ancient times.

sentences.zh: 習俗叛服，前史具之。

translations.literal: Customs of rebellion and submission—former histories fully record them.
translations.idiomatic: Their pattern of alternating rebellion and submission is fully recorded in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 在江淮之間，依託險阻，部落滋蔓，布於數州，東連壽春，西通上洛，北接汝潁，往往有焉。

translations.literal: Between the Yangzi and Huai they relied on perilous obstacles; tribes spread and flourished, spread over several provinces; east connected Shouchun, west reached Shangluo, north adjoined Ru and Ying—they existed here and there.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yangtze and Huai they exploited rugged terrain; their clans multiplied across several provinces from Shouchun in the east to Shangluo in the west and the Ru and Ying rivers in the north.

sentences.zh: 其於魏氏之時，不甚為患，至晉之末，稍以繁昌，漸為寇暴矣。

translations.literal: In the Wei house's time they were not much a calamity; reaching Jin's end, gradually they grew flourishing, step by step becoming raiding and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei dynasty they had not been a major threat, but by the end of Jin they grew more numerous and began raiding in earnest.

sentences.zh: 自劉石亂後，諸蠻無所忌憚，故其族類，漸得北遷，陸渾以南，滿於山谷，宛洛蕭條，略為丘墟矣。

translations.literal: Since the disorder of the Liu and Shi, the various Man had nothing to fear; therefore their clans gradually were able to move north; south of Luhun, filling the valleys and mountains; Wan and Luo desolate and withered, largely becoming mounds and ruins.
translations.idiomatic: After the chaos of the Liu and Shi dynasties the Man no longer had reason to hold back; they drifted northward until the hills south of Luhun teemed with their settlements, while Wan and Luoyang lay nearly in ruins.

sentences.zh: 太祖既定中山，聲教被于河表。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor had settled Zhongshan, his voice and teaching spread to the lands beyond the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Ancestor conquered Zhongshan, imperial authority reached the lands south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 泰常八年，蠻王梅安率渠帥數千朝京師，求留質子以表忠款。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taichang, Man king Mei'an led several thousand chieftains to pay court at the capital, requesting to leave hostage sons to show loyal sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taichang the Man king Mei'an brought several thousand chieftains to the capital and offered hostages to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 始光中，拜安侍子豹為安遠將軍、江州刺史、順陽公。

translations.literal: In Shiguang, An's attendant son Bao was invested as Pacifier of the Distance General, Inspector of Jiang Province, Duke of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shiguang era the court appointed Mei'an's son Bao—who had served as his attendant—Pacifier of the Distance General, inspector of Jiang Province, and Duke of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 興光中，蠻王文武龍請降，詔褒慰之，拜南雍州刺史、魯陽侯。

translations.literal: In Xingguang, Man king Wenwu Long requested surrender; edict praised and comforted him; invested as Inspector of South Yong Province, Marquis of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Xingguang another Man king, Wenwu Long, submitted; the court praised him and named him inspector of South Yong Province and Marquis of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 延興中，大陽蠻酋桓誕擁沔水以北，滍葉以南八萬餘落，遣使內屬。

translations.literal: In Yanxing, Dayang Man chieftain Huan Dan held north of the Mian River and south of the Zhi and Ye—more than eighty thousand households—sent envoys to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanxing the Dayang chieftain Huan Dan controlled more than eighty thousand households north of the Mian River and south of the Zhi and Ye and sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，拜誕征南將軍、東荊州刺史、襄陽王，聽自選郡縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was pleased; invested Dan as Conqueror of the South General, Inspector of East Jing Province, King of Xiangyang; permitted to choose commanderies and counties himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu welcomed the submission and made Huan Dan Conqueror of the South General, inspector of East Jing Province, and King of Xiangyang, allowing him to choose his own administrative districts.

sentences.zh: 誕字天生，桓玄之子也。

translations.literal: Dan's style Tiansheng; he was the son of Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Dan, courtesy name Tiansheng, was a son of Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 初玄西奔至枚回洲，被殺，誕時年數歲，流竄大陽蠻中，遂習其俗。

translations.literal: At first Xuan fled west to Meihui Isle and was killed; Dan was then several years old; he wandered and hid among the Dayang Man, and thus learned their customs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan fled west to Meihui Isle and was killed, Dan was still a small child and took refuge among the Dayang Man, where he grew up in their ways.

sentences.zh: 及長，多智謀，為羣蠻所歸。

translations.literal: When grown, much wisdom and stratagem; all the Man submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he proved shrewd and capable, and the Man tribes rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 誕既內屬，治於朗陵。

translations.literal: Dan once he had submitted inward, governed at Langling.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to Wei he established his seat at Langling.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，王師南伐，誕請為前驅，乃授使持節、南征西道大都督，討義陽，不果而還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, the royal army marched south to attack; Dan requested to serve as vanguard; thereupon he was granted Bearer of Staff, Great Governor of the South Campaign Western Route; he attacked Yiyang but did not succeed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe, when the imperial army marched south, Dan volunteered as vanguard and was made Bearer of the Staff and supreme commander of the western column; he attacked Yiyang but withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 十年，移居潁陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he moved residence to Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he relocated his seat to Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，依例降王為公。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, according to precedent the king was demoted to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his royal title was reduced to duke per standard practice.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加征南將軍、中道大都督，征竟陵，遇遷洛，師停。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, additionally Conqueror of the South General, Great Governor of the Center Route; campaigned against Jingling; encountering the move of the capital to Luoyang, the army halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was further named Conqueror of the South General and commander of the central column for a campaign against Jingling, but operations halted when the court moved the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是時蕭賾征虜將軍，直閤將軍蠻酋田益宗率部曲四千餘戶內屬。

translations.literal: At this time Xiao Ze's General Who Conquers Captives, Direct Retinue General, Man chieftain Tian Yizong led more than four thousand household dependents to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Liang general Tian Yizong, a Man chieftain serving as Direct Retinue General under Xiao Ze, brought more than four thousand households over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 襄陽酋雷婆思等十一人率戶千餘內徙，求居大和川，詔給廩食。

translations.literal: Xiangyang chieftains Lei Posi and eleven others led more than a thousand households to move inward, requesting to dwell at Dahe River; edict granted grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven Xiangyang chieftains led by Lei Posi brought more than a thousand households inland and asked to settle on the Dahe River; the court granted them grain rations.

sentences.zh: 後開南陽，令有沔北之地。

translations.literal: Later South Yang was opened; he was ordered to hold lands north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court opened South Yang and granted him territory north of the Mian River.

sentences.zh: 蠻人安堵，不為寇賊。

translations.literal: Man people settled peacefully; did not become raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Man lived in peace and no longer raided.

sentences.zh: 十八年，誕入朝，賞遇隆厚。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Dan entered court; rewards and treatment were lofty and generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Huan Dan visited the capital and received lavish honors.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Gang [Resolute].
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous name Gang, "Resolute."

sentences.zh: 子暉，字道進，位龍驤將軍、東荊州刺史，襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Hui, style Daojin; post Dragon Quelling General, Inspector of East Jing Province; inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, courtesy name Daojin, held the posts of Dragon Quelling General and inspector of East Jing Province and inherited his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 景明初，大陽蠻酋田育丘等二萬八千戶內附，詔置四郡十八縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Dayang Man chieftain Tian Yuqiu and others, twenty-eight thousand households, submitted inward; an edict established four commanderies and eighteen counties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era the Dayang Man chieftain Tian Yuqiu and others, twenty-eight thousand households in all, submitted to Wei, and the court established four commanderies and eighteen counties for them.

sentences.zh: 暉卒，贈冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Hui died; posthumously awarded General Who Conquers Champions.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died he was posthumously given the title General Who Conquers Champions.

sentences.zh: 三年，魯陽蠻魯北鷰等聚眾攻逼潁川，詔左衞將軍李崇討平之，徙萬餘家於河北諸州及六鎮。

translations.literal: In the third year, Luyang Man Lu Beiyan and others gathered crowds to attack and press Yingchuan; an edict ordered Left Guard General Li Chong to campaign and pacify them, relocating more than ten thousand households to the northern Yellow River provinces and the Six Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Luyang Man Lu Beiyan and others raised forces and pressed Yingchuan. The court ordered Left Guard General Li Chong to suppress them and moved more than ten thousand households to the northern provinces along the Yellow River and to the Six Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 尋叛南走，所在追討，比及河，殺之皆盡。

translations.literal: Soon they rebelled and fled south; wherever pursued, by the time they reached the river they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: They soon rebelled and fled south, but pursuers caught up with them before they reached the river and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 四年，東荊州蠻樊素安反，僭帝號。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, East Jing Province Man Fan Suan rebelled and usurped an imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the East Jing Man chieftain Fan Suan rebelled and proclaimed himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 正始元年，素安弟秀安復反，李崇、楊大眼悉討平之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenshi, Suan's younger brother Xiuan rebelled again; Li Chong and Yang Dayan completely campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenshi Fan Suan's younger brother Xiuan rebelled again; Li Chong and Yang Dayan put down both revolts completely.

sentences.zh: 二年，蕭衍沔東太守田清喜擁七郡三十一縣，戶萬九千遣使內附，乞師討衍。

translations.literal: In the second year, Xiao Yan's Mian East Prefect Tian Qingxi held seven commanderies and thirty-one counties, ten thousand nine thousand households sent envoys to submit inward, begging troops to campaign against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Xiao Yan's prefect of Mian East, Tian Qingxi, controlled seven commanderies and thirty-one counties with nineteen thousand households. He sent envoys to submit to Wei and asked for troops to attack Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 其雍州以東，石城以西五百餘里水陸援路，請率部曲斷之。

translations.literal: From Yong Province east and Shicheng west, more than five hundred li of land and water supply routes, he requested to lead his command and cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: He offered to lead his followers and cut the land and water supply lines more than five hundred li from east of Yong Province to west of Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，蕭衍永寧太守文雲生六部自漢東遣使歸附。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Xiao Yan's Yongning Prefect Wen Yunsheng, six divisions from Han East, sent envoys to return and submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wen Yunsheng, Xiao Yan's prefect of Yongning, sent envoys from six divisions in Han East to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 永平初，東荊州表囗囗太守桓叔興前後招慰大陽蠻歸附者一萬七百戶，請置郡十六、縣五十，詔前鎮東府長史酈道元檢行置之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping, East Jing Province memorialized [missing title] Prefect Huan Shuxing, who before and after had summoned and comforted Dayang Man submitters, ten thousand seven hundred households, requesting establishment of sixteen commanderies and fifty counties; an edict ordered former Chief Clerk of the Eastern Garrison Headquarters Li Daoyuan to inspect and establish them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongping East Jing Province reported that Prefect Huan Shuxing had won over ten thousand seven hundred Dayang Man households and asked to establish sixteen commanderies and fifty counties. The court ordered Li Daoyuan, former chief clerk of the Eastern Garrison headquarters, to inspect the region and set up the new districts.

sentences.zh: 叔興即暉弟也。

translations.literal: Shuxing was Hui's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxing was Hui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 延昌元年，拜南荊州刺史，居安昌，隸於東荊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanchang, appointed Inspector of South Jing Province, dwelling at Anchang, subordinate to East Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanchang he was appointed inspector of South Jing Province, based at Anchang and subordinate to East Jing Province.
