sentences.zh: 三年，蕭衍遣兵討江沔，破掠諸蠻，百姓擾動。

translations.literal: In the third year, Xiao Yan dispatched troops to campaign against the Jiang and Mian, plundering and raiding the various Man; common people were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xiao Yan sent troops against the Jiang and Mian region, raiding the Man settlements and unsettling the local population.

sentences.zh: 蠻自相督率二萬餘人，頻請統帥為聲勢。

translations.literal: The Man on their own organized and led more than twenty thousand men, repeatedly requesting a commander to serve as their visible strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Man mustered more than twenty thousand men on their own and repeatedly asked for a commander to lend them authority.

sentences.zh: 叔興給一統并威儀，為之節度，蠻人遂安。

translations.literal: Shuxing granted one command together with insignia of authority, directing them on their behalf, and the Man people then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxing gave them a command with full insignia and took charge of them, and the Man were pacified.

sentences.zh: 其年，蕭衍雍州刺史蕭藻遣其將蔡令孫等三將寇南荊之西南，沿襄沔上下，破掠諸蠻。

translations.literal: That year, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Yong Province Xiao Zao dispatched his generals Cai Lingsun and three other commanders to raid the southwest of South Jing, up and down along the Xiang and Mian, plundering the various Man.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Xiao Yan's Inspector of Yong Province, Xiao Zao, sent three commanders led by Cai Lingsun to raid southwestern South Jing along the Xiang and Mian rivers and plunder the Man settlements.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋衍龍驤將軍楚石廉叛衍來請援，叔興與石廉督集蠻夏二萬餘人擊走之，斬令孫等三將。

translations.literal: Man chieftain Yan's Dragon Quelling General Chu Shilian rebelled against Yan and came requesting aid; Shuxing together with Shilian supervised and gathered more than twenty thousand Man and Chinese, drove them off, and beheaded Lingsun and the three other commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Man chieftain Chu Shilian, a Dragon Quelling General under Xiao Yan, defected to Wei and asked for help. Shuxing and Shilian jointly mustered more than twenty thousand Man and Han troops, routed the invaders, and killed Cai Lingsun and the other two commanders.

sentences.zh: 藻又遣其新陽太守邵道林於沔水之南，石城東北立清水戍，為抄掠之基。

translations.literal: Zao again dispatched his Xinyang Prefect Shao Daolin to establish Qingshui garrison south of the Mian River, northeast of Shicheng, as a base for raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zao then sent his prefect of Xinyang, Shao Daolin, to build Qingshui garrison south of the Mian River northeast of Shicheng as a base for raids.

sentences.zh: 叔興遣諸蠻擊破之。

translations.literal: Shuxing dispatched the various Man to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxing sent the Man against the garrison and destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 四年，叔興上表請不隸東荊，許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shuxing submitted a memorial requesting not to be subordinate to East Jing; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Shuxing memorialized asking to be removed from East Jing's jurisdiction, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍每有寇抄，叔興必摧破之。

translations.literal: Whenever Xiao Yan had raiding incursions, Shuxing invariably crushed and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiao Yan launched raids, Shuxing invariably broke them up.

sentences.zh: 正光中，叔興擁所部南叛。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang, Shuxing led his command south in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengguang his relative Shuxing led their followers south in revolt.

sentences.zh: 蠻首成龍強率戶數千內附，拜為刺史。

translations.literal: Man chieftain Cheng Longqiang led several thousand households to submit inward; invested as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The Man chieftain Cheng Longqiang brought several thousand households over and was appointed inspector.

sentences.zh: 蠻帥田午生率戶二千內徙揚州，拜為郡守。

translations.literal: Man commander Tian Wusheng led two thousand households to move inward to Yang Province; invested as commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Man leader Tian Wusheng resettled two thousand households in Yang Province and was made a commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍義州刺史、邊城王文僧明，鐵騎將軍、邊城太守田官德等率戶萬餘舉州內屬，拜僧明平南將軍、西豫州刺史，封開封侯；

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Yi Province, Bian-cheng Wang Wensengming; Iron Cavalry General, Bian-cheng Prefect Tian Guande and others led more than ten thousand households, raising the province to submit inward; invested Sengming as Pacifier of the South General, Inspector of West Yu Province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Kaifeng;
translations.idiomatic: Wensengming, king of Bian-cheng and inspector of Yi under Xiao Yan, and Tian Guande, Iron Cavalry General and prefect of Bian-cheng, led more than ten thousand households and surrendered their whole province; Wensengming was made Pacifier of the South General and inspector of West Yu Province and enfeoffed as Marquis of Kaifeng;

sentences.zh: 官德龍驤將軍、義州刺史；

translations.literal: Guande Dragon Quelling General, Inspector of Yi Province;
translations.idiomatic: Guande was named Dragon Quelling General and inspector of Yi Province;

sentences.zh: 自餘封授各有差。

translations.literal: The remaining grants and appointments each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: The others received titles and posts of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 僧明、官德並入朝，蠻出山至邊城、建安者八九千戶。

translations.literal: Sengming and Guande both entered court; Man coming out of the mountains to Bian-cheng and Jian'an numbered eight or nine thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wensengming and Guande both came to court, while eight or nine thousand Man households emerged from the hills to settle at Bian-cheng and Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 義州尋為蕭衍將裴邃所陷。

translations.literal: Yi Province soon was overrun by Xiao Yan's general Pei Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province was soon recaptured by Xiao Yan's general Pei Sui.

sentences.zh: 衍定州刺史田超秀亦遣使求附，請援歷年，朝廷恐輕致邊役，未之許。

translations.literal: Yan's Inspector of Ding Province Tian Chaoxiu also sent envoys requesting attachment; begging aid for years; the court feared lightly causing border campaigns; did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chaoxiu, Xiao Yan's inspector of Ding Province, also sent envoys offering submission and pleading for support year after year, but the court worried about triggering border warfare and refused.

sentences.zh: 會超秀死，其部曲相率內附，徙之六鎮、秦隴，所在反叛。

translations.literal: Meeting Chaoxiu's death, his command followers together submitted inward; they were relocated to the Six Garrisons, Qin and Long; everywhere they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoxiu died his followers surrendered en masse and were resettled in the Six Garrisons and the Qin-Long region, where they rose in rebellion wherever they were sent.

sentences.zh: 二荊、西郢，蠻大擾動，斷三鵶路，殺都督，寇盜至於襄城、汝水，百姓多被其害。

translations.literal: East and West Jing, West Ying—Man greatly disturbed and moved; cut the Three Geese Road; killed governors; raiding bandits reached Xiangcheng and the Ru River; common people largely suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: In East and West Jing and West Ying the Man rose on a vast scale, severed the Three Geese Road, killed frontier commanders, and raided as far as Xiangcheng and the Ru River, inflicting great harm on the populace.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將圍廣陵，樊城諸蠻並為前驅，[37]自汝水以南，處處鈔劫，恣其暴掠。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan dispatched generals to besiege Guangling; various Man of Fancheng all served as vanguard, [37] from south of the Ru River, everywhere raiding and plundering, indulging their violent seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent troops to besiege Guangling with the Fancheng Man as their vanguard; [37] from the Ru River southward they plundered at will.

sentences.zh: 連年攻討，散而復合，其暴滋甚。

translations.literal: Year after year attacking and subduing, scattered yet again gathering; their violence grew ever more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the court campaigned against them, but they dispersed and regrouped, and their predations only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 又有冉氏、向氏者，陬落尤盛，餘則大者萬家，小者千戶，更相崇僭，稱王侯，屯據三峽，斷遏水路，荊、蜀行人至有假道者。

translations.literal: Further there were the Ran clan and Xiang clan—settlement clusters especially flourishing; the rest then large ones ten thousand households, small ones a thousand households; each in turn exalting presumption, calling themselves kings and marquises; encamped and holding the Three Gorges; cutting and blocking the water roads; travelers of Jing and Shu even had to borrow passage routes.
translations.idiomatic: The Ran and Xiang clans were especially powerful; other groups ranged from ten thousand households down to a thousand, each lorded over by self-styled kings and marquises who held the Three Gorges and choked off river traffic, forcing travelers between Jing and Shu to seek alternate routes.

sentences.zh: 獠者，蓋南蠻之別種，自漢中達于卭笮川洞之間，所在皆有。

translations.literal: The Liao—in kind they were a separate branch of the Southern Man; from Hanzhong reaching to the caves and ravines between Qiong and Ze; everywhere they existed.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao were a southern offshoot of the Man, found everywhere from Hanzhong to the Qiong-Ze river country.

sentences.zh: 種類甚多，散居山谷，略無氏族之別。

translations.literal: Their kinds were very numerous; scattered dwelling in valleys and mountains; largely without clan and surname distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Their clans were many and scattered through the hills with little sense of lineage or surname.

sentences.zh: 又無名字，所生男女，唯以長幼次第呼之。

translations.literal: Also without names; born males and females were only called by the sequence of elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: They had no personal names at all; children were addressed simply by birth order.

sentences.zh: 其丈夫稱阿謩、阿段，婦人阿夷、阿等之類，皆語之次第稱謂也。

translations.literal: Their husbands were called A-mo, A-duan; women A-yi, A-deng and the like—all language of sequential address.
translations.idiomatic: Men might be called A-mo or A-duan, women A-yi or A-deng—terms that simply marked order of birth.

sentences.zh: 依樹積木，以居其上，名曰「干蘭」，干蘭大小，隨其家口之數。

translations.literal: Relying on trees they piled timber to dwell above—called "gan lan" [tree house]; gan lan size followed the number of mouths in the household.
translations.idiomatic: They built stilt houses from timber erected against trees—these "gan lan" varied in size according to family size.

sentences.zh: 往往推一長者為王，亦不能遠相統攝。

translations.literal: Often they promoted one elder as king; yet could not govern and control from afar.
translations.idiomatic: They sometimes recognized an elder as king, but no one could rule effectively over distant groups.

sentences.zh: 父死則子繼，若中國之貴族也。

translations.literal: Father died then son succeeded—as Chinese noble houses.
translations.idiomatic: Succession passed from father to son much like Chinese aristocratic families.

sentences.zh: 獠王各有鼓角一雙，使其子弟自吹擊之。

translations.literal: Each Liao king had one pair of drum and horn; he had his young sons blow and strike them themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Each Liao chieftain kept a drum and horn pair for his sons to play.

sentences.zh: 好相殺害，多不敢遠行。

translations.literal: They liked mutual killing; mostly dared not travel far.
translations.idiomatic: They were prone to feuding and rarely ventured far from home.

sentences.zh: 能臥水底，持刀刺魚。

translations.literal: Able to lie beneath water, holding knife to stab fish.
translations.idiomatic: They could swim underwater and spear fish with a blade.

sentences.zh: 其口嚼食並鼻飲。

translations.literal: Their mouths chewed food and also nose drank.
translations.idiomatic: They ate with their mouths and drank through their noses.

sentences.zh: 死者豎棺而埋之。

translations.literal: The dead—coffin upright, then buried.
translations.idiomatic: They buried the dead in upright coffins.

sentences.zh: 性同禽獸，至於忿怒，父子不相避，惟手有兵刃者先殺之。

translations.literal: Nature same as birds and beasts—when it came to wrath, father and son did not avoid each other; whoever had weapon in hand first killed.
translations.idiomatic: Their tempers were savage; in rage a father and son would not hold back, and whoever held a weapon struck first.

sentences.zh: 若殺其父，走避，[40]求得一狗以謝其母，母得狗謝，不復嫌恨。

translations.literal: If one killed his father, he fled and hid, [40] sought to obtain one dog to apologize to his mother; mother receiving the dog apology no longer bore hatred.
translations.idiomatic: A parricide would flee, [40] then offer a dog to appease his mother; once she accepted the dog, her anger ceased.

sentences.zh: 若報怨相攻擊，必殺而食之。

translations.literal: If settling grudges and mutually attacking, they must kill and eat.
translations.idiomatic: When feuding they killed enemies and ate the flesh.

sentences.zh: 平常劫掠，賣取猪狗而已。

translations.literal: In ordinary raiding, they sold for pigs and dogs, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary raids yielded little beyond pigs and dogs for sale.

sentences.zh: 親戚比隣，指授相賣，被賣者號哭不服，逃竄避之，乃將買人捕逐，指若亡叛，獲便縛之。

translations.literal: Relatives and neighboring settlements pointed out and sold one another; the sold one wailed and would not submit, fled and hid to avoid; then they brought the buyers to pursue and catch—as if a fugitive rebel, once caught they were bound.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and neighbors sold one another into bondage; captives wept and fled, but buyers hunted them down like runaway fugitives and bound them on capture.

sentences.zh: 但經被縛者，即服為賤隸，不敢稱良矣。

translations.literal: Once one had been bound, he submitted and became base slave; did not dare to call himself good free person.
translations.idiomatic: Once bound, a captive accepted servile status and no longer claimed to be free.

sentences.zh: 亡失兒女，一哭便止，不復追思。

translations.literal: Losing sons and daughters—one cry then stopped; no further remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: When children were lost they cried once and then ceased to mourn them.

sentences.zh: 惟執盾持矛，不識弓矢。

translations.literal: Only holding shield and grasping spear—they did not know bow and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: They fought with shields and spears but did not use bows.

sentences.zh: 用竹為簧，羣聚鼓之，以為音節。

translations.literal: Using bamboo for reeds, they gathered in groups to drum them, taking this as rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: They made bamboo reed pipes and drummed them together for music.

sentences.zh: 能為細布，色至鮮凈。

translations.literal: Able to weave fine cloth; colors very bright and clean.
translations.idiomatic: They wove fine cloth of vivid, immaculate color.

sentences.zh: 大狗一頭，買一生口。

translations.literal: One large dog—buys one living mouth [slave].
translations.idiomatic: A large dog could buy one captive.

sentences.zh: 其俗畏鬼神，尤尚淫祀。

translations.literal: Their custom feared ghosts and spirits; especially esteemed excessive sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: They feared spirits and practiced elaborate, often immoderate rites.

sentences.zh: 所殺之人，美鬢髯者必剝其面皮，籠之於竹，及燥，號之曰「鬼」，鼓舞祀之，以求福利。

translations.literal: People they killed—those with beautiful beard and whiskers must have their face skin peeled, caged in bamboo; when dry, called "ghost"; dancing and drumming to sacrifice them, seeking blessing and profit.
translations.idiomatic: They flayed the faces of bearded victims, dried them in bamboo cages, called them "ghosts," and danced before them seeking good fortune.

sentences.zh: 至有賣其昆季妻奴盡者，乃自賣以供祭焉。

translations.literal: Reaching the point of selling brothers and sisters, wives and slaves entirely; then selling oneself to provide sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Some sold siblings, wives, and slaves and even themselves to fund sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 鑄銅為器，大口寬腹，名曰銅爨，既薄且輕，易於熟食。

translations.literal: Casting copper as vessels—large mouth, broad belly—called "tong cuan" [copper cauldron]; both thin and light; easy to cook food quickly.
translations.idiomatic: They cast thin, light copper cauldrons with wide mouths and bellies, ideal for quick cooking.

sentences.zh: 建國中，李勢在蜀，諸獠始出巴西、渠川、廣漢、陽安、資中，攻破郡縣，為益州大患。

translations.literal: During Jianguo, Li Shi was in Shu; various Liao first emerged from Baxi, Quchuan, Guanghan, Yang'an, Zizhong; broke commanderies and counties; became a great calamity of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianguo era, while Li Shi held Shu, Liao bands from Baxi, Quchuan, Guanghan, Yang'an, and Zizhong overran commanderies and counties and became a major scourge in Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 勢內外受敵，所以亡也。

translations.literal: Shi received enemies within and without; therefore perished.
translations.idiomatic: Beset by enemies at home and abroad, Li Shi fell—which is why his state collapsed.

sentences.zh: 自桓溫破蜀之後，力不能制，又蜀人東流，山險之地多空，獠遂挾山傍谷。

translations.literal: Since Huan Wen broke Shu afterward, strength could not control them; moreover Shu people flowed east; perilous mountain places mostly empty; Liao then clung to mountains beside valleys.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen conquered Shu the court lacked the strength to control them; as Sichuan refugees drifted east, mountain valleys emptied and the Liao settled along the ridges.

sentences.zh: 與夏人參居者頗輸租賦，在深山者仍不為編戶。

translations.literal: Those mingling and dwelling with Xia people largely paid rent and taxes; those in deep mountains still were not registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Liao living among Chinese subjects often paid taxes, while those deep in the mountains remained outside the household registers.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍梁益二州歲歲伐獠以自裨潤，公私頗藉為利。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Liang and Yi two provinces year after year attacked Liao for self-supplement and profit; public and private largely relied on this as profit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Yan the Liang and Yi provinces raided the Liao annually for plunder, and both officials and private parties profited from it.

sentences.zh: 正始中，夏侯道遷舉漢中內附，世宗遣尚書邢巒為梁益二州刺史以鎮之，近夏人者安堵樂業，在山谷者不敢為寇。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, Xiahou Daqian raised Hanzhong to submit inward; Shizong dispatched Minister Xing Luan as Inspector of Liang and Yi provinces to garrison them; those near Xia people settled peacefully and took joy in their work; those in valleys and mountains dared not become raiders.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi Xiahou Daqian brought Hanzhong over to Wei; Emperor Shizong sent Minister Xing Luan to govern Liang and Yi, and while Liao near Chinese settlements lived peacefully, those in the hills ceased raiding.

sentences.zh: 後以羊祉為梁州，傅豎眼為益州。

translations.literal: Later Yang Zhi was made Liang Province, Fu Shuyan Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Zhi was appointed to Liang Province and Fu Shuyan to Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 祉性酷虐，不得物情。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was cruel and tyrannical; did not obtain the sentiment of things/people.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi was cruel and won no sympathy from the people.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍輔國將軍范季旭與獠王趙清荊率眾屯孝子谷，祉遣統軍魏胡擊走之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Assistant State General Fan Jixu and Liao king Zhao Qingjing led the masses to encamp at Xiaozi Valley; Zhi dispatched Commanding General Wei Hu to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jixu, Xiao Yan's Assistant State General, and the Liao king Zhao Qingjing camped at Xiaozi Valley until Yang Zhi sent Commander Wei Hu to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 後蕭衍寧朔將軍姜白復擁夷獠入屯南城，梁州人王法慶與之通謀，眾屯於固門川，祉遣征虜將軍囗囗討破之。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Yan's Pacifier of the North General Jiang Bai again led Yi Liao to enter and encamp at South City; Liang Province man Wang Faqing conspired with them; masses encamped at Gumen River; Zhi dispatched General Who Conquers Captives [name lost in text] to campaign and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiang Bai, Xiao Yan's Pacifier of the North General, again led Yi and Liao forces to South City, where they conspired with Liangzhou native Wang Faqing and encamped at Gumen River; Yang Zhi sent General Who Conquers Captives [name lost in text] to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 豎眼施恩布信，大得獠和。

translations.literal: Shuyan distributed grace and spread trust; greatly obtained Liao harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan won the Liao over through kindness and good faith.

sentences.zh: 後以元法僧代傅豎眼為益州，法僧在任貪殘，獠遂反叛，勾引蕭衍軍圍逼晉壽。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Faseng replaced Fu Shuyan as Yi Province; Faseng in office was greedy and cruel; Liao then rebelled; enticed Xiao Yan's army to surround and press Jingshou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Faseng replaced Fu Shuyan in Yi Province; his greed and cruelty provoked Liao rebellion and brought Xiao Yan's forces to besiege Jingshou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂之，以豎眼先得物情，復令乘傳往撫。

translations.literal: The court was worried; because Shuyan had first obtained the sentiment of things, again ordered him to ride post relay to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the court turned again to Fu Shuyan—who had already won local trust—and sent him posthaste to restore order.

sentences.zh: 獠聞豎眼至，莫不欣然，拜迎道路，於是而定。

translations.literal: The Liao heard Shuyan had arrived; none were not pleased; bowing and welcoming along the roads; thus order was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Fu Shuyan was coming, the Liao turned out in joy to greet him along the roads, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 及元恒、元子真相繼為梁州，並無德績，諸獠苦之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Heng and Yuan Zizhen in succession became Liang Province, both without virtue or achievement; the various Liao suffered under them.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Heng and Yuan Zizhen served in turn as governor of Liang Province, both without merit or virtue, the Liao endured their rule with hardship.

sentences.zh: 其後朝廷以梁益二州控攝險遠，乃立巴州以統諸獠，後以巴酋嚴始欣為刺史。

translations.literal: Afterward the court, because Liang and Yi two provinces controlled and held perilous remote [lands], then established Ba Prefecture to govern the various Liao; later made Ba chieftain Yan Shixin inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court then created Ba Prefecture to govern the Liao, finding Liang and Yi too distant and rugged to control directly, and later appointed the Ba chieftain Yan Shixin as its inspector.

sentences.zh: 又立隆城鎮，所綰獠二十萬戶，彼謂北獠，歲輸租布，又與外人交通貿易。

translations.literal: Also established Longcheng garrison, governing Liao of two hundred thousand households; those there call them Northern Liao; yearly paying rent and cloth; also trading with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison was also set up at Longcheng over two hundred thousand Liao households—the so-called Northern Liao—who paid annual taxes in cloth and traded with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 巴州生獠並皆不順，其諸頭王每於時節謁見刺史而已。

translations.literal: Ba Prefecture raw Liao were all not compliant; their various head-kings only at seasons and festivals paid court calls to the inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The unassimilated Liao of Ba Prefecture remained restive; their chieftains paid the inspector only seasonal courtesy visits.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，諸獠以始欣貪暴，相率反叛，攻圍巴州。

translations.literal: Early Xiaochang, the various Liao because Shixin was greedy and violent, together rose in rebellion, attacked and besieged Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era the Liao rose together against Yan Shixin's greed and cruelty and besieged Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 山南行臺勉諭，即時散罷。

translations.literal: The Southern Mountain Circuit Intendant admonished and instructed, [41] immediately dispersed and disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Mountain circuit intendant counseled them, [41] and the rebels dispersed at once.

sentences.zh: 自是獠諸頭王相率詣行臺者相繼，子建厚勞賚之。

translations.literal: From this the Liao various head-kings in succession came to the circuit intendant one after another; Zijian generously rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Liao chieftains came in steady succession to the circuit intendant, and Zijian rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 始欣見中國多事，又失彼心，慮獲罪譴。

translations.literal: Shixin saw China had many troubles, also lost their hearts, feared receiving punishment and reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin saw the realm in turmoil, knew he had lost the people's trust, and feared imperial punishment.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍南梁州刺史陰子春扇惑邊陲，始欣謀將南叛。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan's Southern Liang Province Inspector Yin Zichun incited the borderlands; Shixin plotted to rebel southward.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zichun, Xiao Yan's inspector of Southern Liang, was stirring the frontier, and Shixin plotted to defect south.

sentences.zh: 始欣族子愷時為隆城鎮將，密知之，嚴設邏候，遂禽蕭衍使人，并封始欣詔書、鐵券、刀劍、衣冠之屬，表送行臺。

translations.literal: Shixin's clansman son Kai then was Longcheng garrison general; secretly knew it; strictly set patrol guards; then captured Xiao Yan's envoy, together sealed Shixin's edicts, iron bonds, swords, robes and caps and the like, memorial sent to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, Shixin's kinsman and commander at Longcheng, learned of the plot in secret, tightened patrols, seized Xiao Yan's envoy, and sent the court a sealed packet of Shixin's edicts, iron bonds, arms, and regalia.

sentences.zh: 子建乃啟以鎮為南梁州，愷為刺史，發使執始欣，囚於南鄭。

translations.literal: Zijian then memorialized to make the garrison Southern Liang Province, Kai as inspector, dispatched envoys to seize Shixin, imprisoned at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian petitioned to elevate the garrison to Southern Liang Province with Kai as governor, then sent men to seize Shixin and hold him at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 遇子建見代，梁州刺史傅豎眼仍為行臺。

translations.literal: Encountering Zijian being replaced, Liang Province Inspector Fu Shuyan still became circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijian was replaced, Fu Shuyan of Liang Province took over as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 豎眼久病，其子敬紹納始欣重賂，使得還州。

translations.literal: Shuyan long ill; his son Jingshao received Shixin's heavy bribes, enabled him to return to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan had been ill for some time; his son Jingshao accepted heavy bribes from Shixin and secured his release back to office.

sentences.zh: 始欣乃起眾攻愷，屠滅之，據城南叛，蕭衍將蕭玩率眾援接。

translations.literal: Shixin then raised masses to attack Kai, slaughtered and destroyed him, held the city and rebelled south; Xiao Yan's general Xiao Wan led masses to assist and receive.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin raised troops, slaughtered Kai, seized the city, and defected south; Xiao Yan's general Xiao Wan marched to his aid.

sentences.zh: 時梁益二州並遣將討之，攻陷巴州，執始欣，遂大破玩軍。

translations.literal: At the time Liang and Yi two provinces both dispatched generals to attack them, captured Ba Prefecture, seized Shixin, then greatly broke Wan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from Liang and Yi provinces then marched against them, retook Ba Prefecture, captured Shixin, and routed Xiao Wan's army.

sentences.zh: 及斬玩，以傅曇表為刺史。

translations.literal: When Wan was beheaded, made Fu Tanbiao inspector.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Wan was executed, Fu Tanbiao was appointed inspector.

sentences.zh: 後元羅在梁州，為所陷，自此遂絕。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Luo was in Liang Province, was trapped by them, [42] from this then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yuan Luo governed Liang Province, he was brought down by them, [42] and the account ends here.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：氐、羌、蠻、獠，風俗各異，嗜欲不同，言語不通，聖人因時設教，所以達其志而通其俗也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Di, Qiang, Man, Liao—customs each different; appetites and desires not the same; speech not mutually understood; the sage according to the times established teaching, thereby to reach their aims and connect with their customs.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Di, Qiang, Man, and Liao each had distinct customs, desires, and languages; the sage ruler adapts instruction to the times so that their aims may be understood and their ways accommodated.

sentences.zh: 然而外寧必有內憂，覽之者不可不誡慎也。

translations.literal: Yet external peace necessarily has internal worry; those who read this cannot fail to be warned and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet outward calm always harbors inner peril—readers must take this as a warning.

sentences.zh: 魏書卷一百一 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，卷末有宋人校語

translations.literal: Book of Wei, juan 101 — in various editions' tables of contents this fascicle is marked "lacuna"; at the fascicle's end there are collation notes by Song scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei, juan 101: various editions mark this fascicle "lacuna" in their tables of contents, and Song-dynasty collation notes appear at its end.

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Entered into Textual Verification in the Palace Edition〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Palace Edition, entered into textual verification〉

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書列傳第八十九亡，史臣論蓋略北史。」

translations.literal: It states: "Wei Shou's book, Biography 89, is lost; the historian's appraisal was largely taken from the History of the Northern Dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: It states, "Wei Shou's original Biography 89 is lost; the historian's appraisal was largely drawn from the History of the Northern Dynasties."

sentences.zh: 錢氏考異卷二八氐傳條據此篇用東晉年號，不斥晉帝姓名，以為「蓋非魏收書之舊」。

translations.literal: Qian's Kaoyi juan 28, Di biography entry, on the basis that this piece uses Eastern Jin era names and does not name Jin emperors, holds that "it is likely not Wei Shou's book's original."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin, Kaoyi juan 28, Di biography entry, notes that because this text uses Eastern Jin era names without naming Jin emperors, it is "likely not Wei Shou's original."

sentences.zh: 其實此卷諸傳都以北史相同諸傳補而刪去魏以後事。

translations.literal: In fact this fascicle's various biographies were all supplemented from the corresponding biographies in the History of the Northern Dynasties, deleting matters after Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In fact every biography in this fascicle was patched from the corresponding Northern Dynasties accounts, with post-Wei material removed.

sentences.zh: 騰勇健多計略 按宋書卷九八氐胡傳「騰」下有「子駒」二字。

translations.literal: Teng was brave and strong with many stratagems. Note: Song shu juan 98, Di and Hu biography, below "Teng" has the two characters "zi Ju."
translations.idiomatic: Teng was brave and resourceful. Note: Song shu juan 98, Di and Hu biography, reads "zi Ju" after "Teng."

sentences.zh: 徙居仇池者始於駒，周書卷四九氐傳、通典卷一八九氐條同，這裏「騰」下當脫「子駒」二字。

translations.literal: Those who moved to dwell at Chouchi began with Ju; Zhou shu juan 49 Di biography, Tongdian juan 189 Di entry agree; here below "Teng" the two characters "zi Ju" must be missing.
translations.idiomatic: Settlement at Chouchi began with Ju; Zhou shu juan 49 and Tongdian juan 189 agree. Here "zi Ju" is missing after "Teng."

sentences.zh: 國子安叛苻生殺俊復稱藩於晉安死子世自立為仇池公 冊府卷九六六

translations.literal: Guo, son An, rebelled against Fu Sheng, killed Jun, again declared vassalage to Jin; An died, son Shi self-established as Duke of Chouchi. Cefu juan 966
translations.idiomatic: Guo's son An rebelled against Fu Sheng, killed Jun, and renewed vassalage to Jin; when An died, son Shi declared himself Duke of Chouchi. Cefu juan 966

sentences.zh: 〈一一三六一頁〉
「叛」作「奢」，「安死」作「及死」。

translations.literal: "Rebel" reads "she"; "An died" reads "ji si."
translations.idiomatic: "Rebel" appears as "she"; "An died" appears as "when he died."

sentences.zh: 按宋書卷九八作「安奔苻生，俊遣使歸藩。

translations.literal: Note: Song shu juan 98 reads "An fled to Fu Sheng; Jun dispatched envoys to return to vassalage.
translations.idiomatic: Song shu juan 98 reads, "An fled to Fu Sheng; Jun sent envoys to renew vassalage.

sentences.zh: 〈中略〉

translations.literal: 〈middle omitted〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈omitted〉

sentences.zh: 俊卒，子世立」。

translations.literal: Jun died; son Shi succeeded."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun died, son Shi succeeded."

sentences.zh: 考楊安在苻堅時屢任將帥，見晉書卷一一三苻堅載記。

translations.literal: Examining: Yang An during Fu Jian's time repeatedly held general and commander posts; see Jin shu juan 113, Annals of Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang An repeatedly held command under Fu Jian; see Jin shu juan 113, Annals of Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 並無「叛」苻生，歸晉之事。

translations.literal: Entirely without "rebelled" against Fu Sheng, returned to Jin matters.
translations.idiomatic: There is no record of his "rebel" against Fu Sheng or of returning to Jin.

sentences.zh: 且此傳先沒有說他歸苻生，何以忽言其「叛」？

translations.literal: Moreover this biography earlier never said he submitted to Fu Sheng; why suddenly speak of his "rebellion"?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the biography never said he had submitted to Fu Sheng—why suddenly call it a "rebellion"?

sentences.zh: 知這裏「叛」乃「奔」之訛，冊府已訛「奢」，尚存痕跡，當是後人以不可解，妄改為「叛」。

translations.literal: Know that here "rebel" is the error for "flee"; Cefu already erred "she," still preserving traces; it must be that later people, finding it incomprehensible, rashly changed it to "rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Here "rebel" is a corruption of "flee"; Cefu's "she" still preserves the trace. Later copyists, finding the passage unintelligible, wrongly emended it to "rebel."

sentences.zh: 楊俊也非為安所殺，世乃俊子。

translations.literal: Yang Jun also was not killed by An; Shi was Jun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun was not killed by An; Shi was Jun's son.

sentences.zh: 「殺」字當涉上「殺國自立」而衍。

translations.literal: The character "kill" must have been extended from the above "killed the state and self-established."
translations.idiomatic: The word "killed" was likely interpolated from the earlier phrase "killed the ruler and seized power."

sentences.zh: 「安死」本作「及死」，承上文指俊死，冊府不誤。

translations.literal: "An died" originally read "when he died," continuing the above referring to Jun's death; Cefu is not in error.
translations.idiomatic: "An died" originally read "when he died," referring to Jun's death above; Cefu is correct.

sentences.zh: 原文當作「國子安奔苻生，俊復稱藩於晉，及死，子世自立為仇池公」。

translations.literal: The original text should read "Guo's son An fled to Fu Sheng; Jun again declared vassalage to Jin; when he died, son Shi self-established as Duke of Chouchi."
translations.idiomatic: The original should read: "Guo's son An fled to Fu Sheng; Jun renewed vassalage to Jin; when he died, son Shi declared himself Duke of Chouchi."

sentences.zh: 與宋書合。

translations.literal: Agrees with Song shu.
translations.idiomatic: This agrees with the Song shu.

sentences.zh: 遣使詣簡文帝 冊府

translations.literal: Dispatched envoys to call on Emperor Jianwen. Cefu
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to call on Emperor Jianwen. Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same fascicle and page as above〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same volume and page〉

sentences.zh: 「詣」下有「闕」字，按文理當有此字。

translations.literal: Below "call on" there is the character "lacuna"; according to the sense there should be this character.
translations.idiomatic: After "call on" the text marks a lacuna; context requires a word there.

sentences.zh: 「簡文帝」三字屬下讀。

translations.literal: The three characters "Emperor Jianwen" belong to the reading below.
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Jianwen" belongs with the following clause.

sentences.zh: 通志卷一九五氐傳「闕」字作「建康」，當是鄭樵所見本已脫此字，以意增。

translations.literal: Tongzhi juan 195 Di biography reads the "lacuna" character as "Jiankang"; it must be that the edition Zheng Qiao saw had already lost this character and he added it by conjecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi juan 195, Di biography, supplies "Jiankang" for the lacuna—Zheng Qiao's edition had already lost the word and he supplied it by conjecture.

sentences.zh: 堅以女妻佛奴子定 諸本脫「女」字，今據北史卷九六、冊府

translations.literal: Jian gave his daughter in marriage to Fonu's son Ding. Various editions omit the character "daughter"; now according to Bei shi juan 96, Cefu
translations.idiomatic: Jian gave his daughter in marriage to Fonu's son Ding. Various editions omit "daughter"; restored per Bei shi juan 96 and Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same fascicle and page as above〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same volume and page〉

sentences.zh: 及宋書卷九八補。

translations.literal: And Song shu juan 98 supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: and Song shu juan 98.

sentences.zh: 登國四年 按宋書卷九八事在太元十五年

translations.literal: Dengguo, year 4. Note: Song shu juan 98 places the event in Taiyuan, year 15
translations.idiomatic: Dengguo, year 4. Note: Song shu juan 98 places the event in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan

sentences.zh: 當魏登國五年，「四」字應作「五」。

translations.literal: should be Wei Dengguo, year 5; the character "four" should read "five."
translations.idiomatic: —corresponding to Wei Dengguo year 5; "four" should read "five."

sentences.zh: 玄字黃眉 諸本及北史卷九六「字」作「子」。

translations.literal: Xuan, style name Huangmei. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 read "style name" as "son."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Huangmei. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 mistakenly read "styled" as "son."

sentences.zh: 宋書卷九八、通志卷一九五作「字」。

translations.literal: Song shu juan 98, Tongzhi juan 195 read "style name."
translations.idiomatic: Song shu juan 98 and Tongzhi juan 195 read "style name."

sentences.zh: 按下文所敍均玄事，不及「黃眉」，知作「字」是，今據改。

translations.literal: Examining the narrative below, all are Xuan's affairs, not reaching "Huangmei"; know that reading "style name" is correct; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative below concerns Xuan alone, not Huangmei; "style name" is correct and is adopted here.

sentences.zh: 仍奉晉義熙之號 諸本及北史卷九六「義熙」作「永熙」，晉無此年號，今據宋書卷九八改。

translations.literal: Still upheld Jin's Yixi era name. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 read "Yixi" as "Yongxi"; Jin had no such era name; now changed according to Song shu juan 98.
translations.idiomatic: Still upheld Jin's Yixi era name. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 read "Yongxi," but Jin had no such era; emended per Song shu juan 98.

sentences.zh: 鎮石昌 宋書卷九八「石」作「宕」。

translations.literal: Garrisoned Shichang. Song shu juan 98 reads "shi" as "dang."
translations.idiomatic: Garrisoned Shichang. Song shu juan 98 reads "Shi" as "Dang."

sentences.zh: 按「石昌」不見他處，但宕昌乃羌族居地，自有王，下宕昌傳也沒有說曾為楊氏占領，亦可疑，今仍之。

translations.literal: Note: "Shichang" is not seen elsewhere; but Dangchang was Qiang people's dwelling land, having its own king; the Dangchang biography below also does not say it was ever occupied by the Yang clan—also doubtful; now retained as is.
translations.idiomatic: "Shichang" appears nowhere else; Dangchang was Qiang territory with its own king, and the Dangchang biography does not record Yang occupation—doubtful, but the text is retained.

sentences.zh: 獲雍州流人七千餘家還于仇池 諸本及北史卷九六「雍」作「維」，當時無此州名。

translations.literal: Captured Yong Province displaced people of more than seven thousand households, returned them to Chouchi. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 read "Yong" as "Wei"; at the time there was no such province name.
translations.idiomatic: Captured more than seven thousand refugee households from Yong Province and resettled them at Chouchi. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 read "Yong" as "Wei," but no such province existed.

sentences.zh: 按卷四上世祖紀上延和三年正月記「楊難當克漢中，送雍州流民七千家於長安」，即此掠獲之戶，「維」乃「雍」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Note: Juan 4, Part 1, Annals of Shizu, Part 1, Yanhe year 3, first month records "Yang Nandang captured Hanzhong, sent Yong Province displaced people of seven thousand households to Chang'an"—these are the seized households; "Wei" is the error for "Yong"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Annals of Shizu, Yanhe year 3, records Yang Nandang capturing Hanzhong and sending seven thousand Yong Province refugees to Chang'an—the same households; "Wei" is a corruption of "Yong" and is corrected.

sentences.zh: 文德後自漢中入統汧隴 按宋書卷九八作「率軍自漢中西入，搖動汧隴」。

translations.literal: After Wende, from Hanzhong entered and unified Qian and Long. Note: Song shu juan 98 reads "led the army from Hanzhong westward, shook Qian and Long."
translations.idiomatic: After Wende, from Hanzhong he entered and unified Qian and Long. Song shu juan 98 reads, "led his army west from Hanzhong and stirred Qian and Long."

sentences.zh: 據宋書卷九五索虜傳，乃元嘉二十七年伐魏詔書中語詔作

translations.literal: According to Song shu juan 95, Suolu biography, it is language from the Yuanjia year 27 campaign-against-Wei edict; the edict reads
translations.idiomatic: Song shu juan 95, Suolu biography, shows this comes from the Yuanjia year 27 edict for war against Wei, which reads

sentences.zh: 〈「震盪汧隴」〉，

translations.literal: 〈"shake Qian and Long"〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈"to shake Qian and Long"〉

sentences.zh: 本非實事，下文說文德「有陰平、武興之地」，距汧隴尚遠，談不上「入統」。

translations.literal: originally not a real event; the text below says Wende "held Yinping and Wuxing lands," distant from Qian and Long—cannot speak of "entering and unifying."
translations.idiomatic: —rhetoric, not fact. Below, Wende is said to hold Yinping and Wuxing, far from Qian and Long; "entering and unifying" them is impossible.

sentences.zh: 北史殿本「統」作「絕」，當是以意改，然「統」字必誤。

translations.literal: Bei shi Palace Edition reads "unify" as "cut off"; it must have been changed by conjecture, yet the character "unify" is certainly wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Bei shi Palace Edition reads "unify" as "cut off"—a conjectural emendation—but "unify" is certainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 集始遂入蕭賾 張森楷云：「楊靈珍襲武興，據齊書氐傳

translations.literal: Jishi then entered Xiao Ze. Zhang Senkai says: "Yang Lingzhen attacked Wuxing; according to Qi shu Di biography
translations.idiomatic: Jishi then entered Xiao Ze. Zhang Senkai notes: "Yang Lingzhen attacked Wuxing; according to Qi shu, Di biography

sentences.zh: 〈卷五九〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 59〉

sentences.zh: 在建武世，則是蕭鸞，非蕭賾也。」

translations.literal: in the Jianwu era, then it is Xiao Luan, not Xiao Ze."
translations.idiomatic: this occurred in the Jianwu era—it was Xiao Luan, not Xiao Ze."

sentences.zh: 按張說是。

translations.literal: Note: Zhang's statement is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang is correct.

sentences.zh: 北史卷九六作「入齊」。

translations.literal: Bei shi juan 96 reads "entered Qi."
translations.idiomatic: The Bei shi juan 96 version reads "entered Qi."

sentences.zh: 魏書照例不稱南朝國號，直稱帝名，補此傳者也改從此例，却未考年月，以致誤「鸞」為「賾」。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei by rule does not name the Southern Dynasty state title, directly naming emperors; those who supplemented this biography also changed to follow this rule, yet did not examine year and month, thereby erring "Luan" as "Ze."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei normally names Southern emperors rather than their dynasties; the supplementer followed that convention but failed to check dates, mistaking "Luan" for "Ze."

sentences.zh: 遣舊老及長史七那樓追謝留之 晉書卷九七吐谷渾傳「七那樓」作「史那樓馮」，宋書卷九六吐谷渾傳作「乙那樓」。

translations.literal: Dispatched old elders and Chief Clerk Qinalou to pursue, apologize, and detain him. Jin shu juan 97 Tuyuhun biography reads "Qinalou" as "Shinalou Feng"; Song shu juan 96 Tuyuhun biography reads "Yinalou."
translations.idiomatic: He sent elders and chief clerk Qinalou to pursue, apologize, and detain him. Jin shu juan 97 reads "Shinalou Feng"; Song shu juan 96 reads "Yinalou."

sentences.zh: 疑「七」字訛，晉書「史」字亦涉上「長史」而訛，作「乙」是。

translations.literal: Suspect the character "qi" is in error; Jin shu's "shi" character also was corrupted by the above "Chief Clerk"; reading "yi" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Qi" is likely corrupt; Jin shu's "shi" was probably distorted by the preceding "chief clerk"; "Yi" is correct.

sentences.zh: 一回一迷 按宋書卷九六作「一向一遠」。

translations.literal: One turn, one lost. Note: Song shu juan 96 reads "one direction, one distant."
translations.idiomatic: One turn, one lost. Song shu juan 96 reads "one direction, one distant."

sentences.zh: 上云「擁馬令回」，作「回」是，「迷」字疑當作「遠」。

translations.literal: Above it says "embrace the horse and order it to turn back"; reading "turn back" is correct; the character "lost" is suspected should read "distant."
translations.idiomatic: Above reads "hold the horse and turn it back"—"turn back" is correct; "lost" should probably read "distant."

sentences.zh: 作阿干歌徒河以兄為阿干也 諸本及北史卷九六、宋書卷九六「干」並作「于」。

translations.literal: Composed the Agan song Tuohe, taking "elder brother" as agan. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96, Song shu juan 96 all read "gan" as "yu."
translations.idiomatic: He composed the Agan song Tuohe, using agan for "elder brother." Various editions, Bei shi juan 96, and Song shu juan 96 read "gan" as "yu."

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云「『于』應作『干』，晉書

translations.literal: Palace Edition textual verification says "'yu' should read 'gan'; Jin shu
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition textual verification says "'yu' should read 'gan'; Jin shu

sentences.zh: 〈卷九七〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 97〉

sentences.zh: 鮮卑謂兄曰『阿干』是也」。

translations.literal: Xianbei call elder brother 'agan'—that is it."
translations.idiomatic: the Xianbei word for elder brother is 'agan.'"

sentences.zh: 按通志卷一九五吐谷渾傳也作「干」。

translations.literal: Note: Tongzhi juan 195 Tuyuhun biography also reads "gan."
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi juan 195, Tuyuhun biography, also reads "gan."

sentences.zh: 我國東北諸族及蒙古語稱兄音近「阿干」，知「于」字訛，今據晉書、通志改。

translations.literal: Our country's northeastern peoples and Mongolian language call elder brother with sound near "agan"; know the character "yu" is in error; now changed according to Jin shu, Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Northeastern peoples and Mongolian use a word near "agan" for elder brother; "yu" is corrupt and is emended per Jin shu and Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 弟視羆立 按晉書卷九七、宋書卷九六並云視連二子，長曰視羆，少曰烏紇提。

translations.literal: Younger brother Shirpi succeeded. Note: Jin shu juan 97, Song shu juan 96 both say Shirilian had two sons: elder named Shirpi, younger named Wugeti.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Shirpi succeeded. Jin shu juan 97 and Song shu juan 96 both say Shirilian had two sons: the elder Shirpi and the younger Wugeti.

sentences.zh: 這裏「弟」當作「子」。

translations.literal: Here "younger brother" should read "son."
translations.idiomatic: "Younger brother" here should be emended to "son."

sentences.zh: 生二子慕璝利延 按下文「利延」都作「慕利延」，宋書卷九六作「慕延」，省「利」字。

translations.literal: Bore two sons, Mugui and Liyan. Note: below "Liyan" is always written "Muliyan"; Song shu juan 96 reads "Muyan," omitting the character "li."
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Mugui and Liyan. Below, "Liyan" always appears as "Muliyan"; Song shu juan 96 reads "Muyan," omitting "li."

sentences.zh: 這裏「慕」字不宜省，當是脫文。

translations.literal: Here the character "Mu" should not be omitted; it must be missing text.
translations.idiomatic: The "Mu" here should not be dropped; text is missing.

sentences.zh: 汝等各奉吾一隻箭折之地下 北史卷九六、冊府卷九六七

translations.literal: You each take one of my arrows and break it on the ground. Bei shi juan 96, Cefu juan 967
translations.idiomatic: Each of you take one of my arrows and break it on the ground. Bei shi juan 96, Cefu juan 967

sentences.zh: 〈一一三六七頁〉
「折」作「將玩」二字。

translations.literal: "Break" reads as the two characters "jiang wan."
translations.idiomatic: "Break" appears as "take and play with."

sentences.zh: 按下文稱「命母弟慕利延曰：『汝取一隻箭折之』。」

translations.literal: Examining below it says "ordered younger brother by the same mother Muliyan: 'You take one arrow and break it.'"
translations.idiomatic: Below it reads, "He told his younger brother Muliyan, 'Take one arrow and break it.'"

sentences.zh: 若諸子先已各折一箭，何須慕利延更試？

translations.literal: If the various sons had already each broken one arrow, why need Muliyan test again?
translations.idiomatic: If each son had already broken an arrow, why would Muliyan need to test again?

sentences.zh: 這裏「折」字本當作「將玩」，因下「折之」字適在次行相並處而訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "break" originally should read "take and play with"; because below "break it" happened to be adjacent on the next line, it was corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Here "break" originally read "take and play with"; it was corrupted because "break it" appeared on the next line.

sentences.zh: 乞佛日連 諸本「佛」作「拂」，北史卷九六作「佛」。

translations.literal: Qifo Rilian. Various editions read "fo" as "fu"; Bei shi juan 96 reads "fo."
translations.idiomatic: Qifo Rilian. Various editions write "fu" for "fo"; Bei shi juan 96 preserves "fo."

sentences.zh: 按「拂」「佛」譯音無定字，但此傳下文載羣臣議也作「佛」，一篇之中，不應歧異，今據北史改。

translations.literal: Note: "fu" and "fo" in transliteration have no fixed characters; but this biography below, recording the ministers' deliberation, also reads "fo"—within one piece there should not be divergence; now changed according to Bei shi.
translations.idiomatic: Transliteration of "fu" and "fo" varies, but the ministers' deliberation below also reads "fo"; the text should not differ within one biography and is emended per Bei shi.

sentences.zh: 始至萬匹 諸本「萬匹」作「方伯」，北史卷九六作「万匹」。

translations.literal: At first reaching ten thousand bolts. Various editions read "ten thousand bolts" as "regional lord"; Bei shi juan 96 reads "ten thousand bolts."
translations.idiomatic: The first gifts totaled ten thousand bolts. Various editions corrupt this to "regional lord"; Bei shi juan 96 correctly reads "ten thousand bolts."

sentences.zh: 按上文是說漢遺匈奴繒絮事，呼韓邪入朝，初次賜錦繡綺縠雜物八千匹，絮六千斤；

translations.literal: Note: above speaks of Han bestowing on the Xiongnu silk floss matters; Huhanye entered court; first time gifted brocade, embroidery, fine silk, mixed goods of eight thousand bolts, floss six thousand jin;
translations.idiomatic: Above describes Han gifts of silk and floss to the Xiongnu: when Huhanye first came to court he received eight thousand bolts of brocade, embroidery, and fine silk plus six thousand jin of floss;

sentences.zh: 弟二次是錦帛九千匹，絮八千斤

translations.literal: the second time was brocade and silk nine thousand bolts, floss eight thousand jin
translations.idiomatic: the second time, nine thousand bolts of silk and eight thousand jin of floss

sentences.zh: 〈見漢書卷九四下匈奴傳下〉，

translations.literal: 〈see Han shu juan 94, Part 2, Xiongnu biography, Part 2〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈see Han shu juan 94B, Xiongnu biography〉

sentences.zh: 約計為萬匹。

translations.literal: roughly calculated as ten thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: —roughly ten thousand bolts in all.

sentences.zh: 作「方伯」與上文不相連，且漢也未命呼韓邪為方伯。

translations.literal: Reading "regional lord" does not connect with the above text; moreover Han also did not appoint Huhanye as regional lord.
translations.idiomatic: "Regional lord" does not fit the context, and Han never made Huhanye a regional lord.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now changed according to [the above].
translations.idiomatic: Emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 通使于劉彧獻善馬四角羊彧加之官號 百衲、南、北、汲四本兩「彧」字都作「或」，殿、局二本作「彧」。

translations.literal: Sent envoys to Liu Yu, presented fine horses and four-horned sheep; Yu added official titles. In the Bai Na, Nan, Bei, Ji four editions both characters "Yu" all read "huo"; the Dian and Ju editions read "Yu."
translations.idiomatic: "They sent envoys to Liu Yu, presented fine horses and four-horned sheep, and Yu conferred official titles." In the Bai Na, Nan, Bei, and Ji editions both instances of "Yu" are wrongly written "huo"; the Dian and Ju editions read "Yu."

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「兩『彧』字監本俱誤作『或』，北史

translations.literal: The Dian edition Textual Verification says: "Both characters 'Yu' in the Jian edition are all wrongly written as 'huo,' Bei shi
translations.idiomatic: The Dian edition's Textual Verification notes: "Both instances of 'Yu' are incorrectly written 'huo' in the Jian edition. Bei shi

sentences.zh: 〈卷九六〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 96〉

sentences.zh: 云：『通使於宋，獻善馬四角羊，宋文

translations.literal: says: 'Sent envoys to Song, presented fine horses and four-horned sheep; Song Wen
translations.idiomatic: reads: 'They sent envoys to Song, presented fine horses and four-horned sheep; Emperor Wen of Song

sentences.zh: 〈按本作「明」〉

translations.literal: 〈note: this edition reads "Ming"〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈this edition reads "Ming"〉

sentences.zh: 帝加之官號』。

translations.literal: Emperor added official titles to them.'
translations.idiomatic: conferred official titles on them.'

sentences.zh: 『彧』，文

translations.literal: 'Yu,' Wen
translations.idiomatic: 'Yu' refers to Wen

translations.literal: 〈Ming〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor Ming〉

sentences.zh: 帝諱也，今改正。」

translations.literal: Emperor's taboo name; now corrected."
translations.idiomatic: the taboo name of Emperor Ming, and has been emended."

sentences.zh: 按考證說是，今從作「彧」。

translations.literal: Note: the Textual Verification is correct; now following it to write "Yu."
translations.idiomatic: The verification is sound; the text now follows it with "Yu."

sentences.zh: 然檢宋書，獻馬羊在世祖劉駿大明五年，加官在太宗劉彧

translations.literal: Yet examining Song shu, presenting horses and sheep was in the fifth year of Daming of Shizu Liu Jun; adding titles was under Taizong Liu Yu
translations.idiomatic: Yet Song shu shows the horse and sheep tribute in the fifth year of Daming under Shizu Liu Jun, while titles were granted under Taizong Liu Yu

sentences.zh: 〈即明帝〉

translations.literal: 〈that is, Emperor Ming〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor Ming〉

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，本非同時事。

translations.literal: third year of Taishi—originally not the same-time affair.
translations.idiomatic: in the third year of Taishi—these were not the same events.

sentences.zh: 北史刪簡宋書，前稱「宋」，後稱「明帝」本不誤，補此傳者依魏書例改稱宋帝名，則「通使於宋」，當作「通使於劉駿」，却因後有「明帝」字，也一概改作「彧」，殊謬。

translations.literal: Bei shi abbreviated Song shu; front calling "Song," later calling "Emperor Ming" originally was not wrong; the person who supplemented this biography, following Wei shu precedent, changed to call Song emperors by personal names—then "sent envoys to Song" should read "sent envoys to Liu Jun," yet because later there is the character "Emperor Ming," also uniformly changed to "Yu"—utterly mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Bei shi condenses Song shu and is not wrong to say "Song" first and "Emperor Ming" later. Whoever supplemented this biography followed Wei shu practice and substituted the Song emperors' personal names—so "sent envoys to Song" should become "sent envoys to Liu Jun"—yet because "Emperor Ming" appears later, both were changed to "Yu," which is absurd.

sentences.zh: 又宋書作「獻善舞馬」，又稱「皇太子、王公以下上舞馬歌二十七首」，這裏「馬」上當脫「舞」字。

translations.literal: Moreover Song shu reads "presented fine dancing horses," also says "Crown Prince, kings and dukes down submitted twenty-seven dancing-horse songs"; here above "horse" must be missing the character "dance."
translations.idiomatic: Song shu reads "presented fine dancing horses" and mentions "twenty-seven dancing-horse songs submitted by the Crown Prince, kings, and dukes." The character "dance" has dropped out before "horse" here.

sentences.zh: 遣其侍郎時真貢方物提上表稱嗣事 按「提」字不可解，通志卷一九五吐谷渾傳作「併」，恐也是以意改。

translations.literal: Sent his Attendant-in-Ordinary Shi Zhen to present local products, submit memorials claiming succession affairs. Note: the character "ti" is inexplicable; Tong zhi juan 195 Tuyuhun biography reads "bing"; fear also is emendation by guess.
translations.idiomatic: "They sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Shi Zhen to bring tribute and submit a memorial claiming succession." The character "ti" makes no sense; Tong zhi juan 195, Tuyuhun biography, has "bing" instead—likely another arbitrary emendation.

sentences.zh: 乃可加以告責 北史卷九六「告」作「詰」，是。

translations.literal: Then one may add rebuke and censure. Bei shi juan 96 reads "gao" as "jie"—correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Then one may rebuke and censure them." Bei shi juan 96 reads "jie" for "gao," which is correct.

sentences.zh: 但作「告」亦可通，今不改。

translations.literal: But writing "gao" can also pass; now not changed.
translations.idiomatic: "Gao" is still intelligible; left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 涼州城人萬于菩提等東應念生 卷九肅宗紀正光五年七月記此事作「于菩提」。

translations.literal: Liangzhou city men Wan Yu Puti and others eastward joined Niansheng. Juan 9 Suzong annals, seventh month fifth year of Zhengguang records this matter as "Yu Puti."
translations.idiomatic: "The Liangzhou townsman Wan Yu Puti and others joined Niansheng in the east." Juan 9 of the Suzong annals, seventh month of the fifth year of Zhengguang, records this as "Yu Puti."

sentences.zh: 按卷一一三官氏志「勿忸于氏後改為于氏」，廣韵十虞引作「万忸于」。

translations.literal: Note: juan 113 Clans-surnames chronicle "Wuniu-yu clan later changed to Yu clan"; Guang yun, Rhyme-group 10 Yu, cites as "Wanniu-yu."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 113, Clans and Surnames, says the Wuniu-yu clan later became the Yu clan; the Guang yun, Rhyme Yu, cites "Wanniu-yu."

sentences.zh: 這裏「萬」當作「万」，「万于」即「万忸于」之省。

translations.literal: Here "Wan" (ten thousand) should read "Wan" (the clan name); "Wan Yu" is an abbreviation of "Wanniu-yu."
translations.idiomatic: Here the character written as "ten thousand" should be read as the clan name Wan, not as the numeral; "Wan Yu" abbreviates "Wanniu-yu."

sentences.zh: 牧養犛牛羊豕以供其食 諸本及北史卷九六「牧」訛「收」，今據冊府卷九六一

translations.literal: Herded and raised yak, cattle, sheep, and pigs to supply their food. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 corrupt "mu" (herd) as "shou" (collect); now according to Cefu juan 961
translations.idiomatic: "They herd yaks, cattle, sheep, and pigs for food." Various editions and Bei shi juan 96 wrongly read "shou" for "mu"; emended per Cefu juan 961

sentences.zh: 〈一一三０五頁〉、
周書卷四九宕昌傳、通典卷一九０宕昌條改。

translations.literal: Zhou shu juan 49 Dangchang biography, Tong dian juan 190 Dangchang entry changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou shu juan 49 (Dangchang), and Tong dian juan 190 (Dangchang section).

sentences.zh: 父子伯叔兄弟死者即以繼母世叔母及嫂弟婦等為妻 諸本「叔母」上脫「世」字，今據北史卷九六、冊府卷九六一

translations.literal: When father, son, elder and younger uncle, elder and younger brother die, then take stepmother, father's younger brother's wife, elder brother's wife, younger brother's wife, and so on as wives. Various editions above "younger uncle's wife" omit character "shi"; now according to Bei shi juan 96, Cefu juan 961
translations.idiomatic: "When a father, son, uncle, or brother dies, they marry the stepmother, father's younger brother's wife, sister-in-law, and so on." Various editions drop "shi" before "younger uncle's wife"; supplied per Bei shi juan 96 and Cefu juan 961

sentences.zh: 〈一一三０五頁〉、
周書卷四九補。

translations.literal: Zhou shu juan 49 supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhou shu juan 49.

sentences.zh: 席水以南 諸本及北史卷九六、周書卷四九「席」都作「廗」，通典卷一九０作「席」，注云：「席水在今天水上邽縣。」

translations.literal: South of Xi River. Various editions and Bei shi juan 96, Zhou shu juan 49 all read "Xi" as "dai"; Tong dian juan 190 reads "Xi," annotation says: "Xi River is in Tianshui Shanggui county today."
translations.idiomatic: "South of the Xi River." Various editions, Bei shi juan 96, and Zhou shu juan 49 all write "dai" for "Xi"; Tong dian juan 190 has "Xi" and notes: "The Xi River is in Shanggui county, Tianshui, today."

sentences.zh: 按本書卷一０六下地形志下天水上封

translations.literal: Note: this book juan 106 Part 2 Geography Part 2 Tianshui Shang
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 106B of this work, Geography, Tianshui commandery, Shang

sentences.zh: 〈即上邽〉

translations.literal: 〈that is, Shanggui〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shanggui〉

sentences.zh: 縣下云「有席水」。

translations.literal: county below says "has Xi River."
translations.idiomatic: gui county notes "there is a Xi River."

sentences.zh: 「廗」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Character "dai" is corrupt; now changed according to [evidence].
translations.idiomatic: "Dai" is a scribal error; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 七十里有貪汗山 諸本「汗」訛「汙」，今據北史卷九七高昌傳、通典卷一九一高昌條改。

translations.literal: Seventy li away is Tanhan Mountain. Various editions corrupt "han" (sweat) as "wu" (filth); now according to Bei shi juan 97 Gaochang biography, Tong dian juan 191 Gaochang entry changed.
translations.idiomatic: "Seventy li away is Tanhan Mountain." Various editions wrongly read "wu" for "han"; emended per Bei shi juan 97 (Gaochang) and Tong dian juan 191 (Gaochang).

sentences.zh: 高車王可至羅殺首歸兄弟 冊府卷九六六

translations.literal: Gaoche King Kezhiluo killed Shougui brothers. Cefu juan 966
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche King Kezhiluo killed Shougui and his brothers. Cefu juan 966

sentences.zh: 〈一一三六四頁〉、
隋書卷八三高昌傳、通典卷一九一車師條「可至羅」作「阿伏至羅」。

translations.literal: Sui shu juan 83 Gaochang biography, Tong dian juan 191 Cheshi entry read "Kezhiluo" as "Afuzhiluo."
translations.idiomatic: Sui shu juan 83 (Gaochang), and Tong dian juan 191 (Cheshi section) read "Afuzhiluo" for "Kezhiluo."

sentences.zh: 按「阿伏至羅」見卷一０三高車傳，這裏「可」當是「阿」之訛，省「伏」字。

translations.literal: Note: "Afuzhiluo" appears in juan 103 Gaoche biography; here "Ke" must be corruption of "A," omitting character "fu."
translations.idiomatic: "Afuzhiluo" appears in juan 103, Gaoche biography; "Ke" here is a corruption of "A," with "fu" dropped.

sentences.zh: 永平元年 諸本及北史卷九七「永」作「熙」。

translations.literal: First year of Yongping. Various editions and Bei shi juan 97 read "Yong" as "Xi."
translations.idiomatic: "First year of Yongping." Various editions and Bei shi juan 97 read "Xi" for "Yong."

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「通鑑

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai said: "Tong jian
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai writes: "Tong jian

sentences.zh: 〈卷一四七、四五八九頁〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 147, page 4589〉

sentences.zh: 置此於永平元年

translations.literal: places this in first year of Yongping
translations.idiomatic: dates this to the first year of Yongping

sentences.zh: 〈梁天監七年〉，

translations.literal: 〈Liang Tianjian seventh year〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈Liang Tianjian 7〉;

sentences.zh: 據下文有『延昌』，又有『熙平』，則此『熙』字誤也。」

translations.literal: according to below having 'Yanchang,' also having 'Xiping'—then this 'Xi' character is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: given 'Yanchang' below and also 'Xiping,' the 'Xi' here is wrong."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷八世宗紀永平元年歲末，張說是，今據紀改。

translations.literal: Note: the affair appears in juan 8 Shizong annals end of first year of Yongping; Zhang's statement is correct; now changed according to the annals.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears at year-end, first year of Yongping, juan 8, Shizong annals. Zhang is right; emended per the annals.

sentences.zh: 并請國子助教劉變以為博士 北史卷九七「變」作「爕」，疑「變」字訛。

translations.literal: Also requested National University Assistant Instructor Liu Bian to serve as Erudite. Bei shi juan 97 reads "Bian" as "Xie"; suspect character "Bian" is corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: "They also asked that National University Assistant Instructor Liu Bian be made an Erudite." Bei shi juan 97 reads "Xie" for "Bian"; "Bian" may be corrupt.

sentences.zh: 其王像舒治遣使內附高祖拜龍驤將軍鄧至王 按通典卷一九０鄧至條云：「自舒理

translations.literal: Its king Xiang Shu-zhi sent envoys to submit inward; Gaozu appointed Dragon-soaring General, King of Dengzhi. Note: Tong dian juan 190 Dengzhi entry says: "From Shu-li
translations.idiomatic: "King Xiang Shu-zhi sent envoys to submit; Emperor Gaozu made him Dragon-Soaring General and King of Dengzhi." Tong dian juan 190, Dengzhi section, says: "From Shu-li

sentences.zh: 〈即舒治，避唐諱改〉

translations.literal: 〈that is, Shu-zhi, changed to avoid Tang taboo〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shu-zhi, altered to avoid Tang taboo〉

sentences.zh: 至十代孫舒彭附於後魏。」

translations.literal: to tenth-generation descendant Shu Peng submitted to Later Wei."
translations.idiomatic: down to the tenth-generation descendant Shu Peng, who submitted to Later Wei."

sentences.zh: 本書卷七下高祖紀下太和十七年九月乙亥記鄧至王像舒彭遣子舊詣闕朝貢，并奉表求以位授舊。

translations.literal: This book juan 7 Part 2 Gaozu annals Part 2, seventeenth year of Taihe, ninth month yihai, records King of Dengzhi Xiang Shu Peng sent son Jiu to court to pay tribute, also submitted memorial requesting to confer position on Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 7B, Gaozu annals, records that on yihai day, ninth month, seventeenth year of Taihe, King of Dengzhi Xiang Shu Peng sent his son Jiu to court with tribute and asked to transfer the throne to him.

sentences.zh: 舒彭受封當更在前，據紀十五年已記鄧至國「朝貢」。

translations.literal: Shu Peng receiving investiture must have been earlier still; according to annals, fifteenth year already records Dengzhi state "paying tribute."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Peng's enfeoffment must be earlier; the annals already record Dengzhi "paying tribute" in the fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 據此，元宏時遣使並受封者乃像舒彭，通典當本魏書原文，這裏「像舒治」下有脫文。

translations.literal: According to this, in Yuan Hong's time the one who sent envoys and received enfeoffment was Xiang Shu Peng; Tong dian should follow Wei shu original text; here below "Xiang Shu-zhi" there is missing text.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys and enfeoffment under Yuan Hong belong to Xiang Shu Peng, which matches Tong dian's Wei shu source. Text is missing after "Xiang Shu-zhi" here.

sentences.zh: 戶萬九千遣使內附 卷八世宗紀正始二年八月記此事「萬九千」作「萬九十」。

translations.literal: Households ten thousand nine hundred sent envoys inward to submit. Juan 8 Shizong annals, second year of Zhengshi, eighth month records this matter as "ten thousand ninety."
translations.idiomatic: "Nineteen thousand households sent envoys to submit." Juan 8, Shizong annals, eighth month, second year of Zhengshi, reads "ten thousand ninety."

sentences.zh: 叔興給一統并威儀 按語晦澀費解，其意當是給叔興一統帥名義并威儀，疑有訛脫。

translations.literal: Shuxing given one command also regalia. Note: language obscure and hard to parse; the meaning should be giving Shuxing one commander-in-chief title and regalia; suspect there is corruption and omission.
translations.idiomatic: "Shuxing was given one command and regalia." The phrasing is obscure; it likely means Shuxing was granted a commander's title and ceremonial regalia—probably corrupt or incomplete.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋衍龍驤將軍楚石廉叛衍來請援 北史卷九五蠻傳「楚」作「樊」。

translations.literal: Man chieftain Yan, Dragon-soaring General Chu Shilian rebelled against Yan and came to request aid. Bei shi juan 95 Man biography reads "Chu" as "Fan."
translations.idiomatic: "Man chieftain Yan's Dragon-Soaring General Chu Shilian rebelled against Yan and asked for aid." Bei shi juan 95, Man biography, reads "Fan" for "Chu."

sentences.zh: 按樊是蠻族大姓，「楚」當是「樊」之訛。

translations.literal: Note: Fan is a great Man clan surname; "Chu" must be corruption of "Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Fan is a major Man surname; "Chu" is likely a mistake for "Fan."

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將圍廣陵樊城諸蠻並為前驅 北史卷九五「樊」作「楚」。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent generals to besiege Guangling, Fancheng; various Man all served as vanguard. Bei shi juan 95 reads "Fan" as "Chu."
translations.idiomatic: "Xiao Yan sent generals to besiege Guangling and Fancheng; the Man tribes served as vanguard." Bei shi juan 95 reads "Chu" for "Fan."

sentences.zh: 按楚城是西楚州治所

translations.literal: Note: Chucheng is seat of West Chu Province
translations.idiomatic: Chucheng was the seat of West Chu province

sentences.zh: 〈今河南信陽附近〉，

translations.literal: 〈today near Xinyang, Henan〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈near present-day Xinyang, Henan〉,

sentences.zh: 與廣陵

translations.literal: with Guangling
translations.idiomatic: adjacent to Guangling

sentences.zh: 〈西豫州治所今河南息縣〉

translations.literal: 〈West Yu Province seat, today Xixian, Henan〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈seat of West Yu province, present Xixian, Henan〉

sentences.zh: 鄰接，樊城相距尚遠，疑「樊」是「楚」之訛。

translations.literal: neighboring; Fancheng distance still far—suspect "Fan" is corruption of "Chu."
translations.idiomatic: but Fancheng lies much farther away; "Fan" is probably a mistake for "Chu."

sentences.zh: 若中國之貴族也 御覽卷七九六

translations.literal: Like the nobility of the Middle Kingdom. Yulan juan 796
translations.idiomatic: "Like the nobility of the Middle Kingdom." Taiping yulan juan 796

sentences.zh: 〈三五三四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3534〉

sentences.zh: 「貴」作「黨」，疑「貴」字訛。

translations.literal: "Noble" read as "faction"; suspect character "noble" is corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: reads "faction" for "noble"; "noble" may be corrupt.

sentences.zh: 好相殺害多不敢遠行 北史卷九五僚傳「多」下有「死」字。

translations.literal: Fond of mutual killing; many dare not travel far. Bei shi juan 95 Liao biography below "many" has character "die."
translations.idiomatic: "They often kill one another and many dare not travel far." Bei shi juan 95, Liao biography, has "die" after "many."

sentences.zh: 按御覽卷七六三

translations.literal: Note: Yulan juan 763
translations.idiomatic: Taiping yulan juan 763

sentences.zh: 〈三五三四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3534〉

sentences.zh: 「多」下有「仇怨」二字，北史「怨」字訛「死」，又脫「仇」字，補此傳者遂併刪「死」字。

translations.literal: Below "many" are the two characters "enemy hatred"; Bei shi character "yuan" corrupt as "si," also omits "chou"; person who supplemented this biography then together deleted "si" character.
translations.idiomatic: adds "chou yuan" (feud) after "many"; Bei shi corrupts "yuan" to "si" and drops "chou"; whoever patched this biography deleted "si" entirely.

sentences.zh: 走避 北史卷九五「走避」下有「外」字。

translations.literal: Flee and avoid. Bei shi juan 95 below "flee avoid" has character "outside."
translations.idiomatic: "They flee and hide." Bei shi juan 95 adds "wai" (outside) after "zou bi."

sentences.zh: 按御覽卷七九六

translations.literal: Note: Yulan juan 796
translations.idiomatic: Taiping yulan juan 796

sentences.zh: 〈三五三四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3534〉

sentences.zh: 有「於外」二字，當是魏書原文，此傳以北史補，當脫「外」字。

translations.literal: has the two characters "at outside"; should be Wei shu original text; this biography supplemented from Bei shi, should have omitted "outside" character.
translations.idiomatic: has "yu wai" (outside); likely the Wei shu original. This passage was patched from Bei shi and has dropped "wai."

sentences.zh: 御覽先引後魏書，後引北史，似據魏書原文，但更簡略，必經刪節，亦無多異文。

translations.literal: Yulan first cites Later Wei shu, later cites Bei shi; seems to follow Wei shu original text, but more abbreviated, must have undergone abridgment, also not many variant readings.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping yulan cites Later Wei shu first and Bei shi later—closer to Wei shu but briefer and clearly abridged, with few variant readings.

sentences.zh: 山南行臺勉諭 通志卷一九七「行臺」下有「魏子建」三字。

translations.literal: South-of-Mountains Branch Secretariat admonished and instructed. Tong zhi juan 197 below "Branch Secretariat" has the three characters "Wei Zijian."
translations.idiomatic: "The South-of-Mountains Branch Secretariat admonished them." Tong zhi juan 197 adds "Wei Zijian" after "Branch Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 按魏子建為「山南行臺」，見卷九肅宗紀正光五年十二月，卷一０四自序也說「詔子建兼尚書，為行臺。」

translations.literal: Note: Wei Zijian was "South-of-Mountains Branch Secretariat"; see juan 9 Suzong annals twelfth month fifth year of Zhengguang; juan 104 Author's Preface also says "ordered Zijian concurrently Censor-in-Chief, as Branch Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zijian held the South-of-Mountains post (juan 9, Suzong annals, twelfth month, fifth year of Zhengguang); juan 104, Author's Preface, records: "Zijian was ordered to serve concurrently as Minister of the Secretariat and head the Branch Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 這裏當脫「魏子建」三字，致下文忽稱「子建厚勞賚之」，不知「子建」為何人。

translations.literal: Here should be missing the three characters "Wei Zijian," causing below suddenly to call "Zijian generously rewarded them with gifts," not knowing who "Zijian" is.
translations.idiomatic: The name "Wei Zijian" is missing here, so when the text later says "Zijian generously rewarded them," readers cannot tell who Zijian is.

sentences.zh: 後元羅在梁州為所陷 諸本「所」訛「使」，不可通，今據北史卷九五改。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Luo at Liang Province was by [someone] trapped. Various editions corrupt "suo" (by) as "shi" (envoy)—unintelligible; now changed according to Bei shi juan 95.
translations.idiomatic: "Later Yuan Luo in Liang province fell into an ambush." Various editions corrupt "suo" to "shi," which makes no sense; emended per Bei shi juan 95.
